**In a desert.** As if Israel had been an unwanted infant cast out to die, and Jehovah had so found him (see Jer. 2:2; Eze. 16:5, 6; Hosea 9:11).
**Led him about.** Literally, “surrounded him about.” That is, God encircled Israel with protection and infinite mercies (see Ps. 32:10). Thus He always protects His people (see Ps. 34:7).
**Instructed him.** Taught him, as a father would his child (see Ex. 20:1, 2; 34:1, 10).
**The apple of his eye.** Literally, “the pupil of his eye.” The expression thus translated is from the same root as the word for “man,” and may refer, as some think, to the image reflected in the eye. The eye is perhaps the most sensitive organ of the body, and one that a man unconsciously protects more carefully than any other. God regards His people with equal care (see Isa. 49:15).

11.zh:
又如鷹攪動巢窩，在雛鷹以上兩翅搧展，接取雛鷹，背在兩翼之上。

**如鷹。**這裡進一步的引伸出19:4中的比喻，表現上帝溫柔的引導和保護（見申1:31；何11:3）。
**背。**這裡描繪耶和華對其子民的關愛，特別是當他們流浪在曠野的時候（見徒13:18）。上帝的眷顧和管教總是以造就品格為目的的（見來12:11；啟3:19）。祂定意要使人明白在上帝兒子名分的含義。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《給傳道人的證言》255。
**懷愛倫註釋（11–12節）**。《先祖與先知》469；《證言》卷八 150。
11.en:
**As an eagle.** This is a further development of the simile given in Ex. 19:4. It suggests God’s gentle leading and protection (see Deut. 1:31; Hosea 11:3).
**Beareth them.** This word picture suggests the loving care of Jehovah for His people, particularly during their wayward conduct in the wilderness (see Acts 13:18). God’s care and His acts of discipline are always for the purpose of developing character (see Heb. 12:11; Rev. 3:19). He designs that men should become aware of the possibilities inherent in sonship with God.

12.zh:
這樣，耶和華獨自引導他，並無外邦神與他同在。

**耶和華獨自。**從別神那裡得到幫助純屬幻想。而耶和華的大能卻是完全充足的（見詩81:10；何13:4）。
12.en: **The Lord alone.** The help of other gods was pure imagination. In contrast, the power of Jehovah was all-sufficient (see Ps. 81:10; Hosea 13:4).

13.zh:
耶和華使他乘駕地的高處，得吃田間的土產；又使他從磐石中咂蜜，從堅石中吸油；

**高處。**比喻上帝勝利的引導（見摩4:13）。參如今用於餘民教會的應許（見賽58:13,14）。
**土產。**這是由於上帝仁慈眷顧，和祂對他們的勞動和順從生活的祝福（見太6:33）。
**從磐石中咂蜜。**指巴勒斯坦的石縫中會找到許多野蜂。蜂蜜喻指上帝的教訓（見箴24:13,14），上帝公義的審判（見詩19:9-11）和祂的聖言（見詩119:103）。這裡主要是指迦南豐富的自然資源。
**從堅石中吸油。**任何好東西都不會缺乏。油或“脂油”是繁榮和奢華的象徵（見結16:13,19）。
13.en:
**On the high places.** A figure of speech suggestive of the triumphant leading of God (see Amos 4:13). Compare the promise applicable today to the remnant church (see Isa. 58:13, 14).
**The increase.** Due to the beneficent care of God and the blessing He would add to their labors, and lives of obedience (see Matt. 6:33).
**Honey out of the rock.** An allusion to the many wild bees to be found in the rocky crevices of Palestine. Honey is used to illustrate divine teachings (see Prov. 24:13, 14), also as a figure of the righteous judgments of God (see Ps. 19:9–11), and His Word (see Ps. 119:103). Here, its primary reference is to the natural bounties of Canaan.
**Oil out of the flinty rock.** Nothing good would be lacking. Oil, or “fatness,” is a symbol of prosperity and luxury (see Eze. 16:13, 19).

15.zh:
但耶書崙漸漸肥胖，粗壯，光潤，踢跳，奔跑，便離棄造他的神，輕看救他的磐石；

**耶書侖。**在詩歌中表示以色列人（見申33:5,26；賽44:2）。該詞源於動詞“使筆直”、“使正直”，指以色列人是“正直人”。在這裡用來責備與上帝對其子民的理想相去甚遠的背道的以色列人。
**漸漸肥胖。**當以色列人富有起來的時候，就開始背叛使他們富有的主（見耶5:28；何2:8；4:16）。
**輕看。**或“嘲笑”。直譯為“當作愚人對待”。關於這個動詞，見“行事愚頑”（箴30:32）、“辱沒你”（鴻3:6）、“藐視”（彌7:6）。以及源於相同詞根的形容詞：“愚昧”（申32:6,21）、“愚頑人”（詩14:1；53:1；箴17:7,21；30:22；耶17:11）、“愚頑的先知”（結13:3）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖與先知》413。
**懷愛倫註釋（15–21節）**。《先知與君王》395。
15.en:
**Jeshurun.** A poetical name for Israel (see Deut. 33:5, 26; Isa. 44:2). It is derived from the verb “to be straight,” “to be upright,” and is applied to Israel as “the upright one.” It is probably used here in reproach, of an apostate Israel that would fall far short of God’s ideal for His people.
**Waxed fat.** When Israel became prosperous they rebelled against Him who had given them prosperity (see Jer. 5:28; Hosea 2:8; 4:16).
**Lightly esteemed.** Or, “scoffed at.” Literally, “treated as a fool.” For this same verb, see “hast done foolishly” (Prov. 30:32), “make thee vile” (Nahum 3:6), “dishonoureth” (Micah 7:6). And the adjective of the same root: “foolish” (Deut. 32:6, 21), “fool” (Ps. 14:1; 53:1; Prov. 17:7, 21; 30:22; Jer. 17:11), “foolish prophets” (Eze. 13:3).

16.zh:
敬拜別神，觸動神的憤恨，行可憎惡的事，惹了他的怒氣。

以色列人像一個不誠實的妻子，做了拜偶像的可憎之事，惹起耶和華他們上帝的憤怒（出34:14；賽54:5）。
**懷愛倫註釋（16–22節）**。《證言》卷一280，364。
16.en: **Provoked him.** By idolatrous abominations Israel, like an unfaithful wife, provoked the Lord their God to jealousy (Ex. 34:14; Isa. 54:5).

17.zh:
所祭祀的鬼魔並非真神，乃是素不認識的神，是近來新興的，是你列祖所不畏懼的。

見林前10:19,20。異教崇拜中最可憎的事就是將孩子獻給魔鬼（見詩106:37）。犯罪墮落的過程似乎是由許多幾乎無法察覺的階段組成的。第一步可能不是主動的違法，而是消極的犯罪，就是忽略某些積極的要求。一步接著一步地，最終導致人的行為與以前完全相反。然而令人簡直難以相信的是，上帝的選民竟會崇拜魔鬼，將自己的兒女獻為祭物。偏離上帝的道會導致最可怕的後果，正如以色列人所經歷的那樣。
**是近來新興的。**或“最近來的”，參以賽亞的生動描述（賽44:15；另見士5:8）。
**畏懼。**希伯來語動詞表示驚恐、恐懼，如“極其恐慌”（耶2:12；結32:10）。
17.en:
**Sacrificed unto devils.** Compare 1 Cor. 10:19, 20. The supreme abomination of heathen worship was the sacrifice of children to demons (see Ps. 106:37). A sinful course seems to proceed by almost imperceptible stages. The first step may not be a positive act of lawlessness but rather a negative sin, the omission of some positive requirement. One step leads to another, until there may result a complete reversal of one’s former conduct. Yet it seems almost beyond belief that God’s chosen people could have worshiped devils and offered their own sons and daughters as sacrificial offerings. To stray from God’s path may lead to the most fearful alternatives, as it did for Israel.
**Came newly up.** Or, “lately arrived.” Compare Isaiah’s graphic description (Isa. 44:15; see also Judges 5:8).
**Feared not.** The Hebrew verb expresses dread, horror, as, for example, “be horribly afraid” (Jer. 2:12; Eze. 32:10).

18.zh:
你輕忽生你的磐石，忘記產你的神。

**磐石。**見第4節註釋。
**忘記……上帝。**他們一心一意崇拜偶像。
**產你的。**參出19:5,6；耶2:27；和使徒保羅的教訓（林前4:15；門10；加4:19）。
18.en:
**Rock.** See on v. 4.
**Forgotten God.** They would be completely absorbed in idolatry.
**That formed thee.** See Ex. 19:5, 6; cf. Jer. 2:27; the apostle Paul’s teaching (1 Cor. 4:15; Philemon 10; Gal. 4:19).

19.zh:
耶和華看見他的兒女惹動他，就厭惡他們，說：

**厭惡。**直譯為“踢開”、或“藐視”。關於這個動詞的其他例子，見箴1:30；5:12；15:5；哀2:6。
19.en: **Abhorred.** Literally, “spurned,” or “despised.” For other instances of this verb see Prov. 1:30; 5:12; 15:5; Lam. 2:6.

21.zh:
他們以那不算為神的觸動我的憤恨，以虛無的神惹了我的怒氣。我也要以那不成子民的觸動他們的憤恨，以愚昧的國民惹了他們的怒氣。

**憤恨。**見第16節。
**不算為神的。**或“不是神的”。他們所崇拜的偶像代表並不存在的神。不可能有神憑藉偶像工作。
**不成子民。**直譯為“不是民的”。
**愚昧的國民。**對前一句“不成子民”進一步的描述。
許多猶太教註釋家認為這指的是聖殿第一次被迦勒底人毀壞，引用的經文是：“迦勒底人之地向來沒有這民”（賽23:13；參哈1:5,6）。他們認為迦勒底人直到上帝興起他們來懲罰以色列人時，才作為一個國家出現。但這種說法缺乏歷史依據。使徒保羅將申32:21用於外邦人在猶太民族拒絕彌賽亞之後接受了福音（見羅10:19；參帖前2:15,16）。另見基督在太21:43,44中的話。
21.en:
**Jealousy.** See v. 16.
**Not God.** Or, “a no-god.” The idols they worshiped represented gods that did not exist. There were no gods working in and through the idols.
**Not a people.** Literally, “a no-people.”
**A foolish nation.** A further description of the “no-people” in the preceding sentence.
Many Jewish commentators refer this to the first destruction of the Temple by the Chaldeans, quoting: “Behold the land of the Chaldeans; this people was not” (Isa. 23:13; cf. Hab. 1:5, 6). The commentators maintain that the Chaldeans had no national status of any moment until God raised them up to punish Israel. But this argument is historically invalid. The apostle Paul applies Deut. 32:21 to the taking of the gospel to the Gentiles, upon the refusal of the Jewish nation to accept the Messiah (see Rom. 10:19; cf. 1 Thess. 2:15, 16). See also the words of Christ in Matt. 21:43, 44.

22.zh:
因為在我怒中有火燒起，直燒到極深的陰間，把地和地的出產盡都焚燒，山的根基也燒著了。

**火。**象徵大災難（見結30:8）或突然發怒（見耶15:14；17:4）。“陰間”是比喻毀滅（見箴15:11；詩86:13）。
**極深的陰間。**直譯為“示阿勒的深淵”（英文RSV版），就是“墳墓”的深淵。喻指完全消滅。
**山。**猶太教註釋家說耶路撒冷是造在山上並被山環繞的（見詩125:2），認為尼布甲尼撒的侵略部分應驗了這個預言（見王下25:1-7）。
22.en:
**Fire.** A symbol of great calamities (see Eze. 30:8) or a flaring up of anger (see Jer. 15:14; 17:4). “Hell” is a figure of destruction (see Prov. 15:11; Ps. 86:13).
**The lowest hell.** Literally, “the depths of Sheol” (RSV), that is, of the “grave.” A figurative expression denoting total extinction.
**The mountains.** Jewish commentators speak of Jerusalem as established upon and encompassed by mountains (see Ps. 125:2), and refer to the invasion by Nebuchadnezzar as fulfilling, in part, this prediction (see 2 Kings 25:1–7).

23.zh:
我要將禍患堆在他們身上，把我的箭向他們射盡。

比喻上帝的審判（見詩7:12,13；38:2；91:5；哀3:12,13；結5:16）。
**懷愛倫註釋（23–24節）**。《先知與君王》395。
23.en: **Spend mine arrows.** A figure of speech referring to God’s judgments (see Ps. 7:12, 13; 38:2; 91:5; Lam. 3:12, 13; Eze. 5:16).

24.zh:
他們必因飢餓消瘦，被炎熱苦毒吞滅。我要打發野獸用牙齒咬他們，並土中腹行的，用毒氣害他們。

**因飢餓消瘦。**直譯為“飢餓的消耗”。其動詞詞根的意思是“吸出”，其形容詞的意思，如這裡所用的，是因飢餓而“被吸出”或“吸空”。
**炎熱苦毒。**直譯為“火箭”。見下列含有該希伯來詞的經文：詩78:48，“閃電”；歌8:6，“電光”；哈3:5，“熱症”；詩76:3，“火箭”。
**腹行的。**或“爬行的”。原文源於詞根“爬行”或“爬”。
24.en:
**Burnt with hunger.** Literally, “the wastings of hunger.” The verb root means “to suck out,” and the adjective, as here, means “sucked out” or “empty” from hunger.
**Burning heat.** Literally, “the firebolt.” Compare the following verses having the same Hebrew word: Ps. 78:48, “hot thunderbolts”; S. of Sol. 8:6, “coals”; Hab. 3:5, “burning coals”; Ps. 76:3, “arrows.”
**Serpents.** Or, “creeping things.” The word here translated “serpents” is from the root “to crawl,” “to creep.” In Micah 7:17 the same word is translated “worms.”

25.zh:
外頭有刀劍，內室有驚恐，使人喪亡，使少男、童女、吃奶的、白髮的，盡都滅絕。

本節將戰爭描繪為罪惡之極。戰爭不放過男女老少，也不保留任何安全的地方（見耶9:19-22；哀1:20；結7:15）。
25.en: **The sword.** This verse portrays warfare as the climax of evils. It would spare neither age nor sex, and no place could afford safety from its effects (see Jer. 9:19–22; Lam. 1:20; Eze. 7:15).

26.zh:
我說，我必將他們分散遠方，使他們的名號從人間除滅。

希伯來原文的含義不明。有些註釋家認為，“我要將他們吹散”，就是，使他們完全分散。
**懷愛倫註釋（26–30節）**。《證言》卷一365。
26.en: **Scatter them into corners.** Literally, “cleave them to pieces.” The Hebrew reading is not clear. Some commentators suggest, “I will blow them away,” that is, utterly disperse them.

27.zh:
惟恐仇敵惹動我，只怕敵人錯看，說：是我們手的能力，並非耶和華所行的。

**惟恐。**不是指耶和華象人一樣感到恐懼。祂經常用人所能理解的語言來說話（見民14:13-16；出32:12）。
**錯看。**就是沒有看清真相。
**是我們手的能力。**誇耀說他們戰勝以色列人完全是依靠自己的本事，而沒有認識到這是耶和華允許他們勝利的（見賽10:5-11；哈1:15,16）。
27.en:
**I feared.** Not that Jehovah experiences fear as men do. He often speaks in language adapted to human understanding (see Num. 14:13–16; Ex. 32:12).
**Behave.** That is, fail to recognize the true facts of the case.
**Our hand is high.** Boasting that they were victorious over Israel solely on account of their own superiority, failing to realize that Jehovah had granted them the victory (see Isa. 10:5–11; Hab. 1:15, 16).

28.zh:
因為以色列民毫無計謀，心中沒有聰明。

**毫無計謀。**“毫無”的原文來源於動詞“滅亡”、“毀滅”、“使失喪”。該詞在舊約中出現200多次，都作這樣的理解。這句話也可以被譯為“計謀的敗亡”。就是他們隨從假牧人的壞主意，因而滅亡（見耶18:18）。關於其他使用該詞根的經文，見利26:38；書23:16；王下9:8；斯4:16；伯18:17等，均理解為“死亡”（申26:5；伯4:11；29:13；31:19）、“破碎”（詩31:12）、“拋棄”（撒上9:20；詩119:176）。
**懷愛倫註釋（28–31節）**。《先知與君王》395。
28.en: **Void of counsel.** The word here translated “void” is from the verb “to perish,” “to destroy,” “to be lost,” and is so translated in practically every instance of the some 200 times the verb is found in the OT. It can be rendered “perishing of counsel.” That is, they were following thoroughly bad counsel given by false shepherds, and were perishing as a result (see Jer. 18:18). For other texts using this root, see Lev. 26:38; Joshua 23:16; 2 Kings 9:8; Esther 4:16; Job 18:17; etc. The precise form used here is also translated as “perish” (Deut. 26:5; Job 4:11; 29:13; 31:19), “broken” (Ps. 31:12), and “lost” (1 Sam. 9:20; Ps. 119:176).

29.zh:
惟願他們有智慧，能明白這事，肯思念他們的結局。

意思是能清楚看透他們的結局。
29.en: **Their latter end.** The KJV has omitted the preposition “to,” as in the original: “they would discern clear through to their latter end.”

30.zh:
若不是他們的磐石賣了他們，若不是耶和華交出他們，一人焉能追趕他們千人？二人焉能使萬人逃跑呢？

**賣了他們。**本節描述了他們的完全相反的命運，因為他們離棄了耶和華（見利26:8,17,36,37；申28:25）。
**交出他們。**這個動詞還譯為“交在”（撒上24:18）、“交付”（哀2:7；摩6:8）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《給傳道人的證言》277。
30.en:
**Sold them.** This verse depicts a complete reversal of their fortunes, due to their having forsaken Jehovah (see Lev. 26:8, 17, 36, 37; Deut. 28:25).
**Shut them up.** See the same verb, here translated “shut up,” rendered as “delivered” (1 Sam. 24:18), “given up” (Lam. 2:7), “deliver up” (Amos 6:8).

31.zh:
據我們的仇敵自己斷定，他們的磐石不如我們的磐石。

**他們的磐石。**異教國家依賴他們的神求得成功和勝利。但是當他們看到耶和華的大能時，不得不承認祂遠遠超過他們的神（見出14:25；民23,24；書2:9；撒上5:7）。關於以色列人的磐石，見申32:4註釋。
31.en: **Their rock.** The heathen nations trusted their gods for victory and success. But when they witnessed the power of Jehovah they were forced to acknowledge His infinite superiority to their gods (see Ex. 14:25; Num. 23, 24; Joshua 2:9; 1 Sam. 5:7). On the Rock of Israel, see on Deut. 32:4.

34.zh:
這不都是積蓄在我這裡，封鎖在我府庫中嗎？

**懷愛倫註釋（34–35節）**。《先知與君王》396。

37.zh:
他必說：他們的神，他們所投靠的磐石，

**磐石。**諷指假神（見第31節）。
37.en: **Rock.** Ironically used of false gods (see v. 31).

38.zh:
就是向來吃他們祭牲的脂油，喝他們奠祭之酒的，在哪裡呢？他可以興起幫助你們，護衛你們。

見賽46:1,2,7；參王上18:27。
38.en: **Let them rise.** See Isa. 46:1, 2, 7; cf. 1 Kings 18:27.

39.zh:
你們如今要知道：我，惟有我是神；在我以外並無別神。我使人死，我使人活；我損傷，我也醫治，並無人能從我手中救出來。

注意代詞的重複，見何5:14；賽43:11,25；51:12。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《給傳道人的證言》23。
39.en: **I, even I.** Note the repeated pronoun, and compare Hosea 5:14; Isa. 43:11, 25; 51:12.

40.zh:
我向天舉手說：我憑我的永生起誓：

**舉手。**莊嚴許願的標誌。參亞伯拉罕的經歷（創14:22），和以色列人進迦南的經歷（出6:8；尼9:15）。見啟10:5中天使莊嚴的宣誓。
40.en: **Lift up my hand.** The sign of a solemn vow. Compare the experience of Abraham (Gen. 14:22), and that of the children of Israel on entering Canaan (Ex. 6:8; Neh. 9:15). Compare the solemn oath of the angel of Rev. 10:5.

41.zh:
我若磨我閃亮的刀，手掌審判之權，就必報復我的敵人，報應恨我的人。

**我的敵人。**耶和華在詩歌中經常被描述為一個勇士，與其子民的仇敵爭戰（見出15:3；賽14:13）。與上帝的子民為敵就是把自己當作上帝的敵人，並與上帝對抗。
41.en: **Mine enemies.** Jehovah is often depicted in poetic imagery as a warrior, combating the enemies of His people (see Ex. 15:3; Isa. 14:13). To oppose God’s people is to set oneself up as an enemy of God and to fight against Him.

42.zh:
我要使我的箭飲血飲醉，就是被殺被擄之人的血。我的刀要吃肉，乃是仇敵中首領之頭的肉。

**箭。**比喻殺戮（見賽34:5,6；66:16）。見基督對其再來時景象的描述（太24:36-44；可13:35-37），和彼得的預言（彼後3:10）。
42.en: **Arrows.** Figurative of great slaughter (see Isa. 34:5, 6; 66:16). Compare the words of Christ respecting scenes connected with His second coming (Matt. 24:36–44; Mark 13:35–37), and the prophecy of Peter (2 Peter 3:10).

43.zh:
你們外邦人當與主的百姓一同歡呼；因他要伸他僕人流血的冤，報應他的敵人，潔淨他的地，救贖他的百姓。

上帝眷顧祂的土地和子民。這些話將完全應驗在進入新天新地的得救之人身上（見啟21:1-7）。使徒保羅引用了本節證明外邦人必能分享基督所提供的救恩（見羅15:10）。
43.en: **Merciful.** God’s mercy upon His land and his people. These words will meet their complete fulfillment in relation to the saved in the new earth (see Rev. 21:1–7). The apostle Paul quotes this verse to show that the Gentiles must partake of the salvation made available by Christ (see Rom. 15:10).

44.zh:
摩西和嫩的兒子約書亞去將這歌的一切話說給百姓聽。

這是申31:30的重複。約書亞（見民13:8,16）是摩西的同工（見申31:3,7,14,23）。
44.en: **He, and Hoshea.** A repetition of Deut. 31:30, except that Hoshea, that is, Joshua (see Num. 13:8, 16) is mentioned as the colaborer of Moses (see Deut. 31:3, 7, 14, 23).

47.zh:
因為這不是虛空、與你們無關的事，乃是你們的生命；在你們過約但河要得為業的地上必因這事日子得以長久。

侍奉上帝決不會沒有報償（見申30:20）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《教育論》174；《先知與君王》500。
47.en: **Not a vain thing.** The service of God never goes without its reward (see ch. 30:20).

49.zh:
你上這亞巴琳山中的尼波山去，在摩押地與耶利哥相對，觀看我所要賜給以色列人為業的迦南地。

亞巴琳山是指一個山脈，其中的一個山是尼波山。上帝在此之前已經給予了摩西有關其去世的指示（見民27:12的註釋）。
**觀看……迦南地。**摩西得到了用肉眼觀看應許之地的特權。他還在異象中看到歷代上帝子民的歷史，直到萬物的結局（見《祖》第472-477頁）。
**懷愛倫註釋（49–50節）**。《先祖與先知》470。
49.en:
**Abarim.** Abarim is understood to refer to a mountain range, of which one peak is Nebo. Instruction in respect to his death had been given Moses previously (see on Num. 27:12).
**Behold the land.** Moses was given the privilege of viewing the Promised Land with his natural sight. Beyond that, he saw, in vision, scenes from the history of God’s people down through the ages to the final consummation of all things (see PP 472-477).

50.zh:
你必死在你所登的山上，歸你列祖（原文作本民）去，像你哥哥亞倫死在何珥山上，歸他的列祖一樣。

**歸你本民去。**見民20:24註釋。摩西至死順從。上帝重視他的去世。在某些方面，他是基督的一種預表。上帝使他從孤獨的安息之處復活，安居在天上的迦南，並在基督登山變像的時候派他來鼓勵基督（見可9:2-4）。這是他在主的家中作忠心僕人的獎賞（見來3:5）。
**像你哥哥亞倫。**見民20:24-28；33:38。
**懷愛倫註釋（50–52節）**。《救贖的故事》166。
50.en:
**Gathered unto thy people.** See on Num. 20:24. Moses was obedient unto death, and his death was precious to God. In some respects he was a type of Christ. God raised him from his lonely resting place to dwell in the heavenly Canaan, and sent him to encourage Christ at His transfiguration (see Mark 9:2–4). Such a reward came to him as a faithful servant in his Lord’s house (see Heb. 3:5).
**As Aaron.** See Num. 20:24–28; 33:38.

51.zh:
因為你們在尋的曠野，加低斯的米利巴水，在以色列人中沒有尊我為聖，得罪了我。

**得罪了我。**見民27:14。
**沒有尊我為聖”。**見民20:12；27:14。
51.en:
**Ye trespassed.** See Num. 27:14.
**Sanctified me not.** “Did not revere me as holy” (RSV). See Num. 20:12; 27:14.

52.zh:
我所賜給以色列人的地，你可以遠遠地觀看，卻不得進去。

**不得進去。**摩西曾誠懇地期望得到進入聖地的特權，卻被拒絕了（見申1:37；3:25,27；參來11:13）。
52.en: **Not go thither.** Moses earnestly desired the privilege of entering the Holy Land, but was denied it (see Deut. 1:37; 3:25, 27; cf. Heb. 11:13).

5.en:
**A new wife.** That is, if he is “newly married” (RSV; see ch. 20:5–8).
**Go out to war.** See ch. 20:7. It is to the advantage of the state to enact such measures as will honor and exalt marriage. This law provided time for the firm establishment of the home. Even more important, from the Hebrew point of view, it made more certain an heir to perpetuate the family name and to inherit the family land.
**Business.** Literally, “service,” as the Hebrew word is often translated (Num. 4:23, 30, 35, 39, 43; 8:24). This refers to any public service that would take him away from home.
5.zh:
新娶妻之人不可從軍出征，也不可託他辦理什麼公事，可以在家清閒一年，使他所娶的妻快活。

**新娶妻。**就“剛結婚”（見申20:5-8）。
**不可從軍出征。**見申20:7。制定這種尊重婚姻的措施對國家是有利的。這個律例為家庭的穩定提供了時間。更重要的是，在希伯來人看來，這樣更能確保延續家系並繼承家產的後嗣產生。
**公事。**直譯為“任職”，（見民4:23,30,35,39,43；8:24），指任何遠離家鄉的公共服務。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《復臨信徒的家庭》216。

1.zh:
人若娶妻以後，見他有什麼不合理的事，不喜悅他，就可以寫休書交在他手中，打發他離開夫家。

**不合理的事。**直譯為“裸露”，喻指“羞愧”或“羞辱”，像這裡所指。她所犯的罪不可能是姦淫，因為那是要處以死刑的（申22:22；參太19:9）。這只是丈夫認為不得體或不光彩的行為。猶太人將摩西的這個誡命理解為一個人幾乎可以因任何理由休妻（太19:3,7）。但基督解釋說，上帝的旨意並非是叫人如此輕率地離婚（太19:4-6），而且這個規定只是因為他們“心硬”才被制定的（太19:8）。
**休書。**直譯為“分離的字據”。
**交在她手中。**要有一個正式手續，可能是在證人面前，以便使之具有法律效力並且無可非議。
**打發她離開。**另一個正式的手續。丈夫大概有義務至少為她提供送她平安地回父家所需的資財（見創21:14；參申15:13）。
1.en:
**Uncleanness.** Literally, “nakedness,” and figuratively, as here, “shame” or “dishonor.” Her offense could not have been adultery, for that was punishable by death (Deut. 22:22; cf. Matt. 19:9). It was simply some behavior the husband considered improper or disgraceful. The Jews understood this Mosaic precept to mean that a man might divorce his wife for almost any reason (Matt. 19:3, 7). Christ explained, however, that it was not God’s will for divorce to be thus easily obtained (Matt. 19:4–6), and that this provision had been made only because of the “hardness” of their hearts (Matt. 19:8).
**A bill of divorcement.** Literally, “a note of separation.”
**Give it.** This was to be done formally, perhaps before witnesses, in order that it might be legally valid and incontestable.
**Send her out.** Another formal act. Presumably the husband was under obligation to send her forth provided with at least the necessary means to reach her father’s house in safety (see Gen. 21:14; cf. Deut. 15:13).

2.zh:
婦人離開夫家以後，可以去嫁別人。

**可以去。**她的正式離去等於公開宣佈，她已不再是那人的妻子，因此可以隨意地再婚。“分離的字據”，完全解除了婚姻。
2.en: **She may go.** Her formal departure was a public announcement of the fact that she was no longer the man’s wife and was, therefore, free to remarry. The “note of separation,” or “note of cutting,” completely dissolved the marriage.

4.zh:
打發他去的前夫不可在婦人玷汙之後再娶他為妻，因為這是耶和華所憎惡的；不可使耶和華─你神所賜為業之地被玷汙了。

**在婦人玷汙之後。**和後夫成婚使她對前夫而言成為不潔淨的了。對他而言，再娶她就是犯奸淫罪。她對他而言是不合法的（見耶3:1）。
**使……地被玷汙了。**就是因著容許道德上的墮落。上帝雖然容忍了一些祂肯定不會認可的事情（見申14:26註釋），但有些界限是人所不可超過的。“地”時常被擬人化，彷彿它能感受和行動一樣（見利18:25；賽24:5）。
現今有些人以申24:1-4為依據來支持他們所贊同的“基督教的離婚”。事實上，這幾節經文向我們展示了猶太人的家庭生活。娶妻在當時被視為象購置一份財產一樣。丈夫對妻子的權威幾乎是絕對的。這裡所頒佈之律法的目的是為了改善希伯來女性的命運。這個律例絕非為了建立或認可一個低下的道德標準，而是代表了一種比當時所認可的殘酷習俗高尚得多的道德標準。該律例保證了被休婦女的一定權利，並且實際上防止她被人視為淫婦和被遺棄的人。她離開了前夫的家，成為一個自由的女人和受人尊敬的社會成員，有資格建立一個值得尊敬的婚姻。離婚的文書說明了前夫對她不再有任何合法權利，而且她對他也絲毫不負任何義務──她可以自由地成為另一個人的妻子。她不會因再次結婚而犯奸淫罪，她前夫的權利也不會被侵犯。
摩西所制定的離婚律法不是為了廢除上帝在創造時為婚姻制度所設的理想，而是因為人的“心硬”（太19:8）。被拋棄之女人的命運是非常悽慘的。休書減輕了她的悲慘命運。這個律例只是承認了當時普遍的現實，並試圖加以改善。這個律法只是一種許可，而不是命令。這些周詳的規定是為了取消希伯來人顯然在與異教民族的交往中學來的簡單的離婚程序的。
基督強烈反對這種把妻子當作財產的觀念（太5:27-32；19:3-9）。這種觀念曾給猶太婦女帶來極大的不幸和不公。希列學派把“有什麼不合理的事”（申24:1）解釋為任何可能使丈夫不高興的事情。該學派提供了基督時代流行的猶太教宗教哲學。比較嚴格的，但不太出名的煞買學派將“不合理”定義為已被證實的不正派或姦淫之舉。在基督的時代，希列學派允許人因一些瑣事而離婚，如妻子在公共場合露胳膊、將丈夫的飯燒焦了，或丈夫喜歡上另一個女人。關於這種順便的態度，約瑟夫寫道：“人不論因什麼原因想要休妻（其實許多這樣的原因都在男人身上），就當書面保證他不再以她為妻。這樣，她就可以自由地嫁給另一個丈夫，但在給休書之前，不許她如此做”（《上古史》iv.8.23）。
申24:1-4的律例不是設立了離婚制度，而是因人性的缺點和上帝子民當時低下的道德觀念而容忍了離婚。要想知道上帝對於婚姻的旨意，人們絕不可抱著申24:1-4不放，而應回到創1:27和2:24，正如耶穌所做的（太5:27-32；19:3-9）。應以當時的背景，而不是我們的背景為依據，來理解摩西為當時的百姓所寫的話，而且應時刻想到上帝的理想。基督再次使人注意到上帝在伊甸園所定的理想。第一次的婚姻提供了上帝希望其子民今日效法的典範。
4.en:
**She is defiled.** Consummation of marriage with a second husband made her unclean to her first husband. For him ever to take her again would be to commit adultery. She was unlawful to him (see Jer. 3:1).
**Cause the land to sin.** That is, by permitting moral depravity. Although God tolerated some things of which He certainly could not approve (see on Deut. 14:26), there were limits beyond which man might not transgress. The “land” is often personified, as though it felt and acted (see Lev. 18:25; Isa. 24:5).
Today some individuals refer to Deut. 24:1–4 as a basis for what they are pleased to consider “Christian divorce.” In reality, these verses open to our view the home life of the Jew, in which the taking of a wife was regarded as the acquiring of a piece of property. The husband’s authority over his wife was almost absolute. The purpose of the law here announced was to better the lot of Hebrew women. This law, far from establishing a low moral standard, or approving of one, represented a far higher standard than the cruel customs of the time recognized. The law guaranteed a divorced woman certain rights, and actually protected her from being considered as an adulteress and an outcast. She left her first husband’s home a free woman and a respected member of society, eligible to contract an honorable marriage. The writ of divorce stated that her first husband no longer had any legal claim upon her and that she was in no way obligated to him—she was free to become another man’s wife. Upon marrying again she did not become guilty of adultery, and the rights of her first husband were not infringed upon.
The Mosaic divorce law was instituted, not to annul the ideals of marriage as instituted by God at creation, but because of the “hardness” of men’s hearts (Matt. 19:8). The cast-off, unattached woman’s lot was a deplorable one. The bill of divorce alleviated her unfortunate lot. This law simply recognized the prevailing situation and sought to improve it. This was a law of permission, not one of command. These precise restrictions were designed to eliminate the easy divorce procedure the Hebrews had apparently learned in their association with heathen peoples.
It was against the concept of the wife as property that Christ spoke so emphatically (Matt. 5:27–32; 19:3–9). It had brought great misery and injustice to Jewish womanhood. The school of Hillel, which provided the popular Jewish religious philosophy of the time of Christ, interpreted the expression translated “some uncleanness” (Deut. 24:1) as meaning anything that may have become displeasing to the husband. The stricter, less popular Shammai school defined the “uncleanness” as some proved act of immodesty or adultery. In Christ’s time the Hillel school allowed divorce for such trivialities as the exposure of a woman’s arm in public, the burning of a husband’s meal, or when the husband found another woman more attractive. Of this lax attitude Josephus writes, “He that desires to be divorced from his wife for any cause whatsoever (and many such causes happen among men), let him in writing give assurance that he never will use her again as his wife any more, for by these means she may be at liberty to marry another husband, although before this bill of divorce be given, she is not to be permitted so to do” (Antiquities iv. 8. 23).
The law of Deut. 24:1–4 did not institute divorce, but tolerated it in view of the imperfections of human nature and the low moral concepts of God’s people at that time. To know God’s mind concerning marriage one must not camp at Deut. 24:1–4, but journey back to Gen. 1:27 and 2:24, even as Jesus did (Matt. 5:27–32; 19:3–9). The written counsel of Moses for the people of his day is to be interpreted against the background of his day, not of ours, and ever with the divine ideal in view. Christ lifted men’s eyes once more to that divine ideal ordained in Eden. That first marriage provides the pattern God would have His people follow today.

6.zh:
不可拿人的全盤磨石或是上磨石作當頭，因為這是拿人的命作當頭。

**全盤磨石，或是上磨石。**直譯為“兩個磨石，或其中之一”。“上磨石”的原文可以指一塊石頭，或一塊磨石（士9:53；撒下11:21）。
**人的命。**就是因拿走他預備食物所必需的東西而危及其家庭的健康。東方的窮人數千年來都生活在飢餓的邊緣，像這樣表面上看起來微不足道的東西可能會造成極大的悲劇。
6.en:
**Nether or the upper millstone.** Literally, “both millstones or the part of one.” The word translated “upper millstone” may refer to one stone, or to a piece of the mill (Judges 9:53; 2 Sam. 11:21).
**A man’s life.** That is, by taking from him something essential to the preparation of his food, and thus endangering the health of his family. For centuries the poor of the East have lived on the verge of starvation, and a seemingly little thing such as this might prove tragic.

7.zh:
若遇見人拐帶以色列中的一個弟兄，當奴才待他，或是賣了他，那拐帶人的就必治死。這樣，便將那惡從你們中間除掉。

**拐帶。**見出21:16。綁架和販賣人口是一種死罪。人身自由在上帝看來是十分寶貴的。奴隸制是對上帝、對社會和對奴隸不可寬恕的冒犯。但奴隸制從遠古時期就在東方國家以這樣或那樣的形式存在了。上帝給以色列人的律法是為了及早消除奴隸制。奴隸制是對一切人權和尊嚴的侵犯。
7.en: **Stealing.** See Ex. 21:16. Kidnaping a man to make a slave of him was a crime punishable by death. A man’s personal freedom is precious in God’s sight. Slavery is an inexcusable sin against God and against society, as well as against the slave. Yet slavery has existed in some form or other in Eastern lands from time immemorial. The laws of God gave Israel were designed to eliminate slavery, in time. Slavery violates every human right and decency.

8.zh:
在大痲瘋的災病上，你們要謹慎，照祭司利未人一切所指教你們的留意遵行。我怎樣吩咐他們，你們要怎樣遵行。

**大麻瘋。**這是儀文性不潔淨的最壞形式，因此要採取最謹慎的預防措施。《利未記》中有兩章長篇的論述（13和14章），列舉了詳細的症狀。“災病”的原意是“打擊”。該詞原文還用在申17:8；21:5中。
8.en: **Leprosy.** This was the worst form of ceremonial uncleanness, and therefore the most careful precautions were taken in respect to it. Two lengthy chapters in Leviticus (chs. 13 and 14) list the symptoms in great detail. The “plague,” literally, “the stroke.” The same Hebrew word is used in chs. 17:8; 21:5.

9.zh:
當記念出埃及後，在路上，耶和華─你神向米利暗所行的事。

**米利暗。**見民12章。米利暗是以色列的三位傑出領袖之一（彌6:4）。但她卻突然得了可怕的大麻瘋，並從以色列人的營中被趕出去七天之久（民12:14）。她傑出的地位和她與摩西親密的關係都不能使她倖免於難。最窮最苦的麻瘋病人所得到的待遇和有錢有勢的病人是一樣嚴厲的。猶太人一般認為大麻瘋都是上帝的處罰，但這樣不加區別的看待是不合理的（路13:1-6）。大麻瘋是罪的一種表號。屬靈的麻瘋病只有在耶穌基督裡才能得到治癒。
9.en: **Miriam.** See Num. 12. Miriam was one of three prominent leaders of Israel (Micah 6:4). Yet she was suddenly smitten with the dreadful disease leprosy, and driven from the camp of Israel for seven days (Num. 12:14). Neither her outstanding position nor her personal relation to Moses protected her from it. The poorest and most miserable leper was treated no more harshly than a leper from some wealthy or officially prominent family. There was a tendency among the Jews to view all cases of leprosy as divine judgments, but it is not reasonable to take such a view of all such instances (Luke 13:1–6). Leprosy is a type of sin. The spiritual leper, whose very soul is diseased, can find no cure for his malady outside of Jesus Christ.

10.zh:
你借給鄰舍，不拘是什麼，不可進他家拿他的當頭。

**進他家。**這是保護窮人的法律規定。他的家和家產很不值錢，只有極少的必需品。除了房子和田地之外，可能只有衣服、鍋瓢和粗劣的磨盤。但即使這樣的家庭也要受到尊重，不受侵犯。這樣的家庭幾乎沒有可供借貸的抵押品（見出22:26,27），但卻不得橫加侮辱。家主要到門口，出示他可以提供的抵押品。出借人不得進入那家，隨意取走東西。
**懷愛倫註釋（10–12節）**。《服務真詮》187。
**懷愛倫註釋（10–13節）**。《福山寶訓》111。
10.en: **Into his house.** A legal provision for the protection of the poor. His home and its contents would be of small material value, and would consist of only the barest of necessities. Such a family would probably own nothing more than their clothes, a few pots, and a primitive grinding mill, in addition, perhaps, to house and land. Yet such a home was to be respected and to remain inviolate. It had little to offer as security for a loan (see Ex. 22:26, 27), but it was not to be abused as something of little consequence. The owner would come to the door and display what he could offer as security. The lender was not to enter the home to pick and choose what he wished to take.

11.zh:
要站在外面，等那向你借貸的人把當頭拿出來交給你。

**要站在外面。**上帝在窮苦和卑微的人周圍建起了一道圍牆。上帝重視窮人的財產權利如同祂對待有財富和地位的人一樣。見太18:23-35的比喻。上帝希望基督徒在對待其弟兄時表現出體諒的精神。
11.en: **Thou shalt stand abroad.** Literally, “outside thou shalt stand.” God has erected a fence around the poor and humble. The property rights of the needy are as dear to God as are those of the wealthy and socially prominent. Compare the parable of Matt. 18:23–35. God expects the Christian to manifest considerateness in dealing with his brethren.

12.zh:
他若是窮人，你不可留他的當頭過夜。

**他的當頭。**外衣可能是那窮人唯一可以用來當作“當頭”的值錢東西。拿衣服作為抵押不是罕見的事（申24:17；伯22:6；箴20:16；27:13；摩2:8）。這個當頭不得過夜（出22:25,26）。外衣有許多用途（出12:34；士8:25）。關於歸還窮人當頭的要求，見結18:7,12；33:15。
12.en: **His pledge.** His outer cloak may have been the only worth-while thing the poor man had to offer as his “pledge.” To offer clothing as security was not uncommon (Deut. 24:17; Job 22:6; Prov. 20:16; 27:13; Amos 2:8). This pledge was not to be held overnight (Ex. 22:25, 26). The outer garment was used for many purposes (Ex. 12:34; Judges 8:25). On the requirement of restoring a poor man’s pledge see Eze. 18:7, 12; 33:15.

13.zh:
日落的時候，總要把當頭還他，使他用那件衣服蓋著睡覺，他就為你祝福；這在耶和華─你神面前就是你的義了。

亞伯拉罕的信心使他在上帝面前被算作義。對困苦貧窮的人顯示仁慈也同樣是上帝所喜悅的（太25:34-36）。人是上帝慈愛和憐憫的對象，祂也希望我們這樣對待同胞。“義”字的希伯來原文以陽性和陰性形式都出現過。以色列後來的先知，象摩西在這裡一樣，用陰性形式來指對困苦貧窮之人的同情和關心。這些窮人依靠上帝而活（詩10:14；72:12）。上帝總是提醒祂的子民說，他們對祂的義務包括關心和照顧這些窮人（參撒上2:8）。但同時，他們不應故意把“善事” 行在人面前行（太6:1）。他們應在耶和華面前為義。
13.en: **Righteousness.** The faith of Abraham was reckoned to his account before God as righteousness. The manifestation of mercy to the poor and needy is equally pleasing to God (Matt. 25:34–36). Men are the objects of God’s tender love and mercy, and He would have us look upon our fellow men in the same way. The Hebrew word for “righteousness” appears in both masculine and feminine forms. The later prophets of Israel used the feminine form, as Moses does here, with reference to sympathetic attention to the poor and needy. They were dependent on God (Ps. 10:14; 72:12), who ever reminded His people that their obligation to Him included solicitous care for these needy ones (cf. 1 Sam. 2:8). But at the same time they were not to do their “alms,” literally, “righteousness,” before men (Matt. 6:1). They were to be righteous before the Lord.

14.zh:
困苦窮乏的僱工，無論是你的弟兄或是在你城裡寄居的，你不可欺負他。

**欺負。**直譯為“欺騙”。該希伯來詞語還用在利19:13；撒上12:3,4；利6:2,4。
**僱工。**見利19:13；耶22:13；瑪3:5；雅5:4。
**寄居的。**天生的猶太人和皈依猶太教的人之間不應有任何的區別（利19:34）。
**懷愛倫註釋（14–15節）**。《先祖與先知》532。
14.en:
**Oppress.** Literally, “defraud.” The same Hebrew word is used in Lev. 19:13; 1 Sam. 12:3, 4; Lev. 6:2, 4.
**An hired servant.** See Lev. 19:13; Jer. 22:13; Mal. 3:5; James 5:4.
**Strangers.** No difference was to be made between the natural Jew and the proselyte (Lev. 19:34).
**His hire.** Punctuality in the payment of wages is as positive a divine requirement as Sabbath observance or tithing. It is not an act of benevolence, but of justice. Compare the parable on laborers in the vineyard (Matt. 20:1, 2, 8).
**Setteth his heart.** Literally, “lifteth up his soul.” He lived, as it were, from hand to mouth, and had no reserve.

15.zh:
要當日給他工價，不可等到日落─因為他窮苦，把心放在工價上─恐怕他因你求告耶和華，罪便歸你了。

**工價。**按時發工資和守安息日或交十分之一一樣，都是上帝的要求。這不是善行，而是義務。見葡萄園僱工的比喻（太20:1,2,8）。
**把心放在。**直譯為“心裡指望”。他僅能餬口，沒有任何積蓄。

16.zh:
不可因子殺父，也不可因父殺子；凡被殺的都為本身的罪。

**凡被殺的。**在異教國家中因一人的罪而株連全家的事並不希奇（見但6:24）。但上帝卻要犯罪的人自己承擔全部的罪責（王下14:6；結18:10-24）。聖經在罪的處罰，（另見羅6:23），和犯罪的自然後果（出20:5）之間劃出了一條清楚的界線，就像這裡一樣
16.en:
**Every man.** It was not unusual among the heathen to condemn an entire family for the crime of one member (see Dan. 6:24). But God would have the transgressor himself bear the full penalty of his crime (2 Kings 14:6; Eze. 18:10–24). The Scriptures draw a clear line of distinction between a penalty inflicted for a wrong act, as here (see also Rom. 6:23), and the natural results of such an act (Ex. 20:5).
**Pervert the judgment.** See Ex. 22:22–24.
**A widow’s raiment.** Compare Job 24:3. Justice is not to be denied even the most helpless. The stranger, the widow, the orphan, and the helpless are to enjoy the full protection of the law (see Matt. 18:28–35).

17.zh:
你不可向寄居的和孤兒屈枉正直，也不可拿寡婦的衣裳作當頭。

**屈枉正直。**見出22:22-24。
**寡婦的衣裳。**見伯24:3。即使是對待最無助的人，也要公正。寄居的、寡婦、孤兒和無助的人都應完全受到律法的保護（見太18:28-35）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《服務真詮》187。

18.zh:
要記念你在埃及作過奴僕。耶和華─你的神從那裡將你救贖，所以我吩咐你這樣行。

**你……作過奴僕。**見利19:33,34。自己受過壓迫的壓迫者應受到加倍的譴責。
18.en: **Thou wast a bondman.** Compare Lev. 19:33, 34. The oppressor who has himself experienced the bitterness of oppression is doubly culpable.

19.zh:
你在田間收割莊稼，若忘下一捆，不可回去再取，要留給寄居的與孤兒寡婦。這樣，耶和華─你神必在你手裡所辦的一切事上賜福與你。

**莊稼。**上帝制定了很多改善窮人命運的律例（利19:9,10；23:22）。沒有土地的人有權在田間、葡萄園和橄欖樹林中撿另拾遺。田主可以善意地留下落穗，給窮人帶來快樂，減輕他們的困難，同時也讓自己高興（見箴11:24）。
**懷愛倫註釋（19–21節）**。《服務真詮》186。
**懷愛倫註釋（19–22節）**。《先祖與先知》531。
19.en: **Thine harvest.** God ordained numerous laws for easing the lot of the needy (Lev. 19:9, 10; 23:22). The landless were given the privilege of gleaning the fields, the vineyards, and the olive groves. The landowner could well spare the gleanings, and thereby bring happiness to the poor, relieve their need, and at the same time warm his own heart (see Prov. 11:24).

20.zh:
你打橄欖樹，枝上剩下的，不可再打；要留給寄居的與孤兒寡婦。

**橄欖樹。**每年收穫的時節特別提醒人同情心的價值與美。窮人的存在為我們提供了一個培養慷慨精神的機會。那些在收穫的時節，就是在接受大自然慷慨禮物的時侯仍硬著心腸的人，在其他時候也不太可能慷慨解囊。
20.en: **Olive tree.** From season to season the harvesttime in particular would remind men of the value and beauty of a compassionate spirit. The existence of the poor among us provides an opportunity for cultivating the spirit of generosity. He who remains callous of heart at harvesttime, when he gathers in the bountiful gifts of nature, may scarcely be expected to exercise generosity at other times.

22.zh:
你也要記念你在埃及地作過奴僕，所以我吩咐你這樣行。

**記念。**見第18節；申15:15。我們自己所經歷生活中的艱難和失望，應使我們學會同情那些後來可能與我們有一樣遭遇的人。
22.en: **Remember.** See v. 18; ch. 15:15. Our own difficult and disappointing experiences in life should make us sympathetic toward others who may at a later time be suffering as we once did.

1.en:
**At that time.** That is, the 40 days and nights of intercession spoken of in ch. 9, which followed this command (Ex. 34:1, 2, 28).
**Hew thee.** The first stone tables were provided by God (Ex. 24:12), the second by Moses.
**Make thee an ark.** This command was given during the first period of 40 days (Ex. 25:10). Some Jewish commentators havemaintained that there were two arks, one to go before the people in their warfare and another to remain in the tabernacle, but of this there is no evidence whatever. The ark here referred to can be no other than the ark, for now, 38 years later, the tables were still where Moses first placed them (v. 5).
1.zh:
那時，耶和華吩咐我說：你要鑿出兩塊石版，和先前的一樣，上山到我這裡來，又要做一木櫃。

**那時。**就是第9章中所提到的摩西四十晝夜的代求（出34:1,2,28）。
**你要鑿出。**第一次的石版是上帝提供的（出24:12），第二次是摩西提供的。
**要作一木櫃。**這個命令是在頭一個四十天內發出的（出25:10）。有些猶太教註釋家認為有兩個約櫃，一個是在作戰時行在百姓前面的，另一個是留在帳幕中的，這種觀點沒有絲毫證據。這裡被提到的木櫃只能是約櫃。現在，三十八年過去了，兩塊石版還在最初摩西放置的地方（第5節）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《服務真詮》508。

5.en:
**Came down.** That is, at the close of the 40 days and nights (Ex. 34:28, 29; cf. Ex. 32:15 and Deut. 9:15).
**The ark.** Made by Bezaleel under the direction of Moses (Ex. 37:1; see on Deut. 10:1). The ark was placed in the tabernacle, upon its completion, with the two tables of stone in it in harmony with God’s instructions (Ex. 40:20, 21).
**There they be.** They were still in the ark several centuries later (1 Kings 8:1, 9), during Solomon’s reign. There is no record that they were ever removed from the ark. They are there today (PK 453), and “will be presented before the world as the standard of righteousness” (EGW in RH Jan. 28, 1909, p. 8).
5.zh:
我轉身下山，將這版放在我所做的櫃中，現今還在那裡，正如耶和華所吩咐我的。

**下山。**就是在四十晝夜結束時（出34:28,29；參出32:15和申9:15）。
**櫃。**是由比撒列按照摩西的指示做的（出37:1；見申10:1註釋）。約櫃做完後被放在帳幕內，其中有按照上帝的吩咐而安放的兩塊石版（出40:20,21）。
**現今還在那裡。**數世紀之後，在所羅門在位的時候，石版依然在約櫃中（王上8:1,9）。沒有任何記錄顯示石版曾從約櫃中被取出來過。石版如今還在那裡（《知君》第453頁），並“將展示在世人面前作為公義的標準”（懷愛倫《評論與通訊》1909年1月28日刊，第8頁）。

4.en:
**The ten commandments.** Literally, “the ten words,” as in Ex. 20:1; 34:28; Deut. 4:13. The word thus translated and used in this sense means a “precept” or an “edict” (Esther 1:19). It is also used of a “sentence” or “saying” of a wise man (Eccl. 1:1; etc.), and of an “oracle” or “word” of God (Num. 23:5, 16; Jer. 1:4, 11; etc.). Its use with respect to the Ten Commandments identifies them as a divine revelation and is a remainder of the fact that God spoke them in the hearing of all Israel (Deut. 4:13).
**The day of the assembly.** See on ch. 9:10.
4.zh:
耶和華將那大會之日、在山上從火中所傳與你們的十條誡，照先前所寫的，寫在這版上，將版交給我了。

**十條誡。**直譯為“十言”，見出20:1；34:28；申4:13。其原文的意思就是“訓詞”或“法令”（斯1:19）。此詞也被用來指智慧人所說的“話語”或“言論”（傳1:1等），以及上帝的“話”或“道”（民23:5,16；耶1:4,11等）。此詞用於十條誡命表明它們是上帝的啟示，也是提醒人上帝曾向全體以色列人宣讀它們（申4:13）。
**那大會之日。**見申9:10註釋。

3.en: **Shittim wood.** Literally, “planks of shittim.” This was probably a species of thorny acacia abundant in the vicinity of Sinai.
3.zh:
於是我用皂莢木做了一櫃，又鑿出兩塊石版，和先前的一樣，手裡拿這兩塊版上山去了。

**皂莢木。**直譯為“皂莢木板”。可能是在西乃山附近盛產的一種刺槐樹。

2.en: **I will write.** The law of God is ineffective until we individually permit Him to write it anew on “fleshy tables of the heart” (2 Cor. 3:3; see also Rom. 8:3, 4). It is only when the world beholds the reflection of the law written upon our hearts that it is instructed and edified. As the tables of stone were inscribed by God, and witnessed to His character and will, so the church bears the inscription wrought by the Holy Spirit, set forth for all men to read (2 Cor. 3:2). Such a life is a monument to God’s grace, a memorial of His power operating in the lives of men.
2.zh:
你先前摔碎的那版，其上的字我要寫在這版上；你要將這版放在櫃中。

上帝的律法只有當我們各自允許上帝將律法重新寫“在心版上”時才有效（林後3:3；另見羅8:3,4）。只有當世人目睹寫在我們心版上之律法的形象時，他們才得到教訓和造就。正如石版是上帝親手書寫的，而且是上帝品格和旨意的見證，教會也帶有聖靈所寫的題詞，顯明出來讓眾人唸誦（林後3:2）。這樣的人生是上帝恩典的豐碑，是上帝的大能在人類的生活中運行的紀念。

6.zh:
（以色列人從比羅比尼亞幹（或作：亞乾井）起行，到了摩西拉。亞倫死在那裡，就葬在那裡。他兒子以利亞撒接續他供祭司的職分。

**比羅比尼亞幹。**即民33:32中的比尼亞幹。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖與先知》427。
6.en: **The children of Jaakan.** Bene-jaakan in Num. 33:32.

7.zh:
他們從那裡起行，到了谷歌大，又從谷歌大到了有溪水之地的約巴他。

**從那裡。**就是從比尼亞幹（民33:32）。
**谷歌大。**這是曷哈及甲，直譯為“軍隊之山”（見民33:32）。
**約巴他。**民33:34的約巴他。
**溪水。**這裡的水源豐富，所以不久之後在加低斯的缺水就更顯嚴重了（見民20:3,4）。約巴他可能就是他巴泉，位於亞喀巴灣之北約22英里（35公里）。
7.en:
**From thence.** That is, from Bene-jaakan (Num. 33:32).
**Gudgodah.** This is Hor-hagidgad, literally, “the mount of the troop” (see Num. 33:32).
**Jotbath.** Jotbath of Num. 33:34.
**Rivers of waters.** Here the water was abundant, a fact that no doubt accentuated the lack of it at Kadesh soon after (see Num. 20:3, 4). Jotbath is possibly to be identified with et–Taba, about 22 mi. north of ‘Aqaba.

8.zh:
那時，耶和華將利未支派分別出來，抬耶和華的約櫃，又侍立在耶和華面前事奉他，奉他的名祝福，直到今日。

**那時。**就是在西乃山（見第5,10節）。指的是摩西第二次在山上寄居四十天後的回營。
**將……分別出來。**這裡所使用的希伯來語動詞形式表示獻身侍奉上帝的莊嚴之舉。以色列人也是這樣從其他民族中被“分別出來”（利20:24），利未人從以色列人的其他支派中被“分別出來”（民16:9），藉此使他們特歸耶和華（民8:14）。利未人曾響應摩西的號召，將自己從其他支派中分別出來，在叛教的同胞當中，表明他們擁護上帝的立場（出32:26-29）。在品格上，他們憑著自己的選擇與他們的弟兄分別出來；現在，憑著上帝的選擇，他們被分別出來為上帝服務。
**抬耶和華的約櫃。**當營地從一處遷移到另一處時，這一神聖的職責被分派給了哥轄族（民3:27,31）。
**侍立在耶和華面前。**指在公共崇事中獻身為上帝服務，就像宮中的大臣在國王面前侍奉一樣。祭司向上帝負責。這種說法也被用來表示先知侍奉上帝（王上17:1；18:15）。以及基哈西對先知以利沙的照料（王下5:25）。
**侍奉他。**利未人應作為祭司的助手侍奉他們（民3:6），並且負責照看帳幕（申10:8）。“利未人”這個名稱後來被用來表示祭司支派中非亞倫家族的成員。亞倫的子孫與“利未人”不是同一概念。利未人奉命從事除敬拜和獻祭以外的聖所崇事。
**奉他的名祝福。**見民6:23-27，其中將這句話用來指讚美上帝和舉手祝福百姓。這是祭司所履行的一種莊嚴職責（利9:22）作為早、晚崇事及其他時候所用的結束之舉。國王在重大場合中也為百姓祝福（撒下6:18）。摩西在申21:5節中再次提到了這一點。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《教育論》148，《證言》卷一650。
8.en:
**At that time.** That is, at Sinai (see vs. 5, 10). Reference is to Moses’ return to camp following his second sojourn of 40 days in the mountain.
**Separated.** The form of the Hebrew verb here used indicates a solemn act of dedication to the service of God. In a similar way Israel was “separated” from among other nations (Lev. 20:24), and the Levites from among the tribes of Israel (Num. 16:9), thereby making them peculiarly Jehovah’s (Num. 8:14). The Levites had separated themselves from the other tribes in response to Moses’ call to take a stand for God in the midst of apostasy (Ex. 32:26–29). In character they were separate from their brethren, by virtue of their own choice; now, by virtue of God’s choice, they are separated to His service.
**To bear the ark.** This sacred duty was assigned to the Kohathites, as the camp was moved from one site to another (Num. 3:27, 31).
**Stand before the Lord.** This is a phrase that denotes consecrated devotion to the Lord’s service, in public ministry. They ministered to God as court officials did before a king. The priests were responsible to God. It is used also of the prophets as ministers of God (1 Kings 17:1; 18:15). It is used also of the attendance of Gehazi upon the prophet Elisha (2 Kings 5:25).
**To minister unto him.** The Levites were to serve the priests as their assistants (Num. 3:6), and to take general care of the tabernacle (Deut. 10:8). The name “Levite” came to designate the non-Aaronic membersof the priestly tribe. The sons of Aaron are not technically “Levites.” The Levites were consecrated to the duties of the sanctuary service, other than those of worship and sacrifice.
**Bless in his name.** See Num. 6:23–27, where this expression is used of praising God and blessing the people with uplifted hands. This was a solemn duty performed by priests (Lev. 9:22) as the closing act of the morning and evening service and at other times. On momentous occasions the kings also blessed the people (2 Sam. 6:18). Moses speaks of it again in Deut. 21:5.

9.zh:
所以利未人在他弟兄中無分無業，耶和華是他的產業，正如耶和華─你神所應許他的。）

**無分。**由於利未人被“分別出來”從事聖工（第8節），他們便不能從事較為普通的職業來謀生。正因為如此，除了一些分散在各支派中的城以外，他們沒有被分到屬於自己支派的領土（民18:20；書13:14,33；18:7）。
**他的產業。**這句話的含義可以在申2-4章中找到。利未支派要從會眾獻給耶和華的神聖供物中領受一份。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》433；《教育論》149。
9.en:
**Hath no part.** Inasmuch as the Levites were “separated” to sacred service (v. 8) they could not earn a living by engaging in the more common pursuits. For this reason they were assigned no tribal territory, except for certain cities scattered throughout the other tribes (Num. 18:20; Joshua 13:14, 33; 18:7).
**His inheritance.** The meaning of this expression is found in ch. 2–4. The tribe of Levi was to receive a share in the sacred offerings brought to Jehovah by the congregation.

11.zh:
耶和華吩咐我說：你起來引導這百姓，使他們進去得我向他們列祖起誓應許所賜之地。

**你起來引導。**直譯為“起來，拆營”。原文還出現在民10:2中。此詞也被用來指在採石場打碎或撬開整塊石頭（王上6:7）。
11.en: **Arise, take thy journey.** Literally, “rise, break camp.” The word here translated “journey” appears also in Num. 10:2. It is used, as well, of breaking or prying whole stones loose in a stone quarry (1 Kings 6:7).

12.zh:
以色列啊，現在耶和華─你神向你所要的是什麼呢？只要你敬畏耶和華─你的神，遵行他的道，愛他，盡心盡性事奉他，

**上帝向你所要的。**這個說法與彌6:8相似。。“掃羅”這個名字也來源於相同的詞根，意思就是“所要的”、或“所希望的”。
**敬畏。**直譯為“崇敬”、“敬虔地對待”。崇敬在這裡作為上帝兒女心中要有的一個基本原則。對上帝的正確態度乃是真宗教的基礎（見申6:2的註釋）。
**遵行。**見申8:6的註釋。這是指每日靠聖靈的能力與上帝同行，追求完全的品格（見創5:22）。使徒保羅以不同的言語表達了這個真理（羅6:17,18,22）。
**愛。**只要人心中對上帝有真實的愛，人就不會軟弱地屈從試探了（見創39:9；申13:4；王上8:23,48；約15:10）。
**懷愛倫註釋（12–13節）**。《基督教育原理》477；《先知與君王》326。
12.en:
**God require of thee.** This is similar to Micah 6:8. The word translated “require” also means “to desire,” “to request.” The name “Saul” is from the same root, and means “requested,” “desired.”
**To fear.** Literally, “to reverence,” “to have a pious regard for.” Here reverence is required as a basic principle in the heart of God’s child. A right attitude toward God is the foundation of true religion (see on ch. 6:2).
**To walk.** See on ch. 8:6. This is a daily walk with God in the power of the Holy Spirit, in pursuit of a perfect character (see Gen. 5:22). The apostle Paul states the same truth in different words (Rom. 6:17, 18, 22).
**To love.** Where there is true love of God in the heart, a man will not weakly yield himself to temptation (see Gen. 39:9; Deut. 13:4; 1 Kings 8:23, 48; John 15:10).

13.zh:
遵守他的誡命律例，就是我今日所吩咐你的，為要叫你得福。

**誡命。**其動詞詞根的意思就是“設立”、“建立”。十誡的原則是以上帝的品格為基礎的，因此是被堅固地樹立起來的。所羅門說守誡是“眾人的本分”（傳12:13,14），因為它們表達對上帝和對同胞的愛（太22:36-40）。
13.en: **The commandments.** From the usual word for “commandments.” The verb root means “to set up,” “to establish.” The principles of the Decalogue are based on the character of God, and thus firmly established. Keeping the commandments is said by Solomon to be “the whole duty of man” (Eccl. 12:13, 14), because they express love toward God and one’s fellow men (Matt. 22:36–40).

14.zh:
看哪，天和天上的天，地和地上所有的，都屬耶和華─你的神。

**天。**就是大氣層的天空。
**天上的天。**指上帝的居所（見王上8:27；詩68:32,33；148:1-4）。使徒保羅稱之為“第三層天”（林後12:2），並提到基督升到“諸天之上”（弗4:10）。
**地。**人類應該追求度一種讚美耶和華的生活，如同天上的居民所作的那樣（見詩19:1-6）。
14.en:
**The heaven.** That is, the atmospheric heavens.
**Heaven of heavens.** A reference to the dwelling place of God (see 1 Kings 8:27; Ps. 68:32, 33; 148:1–4). The apostle Paul spoke of “the third heaven” (2 Cor. 12:2) and of Christ ascending “far above all heavens” (Eph. 4:10).
**The earth.** Men should seek to live a life of praise to Jehovah as do the inhabitants of heaven (see Ps. 19:1–6).

15.zh:
耶和華但喜悅你的列祖，愛他們，從萬民中揀選他們的後裔，就是你們，像今日一樣。

**愛他們。**見申7:6,7。
15.en: **To love them.** See ch. 7:6, 7.

16.zh:
所以你們要將心裡的汙穢除掉，不可再硬著頸項。

使徒保羅以相似的口吻向現今的信徒表達了相同的原則（羅2:29）。未受割禮的心對聖靈的呼喚是無動於衷的。受割禮的心乃是愛上帝的心（申30:6；耶4:4）。未受割禮的心是驕傲自大的（利26:41；另見耶9:25；結44:7,9）。該說法還用來指耳朵（耶6:10）以及嘴唇（出6:12,30）。
這種比喻性的說法可能來自耕地的公牛，它們有時將頭和前腿從軛中退出來，試圖擺脫重擔（見尼9:29；亞7:11）。看司提反對猶太人所說的話（徒7:51）。
16.en:
**Be no more stiffnecked.** Literally, “not will ye harden your neck any more.” The apostle Paul expresses the same principle in similar terms for the believer today (Rom. 2:29). An uncircumcised heart is impervious to the appeal of the Holy Spirit. The circumcised heart is one that loves God (Deut. 30:6; Jer. 4:4). An uncircumcised heart is lifted up in pride (Lev. 26:41; see also Jer. 9:25; Eze. 44:7, 9). The same expression is used of the ear (Jer. 6:10) and of the lips (Ex. 6:12, 30).
This figurative expression may come from work bullocks, that sometimes withdraw their shoulders and neck from the yoke in an endeavor to back away from the load (see Neh. 9:29; Zech 7:11). Compare the words in Stephen’s presentation to the Jews (Acts 7:51).

17.zh:
因為耶和華─你們的神─他是萬神之神，萬主之主，至大的神，大有能力，大而可畏，不以貌取人，也不受賄賂。

**萬神之神。**注意詩人的勸告（詩136:2,3），以及巴比倫王對但以理所說的話語（但2:47）。當基督在恩門關閉之時脫去其祭司的服飾，穿上君王的衣袍時，祂將採用類似的頭銜，“萬王之王，萬主之主”（啟19:16，參17:14）。
**至大的上帝。**尼希米用了類似的話（尼9:32）。
**大有能力。**譯自一個表示大英雄、大勇士的字彙（士11:1）。此詞也用來指百獸中最強壯的獅子（箴30:30）。此詞以最高級的形式在申10:14節中用來指上帝的居所，與這個描述上帝的說法相似。
**不以貌取人。**這句話直譯為“祂不抬舉臉面，也不受賄賂”。耶和華總會秉公行事。祭物和禮物不會使祂轉而寬恕故意的邪惡（見出23:8；利19:15）。注意使徒彼得在與哥尼流交談時所使用的話語，哥尼流象彼得一樣也見了一個異象（徒10:34,35）。
**懷愛倫註釋（17–19節）**。《歷代願望》500。
**懷愛倫註釋（17–21節）**。《基督教育原理》477。
17.en:
**God of gods.** Note the exhortation of the psalmist (Ps. 136:2, 3), and the words of the king of Babylon to Daniel (Dan. 2:47). When Christ removes His priestly attire and assumes His royal garments, at the close of probation, He assumes a similar title, “King of kings, and Lord of lords” (Rev. 19:16, cf. 17:14).
**A great God.** Nehemiah uses similar language (Neh. 9:32).
**Mighty.** From a word denoting a great hero, a mighty warrior (Judges 11:1). It is also applied to the lion as the mightiestamong beasts (Prov. 30:30). The superlative used in Deut. 10:14 of God’s dwelling place is similar to this expression for God.
**Regardeth not persons.** This statement reads, literally, “not does he lift up faces, and not does he take a bribe.” Jehovah will always deal justly. Sacrifices and gifts do not influence Him to condone willful wickedness (see Ex. 23:8; Lev. 19:15). Note the words of the apostle Peter in his contact with Cornelius, who, like Peter, had received a vision (Acts 10:34, 35).

18.zh:
他為孤兒寡婦伸冤，又憐愛寄居的，賜給他衣食。

在東方，司法的公正歷來都是出名地遲緩和不穩定，但耶和華不僅毫不偏心，而且行動迅速。在出22:21,22節中，上帝吩咐祂的百姓要絕對公平地對待“寄居的”和無助的人。    。
**寄居的。**原文來源於一個表示“寄居”、“逗留”、“居留”的動詞。此詞指的是臨時居住或者永久定居的外僑（見創12:10；19:9；47:4；賽52:4）。
18.en: **Doth execute.** Throughout history, justice has been notoriously slow and uncertain in the East, but Jehovah is not only impartial but also swift to act. In Ex. 22:21, 22 God enjoins His people to act with absolute impartiality toward the “stranger” and the helpless.

20.zh:
你要敬畏耶和華─你的神，事奉他，專靠他，也要指著他的名起誓。

**專靠。**原文所表達的是對任何事物儘可能牢固地連接或附著。此詞用來指丈夫和妻子成為一體的結合（創2:24），以及身體組織裡的疾病（申28:21,60）。
20.en: **Cleave.** From a verb expressive of the strongest possible attachment, or clinging to anything. It is used of a man and wife becoming one flesh (Gen. 2:24), and of disease within the bodily tissues (Deut. 28:21, 60).

21.zh:
他是你所讚美的，是你的神，為你做了那大而可畏的事，是你親眼所看見的。

參耶17:14中所用有關醫治的話語。
21.en: **Thy praise.** Compare the words in Jer. 17:14 used in connection with healing.

22.zh:
你的列祖七十人下埃及；現在耶和華─你的神使你如同天上的星那樣多。

**如同天上的星。**人口如此迅速的增長只能歸功於上帝的祝福。摩西在這裡重複了上帝對亞伯拉罕的應許（創15:5；參出12:37；民26:51, 62）。
22.en: **As the stars of heaven.** Such an increase in population could have been due only to the blessing of God. Moses here echoes the promise to Abraham (Gen. 15:5; cf. Ex. 12:37; Num. 26:51, 62).

10.19: **Stranger.** From a noun derived from the verb “to sojourn,” “to tarry,” “to abide.” A better translation would be “sojourner.” The term refers to aliens as temporary residents or as permanent settlers (see Gen. 12:10; 19:9; 47:4; Isa 52:4).

12.en: **The sabbath day.** See on Ex. 20:8–11. The fourth commandment has a natural basis reaching back to creation (Gen. 2:1–3); it also has a moral basis in the Creator-creature relationship. The primary purpose of the Sabbath as an institution is to safeguard that relationship. As physical health calls for a day of rest each week, so spiritual health requires the Sabbath for exercising the mind and heart in quest of God, that we may “feel after him, and find him” (Acts 17:27).
12.zh:
當照耶和華─你神所吩咐的守安息日為聖日。

**安息日。**見出20:8-11的註釋。第四條誡命是使人回想到創造的自然依據（創2:1-3），也是建立造物主與受造物之關係的道德依據。安息日作為一種制度其主要目的就是要維護這種關係。正如身體的健康要求人每週要休息一天，屬靈的健康也需要安息日，為的是要運用我們的思想和心靈來尋找上帝，使我們可以“揣摩而得”（徒17:27）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先知與君王》182。

15.en:
**Thou wast a servant.** Every act of God on our behalf constitutes a reason why we should “remember,” that is, to reflect upon, acknowledge, and appreciate this love and beneficent care. It is God’s purpose that on the Sabbath day whatever interferes with the direct and personal fellowship between the creature and his Creator should be laid aside. The Sabbath is a day on which it is our happy privilege to become better acquainted with our Father in heaven, whom to know is life eternal (John 17:3). To know God is to love Him (see 1 John 4:8), to honor Him, and to appreciate the evidences of His paternal goodness (Rom. 1:21).
Their deliverance from Egypt constituted an additional reason why the Israelites should reverence the Sabbath, yet the very words of the fourth commandment itself point back to the origin of the Sabbath at creation (Ex. 20:8–11) as the reason for the command here to “keep the sabbath day to sanctify it.” It should be remembered that the form in which God spoke the Ten Commandments upon Sinai is that given in Ex. 20, not in Deut. 5. As its name implies, the book of Deuteronomy is a recapitulation of the various laws transmitted to Israel at Sinai, with additional explanations given by Moses in an attempt to impress the people with the importance of observing faithfully all that they had been commanded to do. If mention of the deliverance from Egypt in connection with the fourth commandment be taken as limiting its observance, in principle, to those who were thus delivered—literal Israelites—then the principles of the Ten Commandments as a whole belong to the Jews only, for both here (Deut. 5:6) and in Ex. 20:2 God presented His law as based on the fact that He had brought them forth from the land of Egypt.
As literal Israel was delivered from the bondage of Egypt, so God’s people today have been set free from the bondage of sin (Rom. 6:16–18). The Sabbath thus becomes for the Christian a memorial not only of creation but of the re-creation of the image of God in his own heart and mind (see on Deut. 5:8). The Sabbath is thus a “sign” of sanctification (Eze. 20:12)—of redemption as well as of creation.
15.zh:
你也要記念你在埃及地作過奴僕；耶和華─你神用大能的手和伸出來的膀臂將你從那裡領出來。因此，耶和華─你的神吩咐你守安息日。

上帝為我們所做的每一件事都足以成為我們“記念”的理由。所謂“記念”就是深思、承認和感激上帝的大愛和仁慈的顧念。上帝的目的是要人在安息日放下一切妨礙受造物與造物主直接和親密交往的事情。更好地與我們在天上的父相識，這乃是我們在安息日所享有的快樂特權，因為認識祂就是永生（約17:3）。認識上帝就是要愛祂（見約壹4:8）、榮耀祂、欣賞其父愛的證據（羅1:21）。
以色列人從埃及得蒙拯救構成了他們尊重安息日的另一個理由，而第四條誡命本身的話語卻將安息日的起源追溯到創造（出20:8-11），作為這裡所吩咐要“守安息日為聖日”的理由。應該記住的是，上帝在西乃山上頒佈十條誡命所採用的形式是出20章中所給予的形式，不是申5章中所給予的形式。《申命記》，顧名思義，就是概述在西乃山傳給以色列人的各種律法，以及摩西為了使百姓深刻地意識到忠心地遵守上帝一切吩咐的重要性而給予的補充解釋。如果僅以在第四條誡命中提到出埃及的拯救為由，而限定安息日的遵守在原則上只屬於那些被如此拯救的人，即屬肉體的以色列人的話，那麼十條誡命的所有原則都應該只屬於以色列人，因為在這裡（申5:6）和出20:2中，上帝都以祂領他們出埃及地的事實作為祂頒佈其律法的依據。
正如屬肉體的以色列人從埃及的奴役中被拯救出來，上帝的子民如今也從罪的奴役中得了釋放（羅6:16-18）。這樣，安息日對基督徒而言不僅是對創造的記念，而且也是對上帝形象在人思想與心靈中再造的記念（見對申5:8的註釋）。如此，安息日便成為一個成聖的“證據”（結20:12）——救贖以及創造的證據。

22.en:
**Assembly.** The word thus translated refers to the gathering together of people or of their chosen representatives. It is often translated “congregation” (Lev. 4:14, 21), and “company” (Eze. 23:46, 47).
**Two tables of stone.** Also referred to as the “tables of the covenant” (ch. 9:9, 11, 15) and the “two tables of testimony” (Ex. 31:18; 32:15; 34:29).
22.zh:
這些話是耶和華在山上，從火中、雲中、幽暗中，大聲曉諭你們全會眾的；此外並沒有添別的話。他就把這話寫在兩塊石版上，交給我了。

**會眾。**原文指百姓或其代表的集會（見利4:14,21）。又譯為“多人”（結23:46,47）。
**兩塊石版。**也被稱為“立約的版”（申9:9,11,15）和“兩塊法版”（出31:18；32:15；34:29）。

1.zh:
摩西將以色列眾人召了來，對他們說：以色列人哪，我今日曉諭你們的律例典章，你們要聽，可以學習，謹守遵行。

**律例典章。**希伯來原文的用詞與申4:1相同。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–33節）**。《先祖與先知》305-309；《給傳道人的證言》135。
1.en: **The statutes and judgments.** The same Hebrew words as given in ch. 4:1.

2.zh:
耶和華─我們的神在何烈山與我們立約。

**立約。**見出19:5-8；24:3-8。
2.en: **Made a covenant.** See Ex. 19:5–8; 24:3–8.

3.zh:
這約不是與我們列祖立的，乃是與我們今日在這裡存活之人立的。

**我們列祖。**指亞伯拉罕、以撒、雅各和十二位先祖。上帝和“列祖”之間所立的約都是針對個人的。在西乃山，上帝有史以來第一次與一個民族立約。祂要作他們的君王，他們要作祂的臣民。
3.en: **Our fathers.** That is, our forefathers, referring to Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and the 12 patriarchs. The agreements between God and the “fathers” were personal in nature. At Sinai, for the first time in history, God entered into an agreement with an entire nation. He was to be their King, and they His people.

4.zh:
耶和華在山上，從火中，面對面與你們說話─

他們就在祂的面前，但卻“沒有看見形像”（申4:12；另見出20:22）。
4.en: **Face to face.** They were in His immediate presence, yet “saw no similitude” (Deut. 4:12; see also Ex. 20:22).

5.zh:
那時我站在耶和華和你們中間，要將耶和華的話傳給你們；因為你們懼怕那火，沒有上山─說：

摩西是上帝和以色列人之間的中保（出19:10-12,17,21；加3:19）。
5.en: **Between the Lord and you.** Moses was the mediator between God and Israel (Ex. 19:10-12, 17, 21; Gal. 3:19).

8.zh:
不可為自己雕刻偶像，也不可做什麼形像，彷彿上天、下地和地底下、水中的百物。

不能用人所構思的形象來代表上帝。以任何形象來表現上帝都是對上帝的貶低（約4:24）。用物質表現上帝只能歪曲和虧損上帝的尊貴和無限的品格，從而貶低上帝。世上唯一能夠略微與上帝相似的形象就是人類被變化具有上帝形象的品格（創1:26,27；約3:3；羅8:29；林後3:18；西3:10）。
8.en: **Any graven image.** Human conceptions of form cannot be applied to God. It belittles God to represent Him by any outward form (John 4:24). Material representations of God can give only a distorted and imperfect concept of His majesty and infinite character, and therefore depreciate God. The only earthly image that can even remotely resemble God is the human character transformed into the divine likeness (Gen. 1:26, 27; John 3:3; Rom. 8:29; 2 Cor. 3:18; Col. 3:10).

10.zh:
愛我、守我誡命的，我必向他們發慈愛，直到千代。

只有那些愛上帝的人才會順從祂。不由衷的順從只不過是自以為義律法主義的嘗試，想讓上帝對自己有個好印象。而在上帝看來，這根本不是順從。若沒有順從的精意，字句（外在的形式）乃是毫無價值的。但以上帝為至愛的人，會在與祂的合作中找到最大的快樂。
10.en: **Them that love me.** Only those thatlove God can possibly obey Him. Obedience that does not come from the heart is nothing more than a legalistic attempt at self-righteousness, by which a man seeks to commend himself to God. In the sight of heaven such is not obedience at all. Without the spirit of obedience, the letter, the outward form, is worthless. But he who loves God supremely will find his greatest delight in cooperating with Him.

11.zh:
不可妄稱耶和華─你神的名；因為妄稱耶和華名的，耶和華必不以他為無罪。

**妄。**直譯為“虛”，就是虛偽地、偽善地，或以一種輕率、低俗的方式。人對待上帝的態度應當尊敬，表現在言語和行為上。
11.en: **In vain.** Literally, “to vanity,” meaning falsely, hypocritically, or in a thoughtless, common manner. Man’s attitude toward God is to be marked with reverence, and this is to be reflected in words and deeds.

16.zh:
當照耶和華─你神所吩咐的孝敬父母，使你得福，並使你的日子在耶和華─你神所賜你的地上得以長久。

**孝敬。**參使徒保羅在弗6:1-3中的教導（另見出20:12）。只有懂得孝敬和尊重父母權威的孩子才會懂得尊敬和尊重上帝。
16.en: **Honour.** Compare the instruction of the apostle Paul in Eph. 6:1–3 (see also Ex. 20:12). Only the child who learns to honor and respect the authority of his parents will learn to honor and reverence God.

25.zh:
現在這大火將要燒滅我們，我們何必冒死呢？若再聽見耶和華─我們神的聲音就必死亡。

人們已經對於上帝的尊貴有深刻的印象，並且意識到，作為罪人，他們甚至無法在祂面前存活。有罪的意識使他們為自己性命擔憂。惡人最終將選擇死亡，而不願在上帝面前存活（啟6:15-17）。
25.en: **Why should we die?** The people had been duly impressed by the majesty of God, and realized that, as sinners, they could not even live in His presence. Consciousness of sin made them fear for their lives. The wicked will eventually choose to die rather than to live in the presence of God (Rev. 6:15–17).

28.zh:
你們對我說的話，耶和華都聽見了。耶和華對我說：這百姓的話，我聽見了；他們所說的都是。

他們因上帝大能和榮耀的顯現而懷有的極度敬畏，正是上帝想要在他們的思想和心靈中生髮的態度。只有當人在上帝的眼中變得謙卑，與上帝的公義和全能相對比而意識到自己的完全有罪和無助時，上帝才能在他裡面做工並與他合作。
28.en: **They have well said.** Their profound awe at the manifestation of divine power and glory was the very attitude of mind andheart God desired to produce in them. It is only when a man becomes humble in God’s sight, when he realizes his utter sinfulness and helplessness in contrast to God’s righteousness and omnipotence, that God can work in him and with him.

29.zh:
惟願他們存這樣的心敬畏我，常遵守我的一切誡命，使他們和他們的子孫永遠得福。

**這樣的心。**即“這樣的心境”。生活只不過是“心”中或思想中之意念的放映；一個人想的是什麼，他的為人也如何（箴23:7）。上帝更關注的是激發行為的動機而不是外在的行為。如果一個人在他的“心”中定意與上帝合作——“人若有願作的心”（林後8:12）——生活就會被相應地被改變（羅12:2）。內心的順從是唯一真實的順從；惟有這樣的順從才是上帝所喜悅的。
29.en: **Such an heart.** Or, “such a frame of mind.” The life is but a projection of the thoughts of the “heart,” or mind; as a man thinks, so is he (Prov. 23:7). God is not so much concerned with the outward acts as He is with the motives that prompt the acts. If a man purposes in his “heart” to cooperate with God—“if there be first a willing mind” (2 Cor. 8:12)—the life will be transformed accordingly (Rom. 12:2). Heart obedience is the only true obedience; it alone is acceptable to God.

30.zh:
你去對他們說：你們回帳棚去吧！

這個命令批准他們離開上帝面前。以後由摩西來擔任中間人（第5節）。
30.en: **Get you.** A command given in recognition of their request to be released from the presence of God. Moses was henceforth to be the go-between (v. 5).

32.zh:
所以，你們要照耶和華─你們神所吩咐的謹守遵行，不可偏離左右。

那些與上帝立約的人應當全心全意地侍奉祂，不“偏離”隨從自己的傾向（見申17:11,20；28:14）。
32.en: **Not turn aside.** Those who enter into the covenant relationship are expected to serve Him with an undivided heart, and not to “turn aside” to follow their own inclinations (see chs. 17:11, 20; 28:14).

33.zh:
耶和華─你們神所吩咐你們行的，你們都要去行，使你們可以存活得福，並使你們的日子在所要承受的地上得以長久。

上帝的祝福是以順從祂的命令為條件的，這不是憑著其專制的天意，而是因為與永恆的原則合作自然會使生命“長久”。另外，對應許之地的佔領是以他們不斷的忠誠為條件的。立約的條款是他們對迦南地所有權的唯一依據。他們若違犯其中的要求，就將喪失對那地的所有權。
33.en: **Prolong your days.** The blessing of God is conditional upon obedience to His precepts, not by His arbitrary decree, but because cooperation with eternal principles naturally tends to “prolong” life. Furthermore, occupation of the Promised Land was conditional upon their continued loyalty. Their right to Canaan was based exclusively on the provisions of the covenant. Should they violate its requirements, they would forfeit their right to that land.

21.en:
**Men of his city.** The young man was incorrigible, yet the carrying out of so severe a penalty was not left to the father’s judgment; it was the solemn responsibility of the men of the city (see chs. 13:10; 17:5; 22:24). To discipline with severity was within the province of the parent (Prov. 19:18), but not the carrying out of the death penalty. For other crimes that merited the death penalty, see Ex. 21:15, 17; Lev. 20:2, 27; cf. Joshua 7:25.
**Put evil away.** See on ch. 19:20.
21.zh:
本城的眾人就要用石頭將他打死。這樣，就把那惡從你們中間除掉，以色列眾人都要聽見害怕。

這個年輕人雖然不可救藥，但對如此嚴厲之刑罰的施行卻不是父親所能決定的；這是本城眾人的莊嚴職責（見申13:10；17:5；22:24）。對兒女嚴加管教是在父母權限之內的事（箴19:18），但執行死刑卻不在其權限之內。對於其他應受死刑的罪行，見出21:15,17；利20:2,27；參書7:25。
**把那惡……除掉。**見申19:20的註釋。

19.en:
**Lay hold.** Literally, “to hold with firmness,” as a sword (Eze. 30:21).
**Elders.** See on chs. 16:18; 19:12.
**The gate.** See on Gen. 19:1.
19.zh:
父母就要抓住他，將他帶到本地的城門、本城的長老那裡，

**抓住。**直譯為“緊握”，如握刀劍（結30:21）。
**長老。**見申16:18；19:12註釋。
**城門。**見創19:1註釋。

18.en:
**Stubborn and rebellious.** “Stubborn” is from a verb meaning “to be rebellious,” “resentful,” “sullen.” Jewish commentators generally refer this to sons who manifested sullen resentment toward God’s requirements and refused to carry them out. “Rebellious” the Jews applied to one who did the things he was forbidden to do, particularly in relation to parents (see Ps. 78:8; Jer. 5:23).
**Or … of his mother.** Both parents were to be equally honored; both were to be dutifully obeyed.
**Chastened.** That is, “disciplined,” “corrected,” “admonished,” often referring to corporal punishment (see Deut. 8:5; Prov. 19:18; 29:17).
18.zh:
人若有頑梗悖逆的兒子，不聽從父母的話，他們雖懲治他，他仍不聽從，

“頑梗”一詞源於表示“造反”、“怨恨”、“陰沉”的動詞。猶太教註釋家通常以此來指那些對上帝的要求顯示陰沉怨恨並拒絕遵行的兒子。猶太人用“悖逆”來指做不許做之事的人，特別是做父母所禁止之事（見詩78:8；耶5:23）。
**母的話。**父母應受到同等的尊敬；都應被忠實地順從。
**懲治。**就是“管教”、“糾正”、“勸告”，通常指體罰（見申8:5；箴19:18；29:17）。

20.en:
**Stubborn.** See on v. 18.
**Glutton.** See the same expression in Prov. 23:20–22. “Glutton” is better translated, “wastrel,” “riotous eater.” This word implies the idea of being unreasonably lavish, of squandering one’s health and wealth.
20.zh:
對長老說：我們這兒子頑梗悖逆，不聽從我們的話，是貪食好酒的人。

**頑梗。**見第18節註釋。
**貪食……的人。**見箴23:20-22中的相同說法。對“貪食的人”更好的譯法是“無用的人”、“暴食的人”。此詞所暗示的是不合理地浪費，就是糟蹋自身健康和財富的意思。

1.zh:
在耶和華─你神所賜你為業的地上，若遇見被殺的人倒在田野，不知道是誰殺的，

類似的說法見申17:2；24:7。上帝總是強調人類生命和人身權利的神聖性（見創9:5,6註釋）。
1.en: **Found slain.** For a similar expression in respect to other circumstances, see chs. 17:2; 24:7. God has always emphasized the sacredness of human life and of personal rights (see on Gen. 9:5, 6).

2.zh:
長老和審判官就要出去，從被殺的人那裡量起，直量到四圍的城邑，

大概指發現屍體之地附近村鎮中的長老和審判官（申16:18；19:12）。
2.en: **Elders.** Presumably the elders and judges of the villages in the vicinity of the place where the body was found chs. 16:18; 19:12).

3.zh:
看哪城離被殺的人最近，那城的長老就要從牛群中取一隻未曾耕地、未曾負軛的母牛犢，

**最近。**離屍體最近之城的長老將負責履行必要的安葬儀式。人們可能推測殺人犯是來自附近地區的人。
**母牛犢。**沒有說明年齡，但猶太教註釋家稱要二歲。其他地方則要求一隻三歲（創15:9）。
**未曾耕地。**就是：沒有被當作耕畜使用過（見民19:2）。
3.en:
**Next unto.** The elders of the city nearest to the body would be held responsible for the performance of the necessary last rites. It may have been presumed that the slayer was a person from the immediate vicinity.
**Heifer.** The age is not given, though Jewish commentators give two years as the age required. In other circumstances a heifer of three years is specified (Gen. 15:9).
**Wrought with.** That is, not been worked as a draft animal (see Num. 19:2).

4.zh:
把母牛犢牽到流水、未曾耕種的山谷去，在谷中打折母牛犢的頸項。

直譯為“流水不絕的山谷”。本節中所強調的是不斷的流水，而不是大小或表面的狀況。
**耕種。**指未曾耕種過的地方（見創45:6的註釋）。
**打折。**直譯為“折斷”。註釋家們把母牛犢看作兇手的替身。在牲畜年齡的幼小方面和未曾用於普通勞作方面，一定有儀文象徵的因素。
4.en:
**Rough valley.** Literally, “a valley of never-failing water.” The emphasis in the verse here is on the constant flowing water, and not the size or the condition of the surface.
**Eared.** Better, “plowed,” referring to an uncultivated spot (see on Gen. 45:6).
**Strike off.** Literally, “break.” Commentators have seen in the heifer a substitute for the murderer. There is a certain ritualistic element, in that the animal is young and has not been used in common labor.

5.zh:
祭司利未的子孫要近前來；因為耶和華─你的神揀選了他們事奉他，奉耶和華的名祝福，所有爭訟毆打的事都要憑他們判斷。

**祭司。**見申17:9；18:1。住在最近的利未人城中的祭司要到場，以確保一切要求都按照原先所吩咐的執行了。因為所有這樣的案件都要“憑他們”，直譯為“憑他們的口”判斷。利未人的權力影響深遠。他們在一切重大的決定中都有一席之地。在這裡，他們的在場確認了將殺人的責任歸與發現屍體的地區。
5.en: **Priests.** See chs. 17:9; 18:1. The priests of the nearest Levitical city would be present to see that the requirements were carried out in harmony with what had been commanded, for “by their word,” literally, “upon their mouth,” all such cases were to be settled. The authority of the Levites was far reaching. They had a voice in every important decision. In this case their presence gave validity to the placing of the burden of the murder on the district in which the body was found.

6.zh:
那城的眾長老，就是離被殺的人最近的，要在那山谷中，在所打折頸項的母牛犢以上洗手，

**洗手。**他們藉著從山谷的小河中取水，表明他們以及他們所代表之城的無辜。參詩篇作者的話語（詩26:6；73:13），以及彼拉多在審判基督時的作法（太27:24）。
**在……母牛犢以上。**既然母牛犢代表了未知的殺人犯，，那麼這一舉動就象徵著將罪加在它身上。
**打折頸項。**見第4節的註釋。
6.en:
**Wash their hands.** Taking water from the brook of the valley, they thus protested their innocence and that of the city they represented. Compare the words of the psalmist (Ps. 26:6; 73:13), and the action of Pilate at the trial of Christ (Matt. 27:24).
**Over the heifer.** If the heifer represented the unknown slayer, as seems to have been the case, then this act was symbolic of the placing of the guilt upon him.
**Beheaded.** Literally, “whose neck was broken” (see on v. 4).

7.zh:
禱告（原文作回答）說：我們的手未曾流這人的血；我們的眼也未曾看見這事。

**回答。**這是儀文意義上的回答（申27:14）。他們做了鄭重的宣告，符合其聖職的權威。
7.en: **Shall answer.** In a ceremonial sense (ch. 27:14). They made a solemn declaration, in keeping with the authority of their holy office.

8.zh:
耶和華啊，求你赦免你所救贖的以色列民，不要使流無辜血的罪歸在你的百姓以色列中間。這樣，流血的罪必得赦免。

**求你赦免。**原文的意思可能是“遮掩”。阿拉伯語該詞根的意思就是“遮掩”、“隱藏”。通常的譯法是“贖罪”（出30:10；利4:20,26,31,35；5:6,10,13,18等）。源於相同詞根的名詞被譯為“施恩座”（出25:17-22）。其含義就是一個用於保護的遮蓋物。
**所救贖的。**直譯為“購買的”、“付了錢的”。有時被譯為“救贖”（伯33:28；詩55:18；69:18；78:42；119:134）和“救”（撒上14:45）。
**不要使……歸在。**這可能暗示著附近的百姓有部分地責任，或許是因為他們沒有使通往他們城的道路達到應有的安全。
8.en:
**Be merciful.** The word thus translated probably means “to cover.” The RSV has “forgive.” The same root in Arabic means “to cover,” “to hide.” The usual translation is “make an atonement” (Ex. 30:10; Lev. 4:20, 26, 31, 35; 5:6, 10, 13, 18; etc.). The noun from the same root is translated “mercy seat” (Ex. 25:17–22). The idea is that a covering, for protection.
**Redeemed.** Literally, “purchased,” “paid the price for.” It is sometimes translated “deliver” (Job 33:28; Ps. 55:18; 69:18; 78:42; 119:134), and “rescue” (1 Sam. 14:45).
**Lay not.** Literally, “do not permit to remain.” It may possibly be implied that the people of the vicinity were held guilty, in part, perhaps because they had not made the roads leading to their city as safe as they should have been.
**So shalt thou put away.** The Hebrew is emphatic: “and thou, shalt burn out,” meaning to “utterly root out,” or “consume.”

9.zh:
你行耶和華眼中看為正的事，就可以從你們中間除掉流無辜血的罪。

希伯來原文是強調性的，“你，要燒盡”，意思就是“徹底根除”或“除盡”。

10.zh:
你出去與仇敵爭戰的時候，耶和華─你的神將他們交在你手中，你就擄了他們去。

由於迦南人應被全部消滅，所以這裡可能泛指將來與周圍列國的衝突（見申20:13,14,16註釋）。
10.en: **Taken them captive.** Inasmuch as the Canaanites were to be wiped out, it is possible that the reference here is a general one referring to future conflicts with the surrounding nations (see on ch. 20:13, 14, 16).

11.zh:
若在被擄的人中見有美貌的女子，戀慕他，要娶他為妻，

沒有說明她是否已婚，但是如果所有的男人都已殺盡（申20:13），她不是未婚就是寡婦。
11.en: **A beautiful woman.** Nothing is said as to whether she was married, but if all the males were slain ( ch. 20:13), she would be either unmarried or a widow.

12.zh:
就可以領他到你家裡去；他便要剃頭髮，修指甲，

**到你家裡去。**這樣做當然比暗地裡將她藏在別處要體面得多。
**她便要剃頭髮。**可能是出於悲傷；也有可能是為了潔淨，正如有些註釋家所認為的。據說東方的一些寡婦在為她們已故的丈夫哀悼一年結束時行一種類似的儀式。
12.en:
**To thine house.** Literally, “to the midst of thy household,” certainly a more honorable procedure than to keep her secretly elsewhere.
**Shave her head.** Probably in mourning; or for purification, as some commentators think. Some widows in the East are said to perform a similar type of ritual at the end of a year of mourning for their deceased husbands.

13.zh:
脫去被擄時所穿的衣服，住在你家裡哀哭父母一個整月，然後可以與他同房。你作他的丈夫，他作你的妻子。

**在你家裡。**要使她擺脫公眾的目光，隱居一個月（見創38:11）。
**一個整月。**參為亞倫和摩西哀悼的時期（民20:29；申34:8）。這會給她一個調整的時間，使她適應新環境。
**妻子。**上帝顯然是想阻止不正當的關係，並且鼓勵合法的婚姻。就連一個被俘的女子也不應成為男人情慾的玩物；但如果她樂意與上帝的子民和睦相處的話，就應得到一種受人尊敬的身份。
13.en:
**In thine house.** She was to be withdrawn from public gaze, and remain in retirement for one month (see Gen. 38:11).
**A full month.** Compare with the period of mourning for Aaron and Moses (Num. 20:29; Deut. 34:8). This would give her time to adjust herself to her new environment.
**Wife.** It is apparent that God intended to discourage illicit relations, and to encourage lawful marriage. Even a captive woman was not to be made the plaything of a man’s passions, but if willing to live in harmony with God’s people, she was to be given an honorable status.

14.zh:
後來你若不喜悅他，就要由他隨意出去，決不可為錢賣他，也不可當婢女待他，因為你玷汙了他。

**由她隨意。**直譯為“依照她的心意”，就是，無論她想去哪裡。作為她自己的主人，她有決定自己前途的自由。
**不可為錢賣她。**參丈夫想要休掉自己所娶希伯來婢女的情形（出21:8）。
**不可當婢女待她。**直譯為“不虐待”，就是強迫她為奴。
14.en:
**Whither she will.** Literally, “according to her soul,” that is, wherever she desired. She was to be free to determine her own future, as mistress of her own person.
**Not sell her.** Compare the status of the married Hebrew slave whom the husband wished to divorce (Ex. 21:8).
**Not make merchandise.** Literally, “not deal tyrannically,” that is, to force her to become a slave.

15.zh:
人若有二妻，一為所愛，一為所惡，所愛的、所惡的都給他生了兒子，但長子是所惡之妻生的。

**所惡的。**“惡”字在這裡暗示對對方的性厭煩（撒下13:15）。就如雅各和利亞（見創29:16,30,31）。在這種情況下，丈夫對受寵的妻子所生之子女的喜愛很可能會明顯得多。
15.en: **The hated.** The word “hated” in such cases implies sexual aversion toward (2 Sam. 13:15). This was the case with Jacob and Leah (see Gen. 29:16, 30, 31). It is not unlikely that in such case the husband’s affection for the children of the favored wife would be very much more marked.

16.zh:
到了把產業分給兒子承受的時候，不可將所愛之妻生的兒子立為長子，在所惡之妻生的兒子以上，

**給兒子承受。**請注意這裡只提到了兒子，而不是女兒，因為後者不享有雙份的產業。猶太教遺傳認為只有在父親去世之前出生的兒子才有這種特權。遺腹子不享有雙份的產業。
**不可將……立為。**這是相當於現代的執行遺囑（見創24:36；25:5）。
16.en:
**Sons to inherit.** Note that only sons are spoken of, not daughters, for the latter were not entitled to a double portion. Jewish tradition is that only sons born before the death of the father were so privileged. A posthumous son was not entitled to a double portion.
**He may not make.** This is equivalent to the modern execution of a will (see Gen. 24:36; 25:5).

17.zh:
卻要認所惡之妻生的兒子為長子，將產業多加一分給他；因這兒子是他力量強壯的時候生的，長子的名分本當歸他。

**認。**不論其個人感情和偏愛如何。
**多加一份。**直譯為“兩口”，就是兩份。如果一個人有五個兒子，那麼他的產業就要被分成六份，長子得兩份（見創48:22；王下2:9）。
**這兒子是他力量最強壯的時候生的。**就是：他力量的初熟之果（見創49:1-3；另見詩78:51；105:36）。
17.en:
**Acknowledge.** Despite his personal feelings and predilections.
**Double portion.** Literally, “the mouth of two,” that is, two portions. If a man had five sons the inheritance would be divided into six portions, the eldest son receiving two (see Gen. 48:22; 2 Kings 2:9).
**The beginning.** That is, the first fruits of his strength (see Gen. 49:1–3; also (Ps. 78:51; 105:36).

22.zh:
人若犯該死的罪，被治死了，你將他掛在木頭上，

**將他掛在。**絞刑在聖經的記錄中並不少見（創40:22；撒下21:12；斯7:10；9:14）。猶太教註釋家認為是被告先被治死，然後才將屍體掛在樹上。
22.en: **Hang him.** Hanging is not infrequently recorded in the Bible (Gen. 40:22; 2 Sam. 21:12; Esther 7:10; 9:14). Jewish commentators maintain that the accused was put to death, and then the dead body hanged on a tree.

23.zh:
他的屍首不可留在木頭上過夜，必要當日將他葬埋，免得玷汙了耶和華─你神所賜你為業之地。因為被掛的人是在神面前受咒詛的。

**不可留在木頭上過夜。**見書8:29；10:27。
**受咒詛的。**“受咒詛”一詞的詞根也表示“卑劣的”、“卑鄙的”、“蒙羞的”。參使徒保羅在加3:10-14中的論證。
**免得玷汙了……地。**地因死刑犯屍體的暴露而受玷汙。被掛的罪犯被認為是處在上帝的詛咒之下，他的屍體不應暴露在光天化日。耶穌曾被祂自己的百姓定罪，當作罪人中的罪魁，並處在耶和華的詛咒之下（太27:43；參賽53:4）。
23.en:
**Not remain all night.** See Joshua 8:29; 10:27.
**Accursed.** The root translated “accursed” means also to be “despicable,” “contemptible,” “dishonored.” Compare the argument of the apostle Paul in Gal. 3:10–14.
**Land be not defiled.** The land was conceived of as being defiled by the exposure of the bodies of criminals who had suffered the extreme penalty. The criminal who was hanged was thought of as being under God’s ban, and his body was not to remain in the public gaze. Jesus was condemned by His own people as one of the worst of criminals, and as under Jehovah’s curse (Matt. 27:43; cf. Isa. 53:4).

5.en: **Not wear.** This probably refers to the heathen custom—quite common in some lands today—of a simulated change of sex for immoral purposes, men wearing women’s clothes, aping their manners, and offering their bodies for immoral purposes. The word here translated “that which pertaineth” is used of many articles other than clothing, such as “jewels” (Gen. 24:53), “weapons” (Gen. 27:3), “stuff” (Gen. 31:37), “armour” (1 Sam. 14:1, 6), “bag” (1 Sam. 17:40), “furniture” (Nahum 2:9). God made man male and female, and the distinction thus ordained is to be honored and obeyed. The desire to minimize this distinction grows from low ideals and contributes to immorality.
5.zh:
婦女不可穿戴男子所穿戴的，男子也不可穿婦女的衣服，因為這樣行都是耶和華─你神所憎惡的。

**不可穿戴。**這可能是指為不道德的目的而假裝變性的異教習俗。這在現今的一些國家中非常普遍，就是男人穿女人的衣服，模仿她們的樣子，併為不道德的目的而提供他們的身體。“所穿戴的”一詞的原文還用來指除了衣服以外的許多物品，如“珠寶”（創24:53）、“器械”（創27:3）、“傢俱”（創31:37）、“兵器”（撒上14:1,6）、“袋”（撒上17:40）、“寶器”（鴻2:9）。上帝造人乃是造男造女，應當尊重和順從這樣的區別。縮少這種區別的慾望發自低下的思想，造成了淫蕩之風。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《證言》卷一421，457，459。

1.zh:
你若看見弟兄的牛或羊失迷了路，不可佯為不見，總要把他牽回來交給你的弟兄。

這裡嚴肅指出對於朋友或鄰居的福利所應負的責任。這種責任甚至延伸到對仇敵的福利上（出23:4）。“失迷了路”的譯法對希伯來原文的含義表達得不夠充分，原文的意思是“被趕走了”。該詞還譯為“舉[斧子]”（申20:19）、“趕散”（申30:4）、“勾引”（申30:17）、“趕出淨盡”（伯6:13）。如果牲畜在這裡只是迷了路，那麼將它們牽回來就只需要費一些時間和精力而已。但是這節經文也暗示著它們有時是被賊趕走的。在這種情形下，就會有一些個人風險，甚至可能要冒生命的危險。
**佯為不見。**參賽58:7。
**把它牽回來。**僅僅告知主人是不夠的，要盡力歸還他的財產。參良善的撒瑪利亞人的比喻（路10:30-35）。
1.en:
**Thy brother’s ox.** Responsibility for the welfare of a friend or neighbor was strictly enjoined, and extended even to one’s enemies (Ex. 23:4). The KJV translation, “go astray,” is inadequate to the thought of the Hebrew word, which means “being driven away.” The same word is also rendered “forcing” (Deut. 20:19), “driven out” (Deut. 30:4), “drawn away” (Deut. 30:17), “driven quite” (Job 6:13). If the cattle in this instance had merely been going astray, to bring them back would have been nothing more than a matter of time and effort. But the text suggests also that in some instances they were being driven off by thieves. In such cases there was an element of personal risk, possibly involving in some instances the loss of life.
**Hide thyself.** Compare Isa. 58:7.
**Bring them again.** It was not enough to inform the owner, but effort was to be put forth to restore his property. Compare the parable of the good Samaritan (Luke 10:30–35).

2.zh:
你弟兄若離你遠，或是你不認識他，就要牽到你家去，留在你那裡，等你弟兄來尋找就還給他。

這可能包括照看受傷的牲畜，當然也包括為它們提供圈棚和飼養，直到保留牲畜的人能夠找到合法的物主為止。
2.en: **Bring it.** This might involve the care of wounded animals, and certainly their shelter and feeding, until the one holding the cattle would be able to locate the rightful owner.

3.zh:
你的弟兄無論失落什麼，或是驢，或是衣服，你若遇見，都要這樣行，不可佯為不見。

第1,2節所規定的律例也適用於人撿到的任何東西。愛鄰舍的基本原則也包括關心他所喜愛之任何事物。參耶穌這方面的教訓（太5:42-48）。
3.en: **All lost thing.** The same law as in v. 1, 2 was applicable to anything a man might find. The basic principle of love for one’s neighbor included an interest in whatever affected him. Compare the teaching of Jesus on this point (Matt. 5:42–48).

4.zh:
你若看見弟兄的牛或驢跌倒在路上，不可佯為不見，總要幫助他拉起來。

**佯為不見。**就是在被人看到他在遇難牲畜的旁邊之前遛走（見路10:31,32）。
**總要幫助。**見出23:4,5。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《論福利工作》48。
4.en:
**Hide thyself.** That is, slip away before he should be observed in the vicinity of the animals in distress (see Luke 10:31, 32).
**Surely help.** Compare Ex. 23:4, 5.

6.zh:
你若路上遇見鳥窩，或在樹上或在地上，裡頭有雛或有蛋，母鳥伏在雛上或在蛋上，你不可連母帶雛一併取去。

**連母帶雛。**這裡大概是指任何可以食用的潔淨鳥類。上帝體諒低級等動物的感受和生命（太10:29；路12:6），當我們也如此行時，上帝會感到高興並受到尊榮（見利22:27註釋）。以殘害上帝所受造之物為樂，造成它們痛苦，或者不必要地騷擾它們，都是與基督徒的身份不相稱的，也上帝所不喜悅的。
6.en: **The dam with the young.** Or, “the mother with the young.” Presumably, the reference here is to any clean bird that may be eaten. God is considerate of the feeling and lives of His lesser creatures (Matt. 10:29; Luke 12:6), and is pleased and honored when we are also (see on Lev. 22:27). Taking the lives of any of God’s creatures in sport, or annoying them, or disturbing them unnecessarily, is unworthy of a Christian and is displeasing to God.

7.zh:
總要放母，只可取雛，這樣你就可以享福，日子得以長久。

**總要放母。**為了保護物種，保存鳥類的生命。現代的狩獵規則基本上體現了這裡所提出的原則。
7.en: **Let the dam go.** This would protect the species, ensuring the preservation of bird life. Modern game laws generally reflect the principle here set forth.

8.zh:
你若建造房屋，要在房上的四圍安欄杆，免得有人從房上掉下來，流血的罪就歸於你家。

**欄杆。**屋子的平頂應有一個矮欄杆，防止粗心的人跌到下面的街道上。屋頂常被用作晾曬各種穀物和水果，或孩子們玩耍，或傍晚乘涼的地方（見書2:6；撒下11:2；18:24；尼8:16；太10:27；徒10:9）。
8.en: **A battlement.** The flat roof of a house was to have a low parapet to protect an unwary person from falling to the street below. The roof was often used as a place for the drying of various grains and fruits, for children, and for relaxation in the cool of the evening (see Joshua 2:6; 2 Sam. 11:2; 18:24; Neh. 8:16; Matt. 10:27; Acts 10:9).

9.zh:
不可把兩樣種子種在你的葡萄園裡，免得你撒種所結的和葡萄園的果子都要充公。

**兩樣種子。**上帝對他們的田地也有一個類似的吩咐（利19:19）。這個律例可能是為了確保種子的質量。雜交很容易產生次等的變種，而上帝則想保護祂的子民避免這些事。當時選擇性的科學雜交尚不為人知。
**都要充公 。**直譯為“成為聖潔”、“分別為聖”（出29:21,37；撒上21:5；代下26:18；31:6；拉3:5），用來指祭司和利未人、祭物、祭壇、屬上帝的人、教會等。此詞及其派生的名詞在舊約中共出現589次。這裡指葡萄園的出產要成為“聖”，就是“被沒收到聖所”，不得被原主所用，既不可賣掉也不可送人。原主不得從中獲得任何利益。
9.en:
**Divers seeds.** A similar injunction had been given with respect to their fields (Lev. 19:19). This law was probably given to ensure the preservation of seed quality. Inferior varieties could easily result from crossbreeding, and against these God sought to protect His people. Scientific, selective crossbreeding was unknown.
**Be defiled.** Literally, “be holy,” “be sacred,” “be hallowed,” “be consecrated” (Ex. 29:21, 37; 1 Sam. 21:5; 2 Chron. 26:18; 31:6; Ezra 3:5). This term was applied to the priests and Levites, the sacrifices, the altar, to God’s person, the church, etc. Of the 589 times this word and its derivative noun form appear in the OT, this is the only instance where it is translated “be defiled.” The translators apparently misunderstood the meaning. The meaning here is that the product of the vineyard would become “holy,” that is, “forfeited to the sanctuary” (RSV). It was not to be used by the owner, and might neither be sold nor given away. He was not to benefit from it in any way.

10.zh:
不可並用牛、驢耕地。

**牛、驢。**牛是“潔淨的”，而驢是“不潔淨的”。但這可能是一條仁慈的指示，因為這兩種牲畜的大小和力量都不相稱。現今在東方，駱駝和驢有時同負一軛。
10.en: **An ox and an ass.** The ox was a “clean” animal, and the ass “unclean.” However, this charge was probably a humane one, inasmuch as in size and strength the animals are unequal. In the East today camels and asses are sometimes yoked together.

11.zh:
不可穿羊毛、細麻兩樣攙雜料做的衣服。

見利19:19註釋；又見結44:17,19；啟19:8。
11.en: **Woollen and linen.** See on Lev. 19:19; see also Eze. 44:17, 19; Rev. 19:8.

12.zh:
你要在所披的外衣上四圍做繸子。

繸子的原文在舊約別處只用過一次（王上7:17，“網子”）。該詞源於動詞“變大”、“擰”，與民15:37-41中譯為“繸子”的原文不是同一個詞。
**四圍。**或“四角”（參民15:38的“邊”，希伯來原文相同）。“外衣”源於動詞“遮蓋”，可能是一個象斗篷一樣的長方形外袍，至今仍有巴勒斯坦的農民穿著。窮人在晚上用它作為被子。古時候，猶太人公開地在他們的外袍上裝飾“繸子”。由於在受迫害時容易被認出來，他們便將繸子挪到了內衣上。後來他們將繸子，或捻成的繩索縫在禱告時穿戴的小斗篷上。上帝子民的服飾應當是與眾不同的。他們不可隨周圍人群的時尚。
12.en:
**Fringes.** More exactly, “tassels.” The Hebrew word thus translated is used but once more in the OT (1 Kings 7:17, “wreaths”). It is from the verb “to become great,” “to twist,” and is not the same word as that rendered “fringes” in Num. 15:37–41.
**The four quarters.** Or, “the four corners” (RSV; cf. Num. 15:38, “borders,” the same word in Hebrew). The “vesture,” from the verb “to cover,” was probably a rectangular outer garment resembling a cloak, still worn by the peasants of Palestine. The poor used it for a cover at night. Anciently, the Jews wore “tassels” openly on their outer garment. As this readily identified them in times of persecution, they transferred the tassels to the inner garment. Later they adopted the custom of wearing the tassels, or twisted cords, only on the small mantle worn at prayers. The dress of God’s people was to be distinctive. They were not to follow the fashions of the people among whom they lived.

13.zh:
人若娶妻，與他同房之後恨惡他，

**恨惡她。**就是不喜歡她。他顯然不是真正愛她，而是因肉體的吸引而與她結合的。肉體的吸引是建立家庭的最不穩定的基礎。心靈的合一才是夫妻之間唯一可靠和永久的結合。
13.en: **Hate her.** That is, find that he dislikes her. Apparently he had married the woman, not with any real love for her, but primarily from his physical attraction to her. Physical attraction is a most precarious basis upon which to establish a home. Unity of spirit is the only sure and abiding bond between husband and wife.

14.zh:
信口說他，將醜名加在他身上，說：我娶了這女子，與他同房，見他沒有貞潔的憑據；

**信口說。**直譯為“不負責任地指控”。只有卑鄙自私的男人才會為了獲得拋棄她的“合法”權利而誣告他的妻子，敗壞她的名聲。這樣的人應該受到公眾的懲罰（第18節）。關於上帝對誣告的態度，見民14:36,37；申19:18,19。
**見她沒有貞潔的憑據。**即不是處女。。該詞還見諸本章15,17,20節（另見利21:13等）。
14.en:
