**Flee thither.** The devout Christian will certainly think of the sinner’s privilege of fleeing to Christ. As the gates of the cities of refuge were never to be closed to one who sought entrance, so Christ never refuses one who comes to Him contrite and repentant (Ps. 51:17; Isa. 57:15).

4.zh:
誤殺人的逃到那裡可以存活，定例乃是這樣：凡素無仇恨，無心殺了人的，

**無心。**就是“不故意地”，直譯為“無知地”（申4:42；書20:3,5）。
**無仇恨。**涉案人不是故意的（見民35:23）。要誤殺人之人的性命就等於是流無辜人的血。
4.en:
**Ignorantly.** That is, “unintentionally,” literally, “without knowledge” (Deut. 4:42; Joshua 20:3, 5).
**Hated not.** The man responsible had acted unintentionally (see Num. 35:23). To require the life of such an unintentional slayer would be to shed innocent blood.

5.zh:
就如人與鄰舍同入樹林砍伐樹木，手拿斧子一砍，本想砍下樹木，不料，斧頭脫了把，飛落在鄰捨身上，以致於死，這人逃到那些城的一座城，就可以存活，

可能是山坡上的叢林。根據埃及文獻計栽，迦南古時林木繁茂。這是一種過失殺人案（見民35:22）。此人是在從事合法的職業，其同伴的死純屬意外。
**把。**有人認為這指的是斧頭從樹上飛了出去。但實際上是人在砍樹的過程中，斧頭從手柄上脫落。
**存活。**詳見書20:1-4。這裡形象地寓示罪人在基督耶穌裡所能找到的安全。沾滿血跡的人在耶穌裡得洗淨（約壹1:7）。“那些在基督耶穌裡的，就不定罪了”（羅8:1），因為他們“既因信稱義，就藉著我們的主耶穌基督，得與上帝相和”（羅5:1）。
5.en:
**The wood.** Probably hillside thickets. According to Egyptian records Canaan was heavily wooded during patriarchal times. This is a case of unpremeditated homicide (see Num. 35:22). The man was engaged in a lawful pursuit, and the death of his companion was altogether accidental.
**Fetcheth a stroke.** “Swings the axe” (RSV).
**The helve.** Some think this means that the ax flew off from the tree, since the word for tree is the same as the one here translated “helve.” But it is perhaps better to understand it as given in the KJV, that the axhead flew off the handle as the man was in the process of cutting down a tree.
**Live.** Compare Joshua 20:1–4 for additional details. This is a vivid symbolic word picture of the security the sinner may find in Christ Jesus. The bloodstained person is cleansed in Jesus (1 John 1:7). There is “no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus” (Rom. 8:1); for, “being justified by faith,” they have “peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ” (Rom. 5:1).

6.zh:
免得報血仇的，心中火熱追趕他，因路遠就追上，將他殺死；其實他不該死，因為他與被殺的素無仇恨。

**報血仇的。**該詞原文也譯為“親屬”（見得2:20註釋），和“救贖主”（伯19:25；詩19:14；78:35；賽41:14；43:14；54:5）。
**路遠。**在與中央祭壇有關的義務方面，上帝對道路的遙遠和不便表顯了同樣的關注（申12:21；14:24）。
6.en:
**The avenger.** From the same word translated “kinsman” (see on Ruth 2:20), and “redeemer” (Job 19:25; Ps. 19:14; 78:35; Isa. 41:14; 43:14; 54:5).
**The way is long.** The same concern over the length and inconvenience of the road had been shown by God in relation to duties at the central altar (chs. 12:21; 14:24).

7.zh:
所以我吩咐你說，要分定三座城。

三座城在國內不同的地區設立正是為了避免象前幾節經文所提及的不幸情況。
7.en: **Wherefore.** It was to prevent an unfortunate situation like that mentioned in the previous verses that the three cities were established in different parts of the country.

8.zh:
耶和華─你神若照他向你列祖所起的誓擴張你的境界，將所應許賜你列祖的地全然給你，

見創15:18；出23:31；申1:7。
8.en: **Enlarge.** See Gen. 15:18; Ex. 23:31; Deut. 1:7.

9.zh:
你若謹守遵行我今日所吩咐的這一切誡命，愛耶和華─你的神，常常遵行他的道，就要在這三座城之外，再添三座城，

**你若謹守。**領土擴張之應許的應驗有賴乎順從（申11:22-24）。見對亞伯拉罕的應許（創15:18）。
**再添三座城。**共有九座城，因為約旦河兩岸已各有三座城設立（第2節；申4:41-43）。但在該國以後的歷史中，從未提到這三座城。
9.en:
**If thou shalt keep.** The fulfillment of the promises of enlargement was dependent on obedience (ch. 11:22–24). Compare the promise made to Abraham (Gen. 15:18).
**Three cities more.** That would be nine in all, as three on each side of the Jordan had already been stipulated (v. 2; ch. 4:41–43). There is, however, no record of theadditional three ever having been designated in the afterhistory of the nation.

10.zh:
免得無辜之人的血流在耶和華─你神所賜你為業的地上，流血的罪就歸於你。

**無辜之人。**參申21:8；耶7:6。源於表示“使潔淨”、“使自由”的動詞詞根。引伸義為解除因罪而產生的責任。
**流血的罪就歸於你。**參撒下16:8；何12:14。歸於他們的無辜之人的血，就是那個因過失殺人，並在他自己被殺之前無法找到避難所的人。
10.en:
**Innocent.** Compare Deut. 21:8; Jer. 7:6. The word thus translated is from a verb root meaning “to be clean,” “to be free.” Inherent in it is the idea of being free from obligations resulting from guilt.
**Blood be upon thee.** Compare 2 Sam. 16:8; Hosea 12:14. The innocent blood upon them would be that of the manslayer who had killed a man accidentally, and then could not find a place of refuge before he himself was slain.

11.zh:
若有人恨他的鄰舍，埋伏著起來擊殺他，以致於死，便逃到這些城的一座城，

詳見民35:16-24。心中的仇恨會使他“埋伏著”，然後乘機“起來”，將他所憎恨的鄰舍“擊殺……以致於死”（見出21:14）。
11.en: **Hate his neighbour.** For details see Num. 35:16–24. Hatred in the heart of man causes him to “lie in wait,” then “rise up” at the opportune moment, and “smite … mortally” his neighbor whom he detests (see Ex. 21:14).

12.zh:
本城的長老就要打發人去，從那裡帶出他來，交在報血仇的手中，將他治死。

那些得到正式任命和授權的人要在這個重要的事情上採取行動。關於長老合法任命的實例，參申21:2,4,6,19。有關這些城的長老，見書20:1-6。
**交在。**如果發現他有蓄意殺人的罪，就要交給報血仇的人；否則，他就要受到保護（民35:12,24,25）。
12.en:
**The elders.** Those properly appointed and authorized were to act in this important matter. Compare ch. 21:2, 4, 6, 19, for examples of elders legally appointed. For elders of these cities see Joshua 20:1–6.
**Deliver him.** If found guilty of premeditated murder he was to be handed over to the avenger of blood; otherwise, he was to receive protection (Num. 35:12, 24, 25).

13.zh:
你眼不可顧惜他，卻要從以色列中除掉流無辜血的罪，使你可以得福。

**不可顧惜。**見第21節的註釋。
**除掉。**直譯為“剿滅”或“燒盡”，指完全的消除。
13.en:
**Not pity.** See on v. 21.
**Put away.** Literally, “consume” or “burn away,” indicating complete removal.

14.zh:
在耶和華─你神所賜你承受為業之地，不可挪移你鄰舍的地界，那是先人所定的。

**不可挪移。**直譯為：“向後挪移”以便擴張自己的領地，並使鄰舍的領地相應地變小。從遠古時代起，地界就被視為不可侵犯的。咒詛被加在那些暗中挪移地界的人身上（申27:17；另見伯24:2；箴22:28；23:10；何5:10）。
**先人。**不是指遠古時代的人，而是指那些最初分配此地並標出地界的人。
14.en:
**Not remove.** Literally, “move back,” that is, so as to enlarge one’s own piece of property, and leave one’s neighbor correspondingly less. From ancient times landmarks were considered inviolate. A curse was pronounced on the one who surreptitiously moved them (Deut. 27:17; see also Job 24:2; Prov. 22:28; 23:10; Hosea 5:10).
**They of old time.** Or, “the former ones.” Not referring to generations of past time reaching into antiquity, but to those who originally divided the land and marked out the boundaries.

15.zh:
人無論犯什麼罪，作什麼惡，不可憑一個人的口作見證，總要憑兩三個人的口作見證才可定案。

一個人不能因一個證人的見證而被定罪，不論是民事的還是刑事的指控（參申17:6；民35:30）。
15.en: **One witness.** A man could not be condemned on the testimony of one witness, in either a civil or a criminal charge (cf. Deut. 17:6; Num. 35:30).

16.zh:
若有兇惡的見證人起來，見證某人作惡，

作假見證的要被懲罰（第19節）。
16.en: **False witness.** A false witness was to be punished (v. 19).

17.zh:
這兩個爭訟的人就要站在耶和華面前，和當時的祭司，並審判官面前，

難斷的案子可以帶到在耶和華聖所門前的高級法院，訴訟各方會集在耶和華的面前（申17:8-12）。
17.en: **Before the Lord.** A difficult case could be brought to a higher court at the door of the sanctuary of the Lord, where the parties would be in the presence of Jehovah (ch. 17:8–12).

18.zh:
審判官要細細地查究，若見證人果然是作假見證的，以假見證陷害弟兄，

偽證罪是一種最可憎的罪，但許多人甚至在宣誓之後仍毫不猶豫地撒謊。如此公開違背真理的人是在得罪他自己、得罪他的對手、得罪上帝。
18.en: **False witness.** Perjury is a most heinous crime, yet many do not hesitate to lie even under oath. One who thus publicly violates truth sins against himself, his enemy, and God.

19.zh:
你們就要待他如同他想要待的弟兄。這樣，就把那惡從你們中間除掉。

作假見證的必受到他想加給被告的刑罰（見申19:21；參出23:1；詩35:11）。這是罪有應得的法則。
19.en: **As he had thought.** A false witness would have to suffer the penalty he thought to inflict upon the accused (see Deut. 19:21; cf. Ex. 23:1; Ps. 35:11). This is the law of just retribution.

20.zh:
別人聽見都要害怕，就不敢在你們中間再行這樣的惡了。

這個律例必定抑制人的自私，並且有助於培養更高的公共責任感和道德感（見申13:11；17:13）。
20.en: **Commit no more.** This law was bound to restrain selfishness and tended to bring in a higher sense of public duty and morality (see chs. 13:11; 17:13).

21.zh:
你眼不可顧惜，要以命償命，以眼還眼，以牙還牙，以手還手，以腳還腳。

**不可顧惜。**這忠告是對審判官說的，以免他們被誘惑而達不到嚴格的司法要求。
**以命償命。**詳見出21:23-25；利24:19,20。作假見證使一個無罪的人受罪的陰謀是不可寬恕的，因為這表現了作假見證者心中潛在的殺人罪（見太5:22）。他為其無辜的鄰舍所挖的陷阱將成為他自己的墳墓。
21.en:
**Not pity.** This advice is spoken to the judges, lest they be tempted to be more lenient than strict justice required.
**Life shall go.** For further details, see Ex. 21:23–25; Lev. 24:19, 20. A conspiracy to give false testimony and thereby bring an innocent man into jeopardy is unforgivable, for it represents potential murder in the heart of the false witness (see Matt. 5:22). The pit that he dug for his innocent neighbor was to be his own grave.

1.zh:
你出去與仇敵爭戰的時候，看見馬匹、車輛，並有比你多的人民，不要怕他們，因為領你出埃及地的耶和華─你神與你同在。

迦南人有大量的車輛（書11:4；士4:3）。以色列人的軍隊是由步兵組成的；他們從來沒有消除對戰車的恐懼（書17:16；士1:19；撒上13:5,6）。直到大衛的時代，他們才有屬於自己的戰車（撒下8:4）。
**不要怕。**耶和華曾將他們從埃及帶出來；祂會在所要面臨之爭戰的無常變化中與他們同在（詩20:6-8）。
**上帝與你同在。**有關在其他情形中的相同應許，見申1:30,42；7:21。參以賽亞在亞哈斯與利汛和比加發生衝突時對他所發的信息（賽7:4-14；8:8,10）。
1.en:
**Horses, and chariots.** The Canaanites had large numbers of chariots (Joshua 11:4; Judges 4:3). The army of Israel was composed of infantrymen; they never lost their fear of armed chariots (Joshua 17:16; Judges 1:19; 1 Sam. 13:5, 6). Not until David’s time did they have chariots of their own (2 Sam. 8:4).
**Be not afraid.** Jehovah had brought them out of Egypt; He would be with them in the vicissitudes of battle that lay ahead (Ps. 20:6–8).
**God is with thee.** For the same promise under other circumstances see chs. 1:30, 42; 7:21. Compare the message of Isaiah to Ahaz in his conflict with Rezin and Pekah (Isa. 7:4–14; 8:8, 10).

2.zh:
你們將要上陣的時候，祭司要到百姓面前宣告

見民31:6；代下13:12。關於約櫃被抬到戰場上，見撒上4:4,5（參撒下11:11），關於為慶祝勝利而獻給上帝的祭物，見撒上7:9；參撒上13:9-13。
2.en: **The priest shall approach.** See Num. 31:6; 2 Chron. 13:12. For the ark being taken to the field of battle, see 1 Sam. 4:4, 5 (cf. 2 Sam. 11:11), and a sacrifice being offered to God for victory in battle, see 1 Sam. 7:9; cf. 1 Sam. 13:9–13.

3.zh:
說：以色列人哪，你們當聽，你們今日將要與仇敵爭戰，不要膽怯，不要懼怕戰兢，也不要因他們驚恐；

**膽怯。**更好的譯法是，“軟弱”。關於“膽怯”一詞的其他用法，見王下22:19；詩55:21；賽1:6。
3.en: **Faint.** Better, “be soft,” “be tender,” “be weak.” For other uses of the word translated “faint” see 2 Kings 22:19; Ps. 55:21; Isa. 1:6.

4.zh:
因為耶和華─你們的神與你們同去，要為你們與仇敵爭戰，拯救你們。

參大衛的信心（撒上17:45；詩20:7）。在出徵之前常常獻祭，為要祈求祂的同在。在基督復臨前最後的大斗爭中，耶和華被描述為親自作戰的上帝（見賽13:6-14；珥3:9-21；啟16:14-16；19:11-16）。
4.en: **The Lord your God.** Compare the confidence of David (1 Sam. 17:45; Ps. 20:7). Sacrifices were often offered to God at the opening of a campaign in order to invoke His presence. In the last great struggle preliminary to the second coming of Christ, Jehovah is represented as being present in person to do battle (see Isa. 13:6–14; Joel 3:9–21; Rev. 16:14–16; 19:11–16).

5.zh:
官長也要對百姓宣告說：誰建造房屋，尚未奉獻，他可以回家去，恐怕他陣亡，別人去奉獻。

該詞還出現在出5:6,10,14,15,19；民11:16；申1:15；16:18；書1:10等中。他們是行政長官，因為以色列人的軍隊不是由職業士兵組成的。
**奉獻。**原文的動詞用來指祭壇（民7:10）以及聖所（王上8:63；代下7:5）的奉獻，但在這裡指的是私人房屋的奉獻。
**尚未用。**主人不能享用種植葡萄園後頭三年的果實（利19:23等）。在第四年，他要把果實帶到耶路撒冷，在那裡當作感謝祭吃掉（利19:24）。但從第五年起，包括第五年，果實就是他的了（利19:25）。
聘定了妻。這個例外是一種體諒之舉，以便使人不至於沒有孩子而死，為要使他的名分和利益得以延續。這個例外為期一年之久（申24:5）。第5-7節所記載的三種例外必能給國家的經濟帶來有益的影響。大大減輕戰爭給整個民族的生活所帶來的動盪不安與極度擾亂人心的影響。
**懷愛倫註釋（5–8節）**。《先祖與先知》548。
5.en:
**Officers.** The same word here translated “officers” is found in Ex. 5:6, 10, 14, 15, 19; Num. 11:16; Deut. 1:15; 16:18; Joshua 1:10; etc., and as “overseer” in Prov. 6:7. These men were civil magistrates, for the army of Israel was not a body of professional soldiers.
**Dedicated.** The verb thus translated is used of the dedication of an altar (Num. 7:10) and of the sanctuary (1 Kings 8:63; 2 Chron. 7:5), but here of a private house.
**Not yet eaten.** The owner could not lawfully eat the fruit of the vineyard for the first three years after planting (Lev. 19:23; etc.). In the fourth year he was to carry the fruit to Jerusalem and eat it there as a thank offering (Lev. 19:24). But from the fifth year, inclusive, the fruit was his (Lev. 19:25).
**Betrothed a wife.** This exemption was an act of consideration so that the man might not die without having children to perpetuate his name and interests. This exemption lasted one year (ch. 24:5). The three exemptions noted in vs. 5–7 could not fail to have a beneficial effect on the economy of the nation. They were an important alleviation of the insecurity and utterly disturbing effects of war upon the entire life of a people.

8.zh:
官長又要對百姓宣告說：誰懼怕膽怯，他可以回家去，恐怕他弟兄的心消化，和他一樣。

古以色列人覺得有必要保護軍隊免受傳染性的懦弱精神所影響。在基督徒屬靈的爭戰中也同樣需要保持高度的勇氣。勝利是藉著紀律、勇氣、忠心盡職和自我犧牲的精神而取得的（路14:26,27；加6:9）。
8.en: **Fearful and fainthearted.** It was felt necessary to protect the army from the infectious spirit of cowardice. It is equally necessary to maintain a high level of courage in the Christian warfare. Victories are gained by discipline, courage, devotion to duty, and a spirit of self-sacrifice (Luke 14:26, 27; Gal. 6:9).

9.zh:
官長對百姓宣告完了，就當派軍長率領他們。

**軍長。**指的是指揮由千人、百人、或五十人組成之部隊的軍官（見民31:14,48；撒上8:12；22:7；撒下18:1）。該詞的單數形式，用來指整個軍隊的總司令（創21:22；撒下2:8；王上16:16）。
9.en: **Captains.** Referring to officers in command of companies of thousands, hundreds, or fifties (see Num. 31:14, 48; 1 Sam. 8:12; 22:7; 2 Sam. 18:1). The singular number, captain of a “host,” is used to designate the commander in chief of the entire army (Gen. 21:22; 2 Sam. 2:8; 1 Kings 16:16).

10.zh:
你臨近一座城、要攻打的時候，先要對城裡的民宣告和睦的話。

這是投降的條款。見亞蘭的便哈達向以色列王亞哈（王上20:1-6），以及亞述王的代表向猶大王希西家（王下18:17-37）提出的談判條件。
10.en: **Proclaim peace.** Meaning terms of surrender. See offers of negotiation made by Ben-hadad of Syria to Ahab, king of Israel (1 Kings 20:1–6), and by the representative of the king of Assyria to Hezekiah, king of Judah (2 Kings 18:17–37).

11.zh:
他們若以和睦的話回答你，給你開了城，城裡所有的人都要給你效勞，服事你；

原文是一個集體名詞，指的是一個由被迫做苦工的人組成的群體（見英文RSV版）。所羅門王就曾將這樣的負擔加在百姓的身上，總共約有三萬人（王上5:13），為要派他們去黎巴嫩（王上5:14；參王上9:15,20,21；12:18；代下10:18）。在賽31:8中，該詞譯為“服苦的”。
11.en: **Tributaries.** The word thus translated is a collective noun indicating a body of forced laborers (see RSV). King Solomon placed such a levy upon the people, some 30,000 in all (1 Kings 5:13), to be sent to Lebanon (1 Kings 5:14; cf. 1 Kings 9:15, 20, 21; 12:18; 2 Chron. 10:18). In Isa. 31:8 the same word is translated “discomfited.”

12.zh:
若不肯與你和好，反要與你打仗，你就要圍困那城。

拒絕和平的條件被視為宣戰，戰爭便爆發了。
12.en: **No peace.** A rejection of the offer of peace was regarded as a declaration of war, and hostilities began.

13.zh:
耶和華─你的神把城交付你手，你就要用刀殺盡這城的男丁。

拒絕和平的條件就是表示決心繼續崇拜偶像，並行隨之而來的邪淫。如果他們拒絕接受上帝，並轉離偶像崇拜的話，這些偶像崇拜城邦之居民的道德腐敗及完全的墮落會使他們不可避免的遭受毀滅。
13.en: **Smite every male.** The rejection of the offer of peace was the expression of a determination to continue the worship of idols, with all its attendant immoralities. The moral rottenness and total depravity of the inhabitants of idolatrous cities made their destruction inevitable if they refused to accept God and turn their backs upon idolatry.

14.zh:
惟有婦女、孩子、牲畜，和城內一切的財物，你可以取為自己的掠物。耶和華─你神把你仇敵的財物賜給你，你可以吃用。

**掠物。**貴重的金屬、衣物、庫存的食物和各樣的家庭用品（見申2:35）。
14.en: **Spoil.** Precious metals, cloth, stocks of food, and all manner of household goods (see ch. 2:35).

16.zh:
但這些國民的城，耶和華─你神既賜你為業，其中凡有氣息的，一個不可存留；

**城。**特指迦南的各城。沒有必要向他們提出和平條件；上帝先前已經嚴厲禁止寬恕他們中的任何人（出23:31-33；34:11-16）。上帝給予了各樣的警戒來防止以色列人受迦南人所實行的有辱人格之偶像崇拜形式的影響。關於這些人所行之可憎惡的事，見利18:24-28；20:23。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖與先知》492。
16.en: **Cities.** Referring specifically to the cities of Canaan. No peace offer was to be made to them; God had previously given strict injunctions as to sparing any of them (Ex. 23:31–33; 34:11–16). Every precaution was taken to protect Israel from the degrading forms of idolatry practiced by the Canaanites. On the abominations of these people, see Lev. 18:24–28; 20:23.

17.zh:
只要照耶和華─你神所吩咐的將這赫人、亞摩利人、迦南人、比利洗人、希未人、耶布斯人都滅絕淨盡，

**滅絕淨盡。**直譯為“獻掉”，就是消滅掉。
**赫人。**參申7:1和書24:11，其中所列舉的是七個民族，而不是六個。這裡省略了革迦撒人。
**你上帝所吩咐的。**見申7:2；參記載在出23:31-33中的吩咐。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《基督比喻實訓》253。
17.en:
**Utterly destroy.** Literally, “dedicate,” that is, to destruction.
**Hittites.** Compare Deut. 7:1 and Joshua 24:11, where seven nations are enumerated, not six. Here, the Girgashites are omitted.
**Commanded thee.** See ch. 7:2; cf. the instructions recorded in Ex. 23:31–33.

18.zh:
免得他們教導你們學習一切可憎惡的事，就是他們向自己神所行的，以致你們得罪耶和華─你們的神。

這裡指出了採取嚴厲措施的最大理由。極大的邪惡再加上對恩慈的拒絕勢必招致審判（見申7:26；12:31）。當“亞摩利人的罪孽”滿盈時，審判就降臨了（見創15:16；王上21:26）。
**懷愛倫註釋（18–21節）**。《證言》卷四204，455。
18.en: **Abominations.** This points to the supreme reason for the severe measures taken. Great wickedness coupled with the rejection of mercy demanded judgment (see chs. 7:26; 12:31). When “the iniquity of the Amorites” was full, judgment came (see Gen. 15:16; 1 Kings 21:26).

19.zh:
你若許久圍困、攻打所要取的一座城，就不可舉斧子砍壞樹木；因為你可以吃那樹上的果子，不可砍伐。田間的樹木豈是人，叫你蹧蹋嗎？

果樹解人飢渴。果樹無法在一天內長成。
**田間的樹木。**見撒上16:20，直譯為，“餅的驢”，意思就是馱餅的驢。同樣，這裡說果樹是為了供養人的。
19.en:
**The trees.** The fruit trees would give refreshment and sustenance. They could not be grown in a day.
**The tree of the field.** The word “life” is not in the Hebrew text. Compare 1 Sam. 16:20, which reads literally, an “ass of bread,” meaning an ass loaded with bread. Similarly, fruit trees are spoken of as being for the support of men. The RSV reads, “Are the trees in the field men that they should be besieged by you?”

20.zh:
惟獨你所知道不是結果子的樹木可以毀壞、砍伐，用以修築營壘，攻擊那與你打仗的城，直到攻塌了。

**不是結果子的。**直譯為“不為食物”。
**營壘。**直譯為“攻城設施”。這指的是為征服一座城而建造的各種營壘、戰壕等。該詞還譯為“保障”（代下8:5）、“為保障”（代下11:6）、“山寨”（耶10:17，[英文KJV版直譯為“山寨裡的人哪”，中文版為“受圍困的人哪”]）、“堅固的”（彌7:12，[英文KJV版直譯為“從堅固的城邑”，中文版為“從埃及的城邑”]）、“望樓”（哈2:1；參代下26:15；撒下20:15）。
**攻塌。**直譯為“倒塌”（見申28:52；賽32:19）。
20.en:
**For meat.** Literally, “for food.”
**Bulwarks.** Literally, “siege-works” (RSV). The reference is to various of ramparts, trenches, etc., built to aid in the subjugation of a city. The same word is translated “fenced” (2 Chron. 8:5); “for defence” (2 Chron. 11:5); “fortress” (Jer. 10:17); “fortified” (Micah 7:12); “the tower” (Hab. 2:1; cf. 2 Chron. 26:15; 2 Sam. 20:15).
**Be subdued.** Literally, “come down” (see Deut. 28:52; Isa. 32:19).

1.zh:
凡外腎受傷的，或被閹割的，不可入耶和華的會。

一些所謂的“聖人”出於神明的虔誠而故意割除其男性生殖器的做法一直延續至今。這種習俗作為宗教的一部分在許多古代民族中十分盛行（見利21:20）。
**不可入。**強調上帝對毀損人體的痛恨。這條禁令也適用於某些外國人，不讓他們進入會眾敬拜的聖所（尼13:1,7；哀1:10），但不是將他們排除在救恩，或上帝屬靈的殿之外（見賽56:3,5）。後來，在基督徒的屬靈團體中，有一位太監受到上帝所派特使的尊重（徒8:27-40）。太監的工作是服侍以色列和猶大的國王（王下9:32；耶29:2）。
1.en:
**He that is wounded.** The intentional mutilation of the male organs in devotion to a god by some “holy men” survived into modern times. This custom prevailed among various ancient peoples as a part of their religion (see Lev. 21:20).
**Not enter.** To emphasize God’s abhorrence of the mutilation of the human body. The same prohibition, applied to certain foreigners, evidently meant exclusion from the sanctuary, where the congregation worshiped (Neh. 13:1, 7; Lam. 1:10), but not exclusion from salvation, or God’s spiritual house (see Isa. 56:3, 5). Later, in God’s spiritual community of Christian believers, a eunuch was highly honored by a special messenger sent from God (Acts 8:27–40). Eunuchs were employed in the service of the kings of Israel and Judah (2 Kings 9:32; Jer. 29:2).

2.zh:
私生子不可入耶和華的會；他的子孫，直到十代，也不可入耶和華的會。

**私生子。**原文詞根不詳。在猶太教拉比的遺傳中，該詞不是指非婚生子女，而只是指因亂倫而出生的人，或是指一個出身不明的非以色列人或陌生人。家庭和屬靈生活的純潔一直是上帝最為重視的。關於排除在會眾之外，見本章1,3節的註釋。
2.en: **A bastard.** The root of the word thus translated is uncertain. Rabbinical tradition applies this term not to anyone born out of wedlock, but limits it to one born of incest, or else takes it to mean a non-Israelite, or a stranger of unknown ancestry. Purity of family and spiritual life has always been a matter of supreme moment to God. On exclusion from the congregation, see on vs. 1, 3.

3.zh:
亞捫人或是摩押人不可入耶和華的會；他們的子孫，雖過十代，也永不可入耶和華的會。

亞捫人多比雅，曾依據這節經文被排除在聖殿之外（見尼2:10；13:1-8）。
**懷愛倫註釋（3–6節）**。《先知與君王》670。
3.en: **Ammonite or Moabite.** Tobiah, an Ammonite, was excluded from the Temple on the strength of this text (see Neh. 2:10; 13:1–8).

4.zh:
因為你們出埃及的時候，他們沒有拿食物和水在路上迎接你們，又因他們僱了米所波大米的毘奪人比珥的兒子巴蘭來咒詛你們。

亞捫人和摩押人不友好的態度給以色列人增加了許多困難。這兩個民族都和以色列人有血緣關係，但是他們對以色列人連對陌生人應有的禮貌也沒有，更不用說對親屬所應有的禮貌了（創14:18；18:2；19:1,2）。上帝曾經吩咐以色列人不要騷擾亞捫人（申2:19）。這裡所說的，摩押人沒有用食物迎接以色列人，和申2:29節所說的，他們有賣糧給以色列人，這二者之間的矛盾其實只是表面上的而並非屬實。申23:4只是說摩押人沒有心甘情願地以友好的態度給他們提供食物，但沒有說他們不向以色列人出售食物。
**僱了……巴蘭來咒詛你們。**這是摩押人在米甸人的協助下所做的事（民22:4-7）。基督教導說沒有憐憫之心的人不能承受天國（太25:41-46）。對教會所表現的敵意被視為對基督本身的敵意（徒9:4,5）。
4.en:
**Met you not.** The unfriendly attitude of Ammon and Moab added much to the difficulties of the children of Israel. Both were akin to Israel, but did not even show them the common courtesies due to strangers, much less those due to kinsmen (Gen. 14:18; 18:2; 19:1, 2). God had already ordered the Israelites not to distress the Ammonites (Deut. 2:19). The seeming contradiction between the statement here made, that the Moabites did not meet Israel with provisions, and that of ch. 2:29 that they did do so, is more apparent than real. The words of ch. 23:4 imply only that the Moabites did not willingly offer them food in a friendly spirit—not that they did not sell food to the Israelites in return for money.
**Hired against thee Balaam.** This was the work of the Moabites assisted by the Midianites (Num. 22:4–7). Christ taught that the merciless person will not inherit the kingdom (Matt. 25:41–46). Enmity manifested toward the church is regarded as hostility toward Christ Himself (Acts 9:4, 5).

5.zh:
然而耶和華─你的神不肯聽從巴蘭，卻使那咒詛的言語變為祝福的話，因為耶和華─你的神愛你。

先知急於咒詛以色列人，但是耶和華卻將話語放在他的口中，使他無法忍住不說（見民22）。一個惡先知無法將上帝的祝福撇在一邊，而將咒詛加在祂子民的身上。巴蘭的咒詛變成了祝福（民23,24）。聖經中所記載的有關上帝護庇眷顧的其他實例還包括約瑟（創39:1-3；41:39-45）、末底改和猶太人（斯6至10）、年輕的但以理和他的三個朋友（但3:16-30；6:1,2）以及很多其它的例子。
5.en: **God would not hearken.** The prophet was eager to curse Israel, but Jehovah put words into his mouth that he could not refrain from uttering (see Num. 22). It was impossible for a wicked prophet to thrust aside God’s blessings and inflict curses upon His people. The curses of Balaam were turned into blessings (Num. 23, 24). Other examples of God’s protecting care are recorded of Joseph (Gen. 39:1–3; 41:39–45), Mordecai and the Jewish people (Esther 6 to 10), the young man Daniel and his three companions (Dan. 3:16–30; 6:1, 2), and many others.

6.zh:
你一生一世永不可求他們的平安和他們的利益。

這是指他們與異教鄰邦結交（見拉9:12）。就以社交為目的的普通交往而言，以色列人應與這些民族保持完全的分離。在巴力毗珥的經歷已充分顯示這種交往的不幸結局（見民25:1-9）。摩押人是他們的近鄰，無疑會有許多彼此親密自由交往的機會，所以這個警告特別恰當。
6.en: **Seek their peace.** This refers to fraternizing with their heathen neighbors (see Ezra 9:12). Israel was to remain entirely separate from these people, so far as common association for social purposes was concerned. The experience at Baal-peor had demonstrated the tragic results of such association (see Num. 25:1–9). This warning was particularly appropriate in view of the fact that the Moabites were their close neighbors, and there would no doubt be many occasions for free and intimate association.

7.zh:
不可憎惡以東人，因為他是你的弟兄。不可憎惡埃及人，因為你在他的地上作過寄居的。

**以東人。**以色列國和鄰近的以東國之間一直存在著敵對狀態（民20:18-21；見撒下8:13註釋）。
**埃及人。**不要忘記以色列人曾在埃及得到多年的庇護。他們儘管被迫服苦役，卻仍在那裡興旺起來。
**懷愛倫註釋（7–8節）**。《先祖與先知》375。
7.en:
**An Edomite.** There was a permanent state of hostility between the neighboring kingdoms of Israel and Edom (Num. 20:18–21; see on 2 Sam. 8:13).
**An Egyptian.** It was not to be forgotten that Israel had found refuge in Egypt for many years, and had prospered in the land despite enforced hardships.

8.zh:
他們第三代子孫可以入耶和華的會。

**第三代子孫。**以色列人在埃及住了二百年，在遭遇可怕的饑荒時得到了保護和供養。後來出現了逼迫。然而上帝不想讓祂的子民只看到一個國家不好的一面，而且只想到這一點。以東人或埃及人的第三代子孫，只要受了割禮，就可以享有上帝子民的一切特權。這兩個國家在貿易和文化方面可能有很多的交往。
8.en: **Third generation.** For 200 years Israel had found a home in Egypt. They had enjoyed protection and sustenance in a time of terrible famine. Later came persecution. Yet God would not have His people see only the evil side of a nation’s character, and dwell only on it. In the third generation the descendants of an Edomite or an Egyptian were allowed all the privileges of God’s people, upon being circumcised. There was probably considerable intercourse between the two countries, in trade and culture.

9.zh:
你出兵攻打仇敵，就要遠避諸惡。

這裡告誡要嚴格保持身體的清潔和生活的純潔。軍隊出征時，與正常的社會關係隔絕的大批男丁會遇到試探去做卑汙的事。以色列人在上帝面前的狀況要比其為對付敵人所做的軍事準備更重要。上帝不能始終領導不忠實和不潔淨的民族取得勝利。
9.en: **From every wicked thing.** Strictness in respect to physical cleanliness and purity of life is here admonished. As an army on the march, a large body of men cut off from normal social relations has many temptations to lower standards of conduct. The condition of Israel before God was much more important than her military preparations for meeting the enemy. God could not consistently lead a faithless, unclean people to victory.

10.zh:
你們中間，若有人夜間偶然夢遺，不潔淨，就要出到營外，不可入營；

**不潔淨。**見利15:16。事實上，上帝要求以色列軍隊脫離道德的汙穢、儀文的汙穢和身體的汙穢。耶和華在營中引導他們獲得勝利。祂不能容忍那些常與軍事生活相關的低下標準。
**懷愛倫註釋（10–14節）**。《健康勉言》62，81，101。
10.en: **Uncleanness.** See Lev. 15:16. As a matter of fact, God required that Israel’s military forces be free from moral pollution, ceremonial pollution, and natural physical pollution. Jehovah was in the midst of the camp to lead them to victory. He would not tolerate the lowered standards that are all too frequently an accompaniment of military life.

11.zh:
到傍晚的時候，他要用水洗澡，及至日落了才可以入營。

他只有到一天結束時才能重新獲得潔淨。
11.en: **Evening.** He would not regain his cleanness until the close of the day.

12.zh:
你在營外也該定出一個地方作為便所。

要注意生活習慣的清潔衛生。應當實施衛生的規則，不僅是為了感覺的舒適，也是為了保護軍隊的健康。
12.en: **Whither thou shalt go.** Decency and respect for the conventions of life were to be observed. Sanitary rules were to be enforced, not only in deference to fineness of feeling but to protect the health of the army.

13.zh:
在你器械之中當預備一把鍬，你出營外便溺以後，用以鏟土，轉身掩蓋。

**一把鍬。**就是橛子，一種多用途的銳器，用作帳棚的橛子（出27:19；士4:21,22）；紡織的工具（士16:13,14）；或標樁，喻指上帝聖手的保護（賽33:20）。
13.en: **A paddle.** A sharp instrument of various uses. It was used as a pin, or tent peg (Ex. 27:19; Judges 4:21, 22), a tool used in weaving (Judges 16:13, 14); a stake, figuratively used of protection under God’s hand (Isa. 33:20). The RSV reads, “a stick with your weapons.”

14.zh:
因為耶和華─你的神常在你營中行走，要救護你，將仇敵交給你，所以你的營理當聖潔，免得他見你那裡有汙穢，就離開你。

**上帝……行走。**使軍營成為聖地。約櫃在營中象徵著耶和華的同在（見民10:33-36）。動詞“行走”所用的形式暗示在營中來回地行走（見創3:8；13:17；撒下7:6,7）。參使徒保羅在林後6:16至7:1的話。他在寫這段話時可能想到了這節經文。
**免得……有汙穢。**直譯為“任何裸露”，通常指下流的裸露。該詞還出現在創9:22,23；出28:42；利18:6,7等節中。
**離開。**參耶32:40。任何可恥、汙穢和下流的東西都不許隨便放過；否則上帝就不會留在營中了──祂將允許敵人打敗他們。一個不潔淨的教會無法在基督與撒但的鬥爭中獲勝，因為上天的祝福只給那些毫無保留地信靠和順從祂的人。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《教育論》38；《服務真詮》280；《今日的生活》129，《先祖與先知》375；《證言》卷六170。
14.en:
**God walketh.** So making the camp holy ground. The ark was in the camp as a token of Jehovah’s presence (see Num. 10:33–36). The form of the verb “to walk” here used suggests walking up and down in the camp (see Gen. 3:8; 13:17; 2 Sam. 7:6, 7). Compare the statement of the apostle Paul in 2 Cor. 6:16 to 7:1, who may have had this verse in mind at the time he wrote.
**No unclean thing.** Literally, “any nakedness of anything,” commonly meaning indecent exposure. The same word occurs in Gen. 9:22, 23; Ex. 28:42; Lev. 18:6, 7; etc.
**Turn away.** Compare Jer. 32:40. Nothing shameful, unclean, indecent, should be allowed to go unchecked, or God would not remain in the camp—meaning that He would allow them to be defeated by their enemies. An unclean church cannot be victorious in the controversy between Christ and Satan, for Heaven’s blessing awaits only those who trust and obey Him without reserve.

15.zh:
若有奴僕脫了主人的手，逃到你那裡，你不可將他交付他的主人。

**懷愛倫註釋（15–16節）**。《先祖與先知》532。

16.zh:
他必在你那裡與你同住，在你的城邑中，要由他選擇一個所喜悅的地方居住；你不可欺負他。

**與你同住。**在他喜歡的城中（申15:7；16:5；17:2；18:6）。
**不可欺負他。**摩西律法的精神是反對奴隸制度的。他所提倡 的是一種仁慈的精神（利19:33,34）。
16.en:
**Dwell with thee.** In the city that appealed to him (chs. 15:7; 16:5; 17:2; 18:6).
**Not oppress him.** The spirit of the law of Moses was opposed to slavery. Rather, a spirit of kindness was enjoined (Lev. 19:33, 34).

17.zh:
以色列的女子中不可有妓女；以色列的男子中不可有孌童。

**不可有妓女。**這節經文是泛指的，但所似乎主要指宗教性賣淫。“妓女”和“孌童”的希伯來語詞根是相同，意為“聖的”。該詞根還用於聖所（出26:33,34）、聖衣（出28:2,4）、聖壇（出29:37）等。英文RSV版譯為“寺廟妓女”。寺廟賣淫一直是偶像崇拜的特色。這樣的習俗在東方的某些地區一直延續至今。妓女被稱為神靈的女僕。任何形式的賣淫都是上帝所憎惡的，而將賣淫奉為宗教的一部分則是最可憎的墮落。見王上14:23,24；15:12；王下23:7；耶3:2中所提到的與宗教有關的賣淫。
17.en: **No whore.** The language of this verse is general, yet the chief reference seems to be to religious prostitution. The words translated “whore” and “sodomite” both come from the same Hebrew root, which means “sanctified” or “holy,” as applied to the sanctuary (Ex. 26:33, 34), to the holy garments (Ex. 28:2, 4), to the altar (Ex. 29:37), etc. The RSV reads, “cult prostitute.” Temple prostitution has ever been a common feature of idolatry. Such a practice has survived into modern times in some portions of the East. The woman was known as a female servant of the god. Prostitution of the body is an abomination to God, in any case, but to consecrate prostitution as a part of religion is a most abhorrent degradation. See references to prostitution in connection with religion, in 1 Kings 14:23, 24; 15:12; 2 Kings 23:7; Jer. 3:2.

18.zh:
娼妓所得的錢，或孌童（原文作狗）所得的價，你不可帶入耶和華─你神的殿還願，因為這兩樣都是耶和華─你神所憎惡的。

**所得的錢。**指付給普通妓女或寺廟妓女的錢（何9:1；彌1:7）。
**狗所得的價。**“價”與“錢”源於不同的詞根。這是“狗”所得的“價”。“狗”在這裡指第17節的“孌童”。這在希伯來語中是一個貶義詞（撒上17:43；撒下16:9；賽56:10）。見使徒約翰對不能進永恆國度之人的描述（啟22:15）。在東方國家中，流浪狗又餓又髒（王上14:11），是不潔淨和被遺棄的象徵。
18.en:
**The hire.** The word for “hire” is commonly used of the payment to a woman either for common prostitution or for that connected with temple worship (Hosea 9:1; Micah 1:7).
**The price of a dog.** The word “price” is not from the same root as “hire.” It is the “price” or “payment” that the “dog” receives. The word “dog” is here used to designate the person mentioned in v. 17 as a “sodomite.” It is a contemptuous term in Hebrew (1 Sam. 17:43; 2 Sam. 16:9; Isa. 56:10). Compare the apostle John’s description of those who may not enter the eternal kingdom (Rev. 22:15). In Eastern countries dogs roam about half wild, hungry, and unclean (1 Kings 14:11). They are a symbol of uncleanness and of outcasts.

19.zh:
你借給你弟兄的，或是錢財或是糧食，無論什麼可生利的物，都不可取利。

**取利。**見出22:25註釋。這個吩咐不是針對普通的商貿，而是以色列國貧窮救濟法律的一部分，只針對那些有實際困難的人（見出22:25註釋；另見利25:35,36；參尼5:2-5,10-12）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先知與君王》647。
**懷愛倫註釋（19–20節）**。《證言》卷一535。
19.en: **Usury.** See on Ex. 22:25. This injunction does not refer to ordinary business, trade, or commerce; but was part of the poor law of the land of Israel, and designed only for the benefit of those in actual distress (see on Ex. 22:25; see also Lev. 25:35, 36; cf. Neh. 5:2-5, 10–12).

20.zh:
借給外邦人可以取利，只是借給你弟兄不可取利。這樣，耶和華─你神必在你所去得為業的地上和你手裡所辦的一切事上賜福與你。

**外邦人。**非猶太人，不管是不是住在以色列。一個已經皈依猶太教的外國人應被當作兄弟對待（利19:33,34）。
20.en: **A stranger.** A non-Jew, whether a resident in Israel or not. A foreigner who had become a proselyte was to be treated as a brother (Lev. 19:33, 34).

21.zh:
你向耶和華─你的神許願，償還不可遲延；因為耶和華─你的神必定向你追討，你不償還就有罪。

**許願。**就是向耶和華所許的莊嚴誓約，這是一種不可輕視的義務。有關的實例，見創28:20；民21:2；士11:30；撒上1:11；撒下15:7；參民30:2-16。希伯來原文的主要意思是“奉獻”。
**遲延。**這裡沒有提到支付的地點；詳見申12:5,6,11,18-26中。關於償付所許之願的福分，見詩22:25；50:14；56:12,13；61:8；65:1；66:13。
**懷愛倫註釋（21–23節）**。《證言》卷四471。
21.en:
**Vow a vow.** That is, a solemn vow to Jehovah, an obligation not to be treated lightly. For examples see Gen. 28:20; Num. 21:2; Judges 11:30; 1 Sam. 1:11; 2 Sam. 15:7; cf. Num. 30:2–16. The primary meaning of the Hebrew word is “to dedicate.”
**Slack.** From the usual Hebrew word meaning “to delay,” “to tarry,” “to remain behind.” Nothing is said here in respect to the place where payment was to be made; that information is given in ch. 12:5, 6, 11, 18, 26. For the blessedness of paying one’s vows see Ps. 22:25; 50:14; 56:12, 13; 61:8; 65:1; 66:13.

22.zh:
你若不許願，倒無罪。

人不一定要向耶和華許願。所當盡的義務乃是許願之後的履行。違約在上帝看來乃是罪。向上帝許願就是承擔了神聖的義務。不盡義務就會傷害人屬靈的生命（見利27；民30）。
22.en: **Forbear.** It is not obligatory to make vows to Jehovah. What is obligatory is the carrying out of a vow after it has been made. Such a violation is sin in the sight of God. To make a vow to God is to assume a sacred obligation. To withdraw from that obligation is to injure one’s spiritual life (see Lev. 27; Num. 30).

23.zh:
你嘴裡所出的，就是你口中應許甘心所獻的，要照你向耶和華─你神所許的願謹守遵行。

這不是強制性的。許願是自願的，但許了就必須履行。
23.en: **Out of thy lips.** There was no compulsion. The vow was freely made, and must be carried out accordingly.

24.zh:
你進了鄰舍的葡萄園，可以隨意吃飽了葡萄，只是不可裝在器皿中。

這裡主要指是葡萄園裡的工人和過路需要充飢的客旅。在現今的東方，人經過一個村莊前往另一個村莊時，從田間拿一根甘蔗吃仍是常見（見太12:1-9）。
**隨意。**直譯為“照你的心意”。該詞通常譯為“心靈”，但在這裡指的是“食慾”（見詩107:9；箴13:25；賽58:11）。
**在器皿中。**過路人可以解決眼前的飢餓。但把食物帶走就是濫用了為幫助旅客而設的特權。
**懷愛倫註釋（24–25節）**。《歷代願望》284。
24.en:
**Eat grapes.** The primary reference here is to workmen in a vineyard and to travelers passing by and in need of refreshment. It is common practice in the East today for a man to take a stick of sugar cane from a field in passing from one village to another (see Matt. 12:1–9).
**At thine own pleasure.** Literally, “according to thy soul.” The word usually translated “soul,” here means “appetite” (see Ps. 107:9; Prov. 13:25; Isa. 58:11).
**In thy vessel.** Those passing by might eat to satisfy present hunger. But to carry any away would be to abuse a privilege designed as a blessing to the traveler.

25.zh:
你進了鄰舍站著的禾稼，可以用手摘穗子，只是不可用鐮刀割取禾稼。

**用鐮刀。**見可2:23。正當的飢餓應該得到滿足；但多拿就成為偷盜。這個規定與愛人如己的第二條“最大的誡命”一致，也是表示承認收穫來源於上帝。
主人不會在意從他的田裡或果園裡拿走的少量糧食或水果，但這些卻足以滿足過路人一時的飢餓。主人不會覺得自己受了虧待；貧窮的陌生人也不會覺得社會不關心他的需要。
25.en:
**Move a sickle.** Compare Mark 2:23. Legitimate hunger should be satisfied; to take more would be theft. This provision was in harmony with the second “great commandment” of love to one’s neighbor, and was an acknowledgment that the harvest was from God.
The owner would not miss the small quantity of grain or fruit thus taken from his field or orchard, yet it would suffice the immediate hunger of the one passing by. The owner could not properly feel that he had been wronged, nor could the stranger, if poor, come to feel that society was not interested in his needs.

1.zh:
人若有爭訟，來聽審判，審判官就要定義人有理，定惡人有罪。

**爭訟。**根據下文，這是一場導致訴訟的爭端，原文來源於詞根“使激動”、“大聲吵架”、“喊叫”（見創26:22；伯9:3；箴25:9）。這裡所用的名詞形式也出現在創13:7；伯31:13。
**聽審判。**指“上法庭”（英文RSV版），審判的地方（王上7:7；賽28:6）。“審判”還指法庭的司法程序（伯14:3；傳11:9；12:14），和審判官在聽訟之後所宣佈的判決（瑪2:17）。
**定義人有理。**被誣告的人無罪釋放。“義”的原文也指罪人在上帝面前稱義。該詞在這裡指在法律意義上的宣人無罪（見出22:9；撒下15:4；詩94:21；箴17:15；賽5:23）。法庭是按上帝親自的指示而設立的。
**定惡人有罪。**這裡“定……有罪”和“惡人”兩個詞源於相同的詞根。這句話直譯為“使不正常的[沒規矩的]人正常化”。相關的阿拉伯語詞根意為（四肢）“鬆散”，因此指“沒有規矩”或“脫臼”。所作出的判決是為了使之康復，恢復正常，而不是報復性的懲罰。
1.en:
**Controversy.** A dispute leading to litigation, as is plain from what follows. The word thus translated is from the root “to agitate,” “to quarrel noisily,” “to shout” (see Gen. 26:22; Job 9:3; Prov. 25:9). The noun form, as used here, appears also in Gen. 13:7; Job 31:13.
**Unto judgment.** “Into court” (RSV), the place of judgment (1 Kings 7:7; Isa. 28:6). The word “judgment” also refers to the process or procedure of justice in the courts (Job 14:3; Eccl. 11:9; 12:14). Finally, it is used of the decision or “judgment” handed down by a judge after hearing a case (Mal. 2:17).
**Justify the righteous.** Literally, “cause to be righteous the righteous one.” The one falsely accused was to be exonerated and acquitted. The word here translated “righteous” is also used of the righteousness of the justified sinner before God. Here it is used in the legal sense of pronouncing a man not guilty (see Ex. 22:9; 2 Sam. 15:4; Ps. 94:21; Prov. 17:15; Isa. 5:23). Courts were established by God’s own direction.
**Condemn the wicked.** The words here translated “condemn” and “wicked” are from the same root. Literally, the expression would read, “to cause to be regulated the abnormal [unregulated] ones.” The related Arabic root means “to be loose” (of the limbs), and therefore “ill regulated” or “out of joint.” An endeavor was to be made to rehabilitate and regulate, rather than to punish in the sense of vengeance.

2.zh:
惡人若該受責打，審判官就要叫他當面伏在地上，按著他的罪照數責打。

**當面。**就是在證人和審判官面前，在露天的院子裡。讓他伏倒在地，並按照審判官的判決責打他。體罰通常採用棍子（撒下7:14），但有時用帶刺的樹枝（士8:7,16），也用笞或鞭（王上12:11,14）。“蠍子鞭”是用系成硬結的皮條製成的鞭子，上面有鋒利的木片或金屬片。
2.en: **Before his face.** That is, in open court, before the witnesses and the judges. He was made to lie down, and given the number of blows prescribed by the judge. Corporal punishment was usually administered by a stick (2 Sam. 7:14), though sometimes with thorn branches (Judges 8:7, 16), and sometimes with scourges or whips (1 Kings 12:11, 14). “Scorpions” were leather strips tied in hard knots containing sharp pieces of wood or metal.

3.zh:
只可打他四十下，不可過數；若過數，便是輕賤你的弟兄了。

**四十下。**見保羅的經歷（林後11:24）。後來猶太人將鞭數定在39下，以免不留神地超過了應受的40下。
**輕賤。**過分嚴厲的處罰會導致怨恨，使人覺得他受到了不公平的待遇。超過40下就算是不公平。如果處罰在會堂裡執行，鞭打的同時往往還要在證人面前誦讀象申28:58,59這樣的經文。
3.en:
**Forty stripes.** Compare the experience of Paul (2 Cor. 11:24). Later the Jews fixed the number at 39, lest inadvertently more than 40 should be given.
**Vile.** Unduly severe punishment would lead to resentment and the feeling that the man had been unjustly treated. One stroke beyond 40 would be considered unjust. When the punishment was inflicted in the synagogue, it was the custom to read such passages as Deut. 28:58, 59 during the flogging, and in the presence of witnesses.

4.zh:
牛在場上踹穀的時候，不可籠住他的嘴。

從古時起，人們就習慣用牛踹谷。在今天的印度，人們經常給牲畜戴口套。踹谷經常會使牛的蹄子疼痛，而且經常會導致它們瘸腿，特別是在勞作過度的情況下。摩西的這個誡命不僅使“牛”免受殘酷的待遇，也是為了灌輸柔和的精神。這在異教民族中是不常見的。注意箴12:10對這一點所表露的情感。使徒保羅引用了申25:4，證明從事聖工的人應該得到一份適當和充足的工價，與其職分的神聖尊嚴相符（見林前9:9；提前5:18；參太10:10）。忠實的服務，無論是人的還是牲畜的，都應得到充分的認可。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《傳道良助》450；《給傳道人的證言》253；347，493。
4.en: **The ox.** From ancient times it was the custom to use oxen for treading out grain. In India today it is the usual thing to muzzle the animals. The treading out of the grain is often painful to the feet of the oxen, and it is not unusual for them to go lame as a result, especially if overworked at the task. This Mosaic precept not only protected the “ox” from cruel treatment but was designed to inculcate tenderheartedness—a trait that was not common among the heathen. Note the sentiments expressed in Prov. 12:10 on this very point. The apostle Paul referred to Deut. 25:4 as evidence that the ministry should receive a proper and adequate wage, in harmony with the sacred dignity of their office (see 1 Cor. 9:9; 1 Tim. 5:18; cf. Matt. 10:10). Faithful service, whether of men or of animals, deserves generous recognition.

5.zh:
弟兄同居，若死了一個，沒有兒子，死人的妻不可出嫁外人，他丈夫的兄弟當盡弟兄的本分，娶他為妻，與他同房。

這種婚姻的目的是為了給死者提供一個繼承人（見創38:8；太22:25註釋），通常被稱為叔娶嫂制。由此而生的第一個兒子要成為已故兄弟的後嗣，繼承他的名份和產業。拒絕履行這一職責的兄弟將受到公眾的譴責。這種習俗在許多古代民族中都非常流行，但形式稍有不同。在印度某些較早期民族的後代中這種習俗一直延續至今。關於這種婚姻原則的實際操作，聖經中最著名的就是摩押女子路得的例子（得1:22；2:1-4:17）。
5.en: **The duty of an husband’s brother.** The purpose of such a marriage was to provide a successor to the deceased (see on Gen. 38:8; Matt. 22:25). The first son born to such a union, commonly called a levirate marriage, was to become the heir of the deceased brother, in order to perpetuate his name and estate. A brother who refused to carry out this duty was held in public disgrace. This custom was common among many ancient nations, with variations, and survived into modern times among descendants of some of the earlier peoples of India. The best-known Biblical example of the operation of the principle of levirate marriage is that of Ruth the Moabitess (Ruth 1:22; 2:1 to 4:17).

6.zh:
婦人生的長子必歸死兄的名下，免得他的名在以色列中塗抹了。

見民27:4；得4:5。歷代以來，人都非常重視家系的延續。今天的東方國家中依然如此。沒有什麼不幸比無後代更嚴重的了。
6.en: **His name.** Compare Num. 27:4; Ruth 4:5. Men in all ages have valued perpetuation of the family name. This remains true in Oriental countries today, where no greater calamity can come to a man than to die without a male heir.

7.zh:
那人若不願意娶他哥哥的妻，他哥哥的妻就要到城門長老那裡，說：我丈夫的兄弟不肯在以色列中興起他哥哥的名字，不給我盡弟兄的本分。

關於長老在城門口的權威，見申21:19；22:15；得4:1。假如那兄弟覺得他無法愛她，律法並沒有要求他必須與寡婦結婚。但倘若他拒絕與她結婚，她就可以對他提出正式的指控。
7.en: **The elders.** On the authority of the elders at the gate, see Deut. 21:19; 22:15; Ruth 4:1. The law did not require the brother to marry the widow if he felt that he could not love her. But in case he refused to marry her, she could enter a formal complaint against him.

8.zh:
本城的長老就要召那人來問他，他若執意說：我不願意娶他，

**長老。**是城中負責處理此案的領袖。他們無疑地完全瞭解他的情況，並且有權瞭解與此有關的進一步情況。“長老”直譯為“年長的人”。他們極受尊重，權力狠大。
8.en: **The elders.** The “elders” were the responsible city leaders to deal with him. They were no doubt fully acquainted with his circumstances and in a position to secure further information about the case. The “elders,” literally “elderly men,” were held in great respect, and exercised considerable authority.

9.zh:
他哥哥的妻就要當著長老到那人的跟前，脫了他的鞋，吐唾沫在他臉上，說：凡不為哥哥建立家室的都要這樣待他。

**脫了他的鞋。**直譯為他的“淺幫套鞋”。猶太教的遺傳指出這是右腳的鞋。這是一種侮辱之舉，因為不遵從叔娶嫂制的律例（見第5節註釋），被視為自私的表現（見得4:6）。將穿著鞋的腳放在財產上乃是表示人對它的蔑視或合法的所有權（詩60:8；108:9）。所以鞋子被其兄弟的寡妻脫掉乃是表示他不值得尊重，因他拒絕做當做的事。歌7:1用穿鞋的腳寓指美麗和動人。赤腳走路被看作是屈辱（撒下15:30；賽20:2,4），或謙卑的象徵（出3:5；書5:15）。
**在他臉上。**猶太教註釋家通常把這句話解釋為“在他面前”往地上吐唾沫。這似乎是合理的，因為其介詞不是“在……上”，而是“在……旁”或“之前”（申11:25；書10:8）。在他面前吐唾沫就是羞辱他（民12:14）。該動詞在希伯來語聖經中出現三次。
**都要這樣待他。**僅有的例外是不受叔娶嫂制約束的大祭司（利21:13,14），住在遠處的兄弟，以及上了年紀的兄弟。
9.en:
**Loose his shoe.** Literally, his “sandal.” Jewish tradition indicates the shoe of the right foot. The deed here described was regarded as an act of indignity, inasmuch as failure to comply with the levirate law (see on v. 5) was looked upon as a mark of selfishness (see Ruth 4:6). The placing of the shod foot on property proclaimed either one’s contempt for it or one’s rightful ownership over it (Ps. 60:8; 108:9). Accordingly, the removal of the man’s shoe by his brother’s widow proclaimed the man’s unworthiness. He refused to do what was rightfully to be expected of him. Compare S. of Sol. 7:1 for the figure of the sandaled foot as a picture of beauty and desirableness. To go unshod was looked upon as degrading (2 Sam. 15:30; Isa. 20:2, 4) or as a token of humility (Ex. 3:5; Joshua 5:15).
**In his face.** Jewish commentators usually interpret this as spitting on the ground “before his face.” This seems reasonable, because the preposition is not “upon,” but “by” or “before” (Deut. 11:25; Joshua 10:8). Spitting before the face was thought to be humiliating (Num. 12:14). This verb appears three times in the Hebrew Bible.
**So shall it be done.** The only exceptions were the high priest, who was not subject to the levirate law (Lev. 21:13, 14), brothers living at a distance, and the aged.

11.zh:
若有二人爭鬥，這人的妻近前來，要救他丈夫脫離那打他丈夫之人的手，抓住那人的下體，

出21：22講到二人打架傷及孕婦導致流產的賠償。在這裡，男人受到了法律的保護。有些註釋家認為這指的是第5-10節的寡婦抓住她丈夫的弟弟，強迫他與她結婚。如果是這樣的話，這個律例的意思就是禁止那婦人超過得體的限度。但上下文清楚說明，這是指兩人打架，其中一人的妻子試圖幫助她的丈夫。“爭鬥”譯為“摔跤”更妥。該詞在出2:13；21:22；利24:10；撒下14:6中有不同的譯法。
11.en: **Strive together.** In Ex. 21:22 is recorded the case of men quarreling, and the compensation to be given to a pregnant woman injured as a result of a fight between the men. In this case, legal protection is afforded the man. Some commentators have suggested that this refers to the widow of vs. 5–10 taking hold of her brother-in-law to force him into marriage with her. If such be the application, this law would forbid the woman passing beyond the bounds of decency. However, the context makes it clear that this was a personal quarrel in which the wife of one of the men endeavored to help her husband. The word here translated “strive” might better be translated “wrestle.” It is rendered variously in Ex. 2:13; 21:22; Lev. 24:10; 2 Sam. 14:6.

12.zh:
就要砍斷婦人的手，眼不可顧惜他。

不是由被她抓的男人執行，因為他可能已永久性殘疾了。他會將向審判官提出訴訟。這條律例來自出21:24中的原則。有些猶太教註釋家認為不應照字面意義理解這句話。拉比後來將這句話改為一種鉅額的罰款。
12.en: **Cut off her hand.** This was not to be done by the man she grasped, for he would be incapacitated, perhaps permanently injured. He would bring his complaint before the judges. This law is derived from the principle stated in Ex. 21:24. Some Jewish commentators reject the idea that this was to be taken literally. The rabbis later changed the sentence to one of heavy fine.

13.zh:
你囊中不可有一大一小兩樣的法碼。

賣東西時用較輕的砝碼，買東西被用較重的砝碼。直譯為“一大一小兩塊石頭”。古希伯來人的砝碼通常是用石頭做的。摩8:5指出這種不誠實的做法在猶太人中並不罕見。注意箴20:23中有關兩樣砝碼的話。這是耶和華所“憎惡”的，而公道的砝碼是上帝所認可的（箴16:11）。先知彌迦以相似的話語表達了上帝對不公平之砝碼的不悅（彌6:11）。上帝定意使公正和公平的原則在祂的子民中普及。侍奉上帝的人不會欺騙他們的同胞（見約壹4:20）。
**懷愛倫註釋（13–14節）**。《服務真詮》188。
**懷愛倫註釋（13–16節）**。《給管家的勉言》77。
**懷愛倫註釋（13–18節）**。《給傳道人的證言》371。
13.en: **Divers weights.** “Two kinds of weights” (RSV), a lighter weight used in selling and a larger one in purchasing. Literally, “a stone and a stone, large and small.” Ancient Hebrew weights were usually made of stone. Amos 8:5 indicates that this particular type of dishonesty was not uncommon among the Jews. Note the statement about different weights in Prov. 20:23, as an “abomination” to Jehovah, whereas just weights are approved by the Lord (Prov. 16:11). The prophet Micah makes a similar statement on God’s displeasure with unjust weights (Micah 6:11). God designs that among His people principles of justice and equity shall prevail. Those who serve God will not cheat their fellow men (see 1 John 4:20).

14.zh:
你家裡不可有一大一小兩樣的升斗。

**懷愛倫註釋（14–16節）**。《證言》卷七179。

15.zh:
當用對準公平的法碼，公平的升斗。這樣，在耶和華─你神所賜你的地上，你的日子就可以長久。

見利19:35,36。人在做生意時總是想錢賺得容易一些。我們說誠實是最好的策略。但有些商人所遵循的策略就像叢林中張牙舞爪的野獸一樣殘酷。必須承認，這樣的交易常常會給人帶來巨大的財富，甚至很高的社會名望。但是沒有誠實，人永遠也不會有心靈的平安和在上帝面前無愧的良心。
15.en: **Perfect and just weight.** See Lev. 19:35, 36. The tendency to indulge the temptation to make easy profits is not always easily eliminated in business dealings. We speak of honesty as being the best policy. Yet the policy followed by some businessmen is as cruel as that of tooth and claw in the jungle. It must be admitted that such dealings have often brought men enormous riches, and even high repute in society. Yet without honesty there can never be peace of mind and a clear conscience before God.

17.zh:
你要記念你們出埃及的時候，亞瑪力人在路上怎樣待你。

這裡指的是亞瑪力人在以色列人從埃及出來的途中與他們為敵（出17:8-16）。的確，在寫《申命記》的時候，亞瑪力人對以色列人已不再是一種威脅。但耶和華沒有忘記他們對祂的子民所造成的傷害。
**懷愛倫註釋（17–19節）**。《證言》卷二108；《證言》卷五245。
17.en: **Amalek.** The reference here is to the hostility of the Amalekites toward Israel on their journey from Egypt (Ex. 17:8–16). It is true that at the time of the writing of the book of Deuteronomy the Amalekites were no longer a threat to Israel. Yet Jehovah did not forget the injury they had done to His people.

18.zh:
他們在路上遇見你，趁你疲乏困倦擊殺你儘後邊軟弱的人，並不敬畏神。

**擊殺你盡後邊。**反映了他們的懦弱和殘酷（見出17:8-13）。
**並不敬畏上帝。**這是他作惡的原因。不關注正確的原則就沒有睦鄰友好的基礎。
18.en:
**Smote the hindmost.** Reflecting cowardice and cruelty (see Ex. 17:8–13).
**He feared not God.** This was the reason for his evil conduct. Indifference to right principles can scarcely provide a solid foundation upon which to build kindness and love for one’s neighbors.

19.zh:
所以耶和華─你神使你不被四圍一切的仇敵擾亂，在耶和華─你神賜你為業的地上得享平安。那時，你要將亞瑪力的名號從天下塗抹了，不可忘記。

耶和華是慈愛和公義的上帝。消滅亞瑪力人的命令首先是向約書亞發出的（出17:14），但是對這個惡貫滿盈的民族實際的懲罰是分階段完成的。巴拉和基甸（士5:14；6:3；7:12），掃羅和撒母耳（撒上15:1-9），以及大衛（撒上27:8,9；30:1,17），都參與了對亞瑪力人判決的執行。西緬人最終完成了這項任務（代上4:42,43）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖與先知》628；《給傳道人的證言》372。
19.en: **Blot out.** The Lord is a God of love and righteousness. The command to wipe out the Amalekites as a nation was first addressed to Joshua (Ex. 17:14), but the actual work of judgment upon this people, which had filled up its cup of iniquity, was carried out in stages. Barak and Gideon (Judges 5:14; 6:3; 7:12), Saul and Samuel (1 Sam. 15:1–9), and David (1 Sam. 27:8, 9; 30:1, 17), all participated in executing the decree against them. Finally came the children of Simeon, who completed the task (1 Chron. 4:42, 43).

1.zh:
你進去得了耶和華─你神所賜你為業之地居住，

就是在聖地定居。這種說法已重複多次（申17:14）。
1.en: **Come in.** That is, settled in the Holy Land. This form of expression has already been used a number of times (ch. 17:14).

2.zh:
就要從耶和華─你神賜你的地上將所收的各種初熟的土產取些來，盛在筐子裡，往耶和華─你神所選擇要立為他名的居所去，

有關初熟土產的律例，見民18:12；申18:4。
**往……居所去。**要取一部分初熟的果實放在筐子裡，帶到聖所，交給值班的祭司。
2.en:
**The first.** On the law of first fruits see Num. 18:12; Deut. 18:4.
**Unto the place.** A portion of the first ripe fruits was to be taken in a basket, brought to the sanctuary, and given to the priest on duty.

3.zh:
見當時作祭司的，對他說：我今日向耶和華─你神明認，我已來到耶和華向我們列祖起誓應許賜給我們的地。

這是在三大節期中（出23:14-16）。後來，敬拜者要為這些節期將供物帶到耶路撒冷的聖殿，在上帝的聖所讚美祂。他們要藉著認罪和感恩的祈禱，承認上帝恩慈將他們從埃及的奴役中解救出來並帶到應許之地。
3.en: **Thou shalt go.** That is, at the time of the three great feasts (Ex. 23:14–16). In later times the worshipers were to bring their offerings to the Temple in Jerusalem for these feasts, praising God in His sanctuary. With confession of sin and grateful prayer they were to acknowledge God’s goodness in bringing them out of Egyptian bondage into the Promised Land.

4.zh:
祭司就從你手裡取過筐子來，放在耶和華─你神的壇前。

祭司將筐子搖一搖並放在耶和華面前，以此承認耶和華對那地的所有權。這個一個歡樂的儀式，感激上帝賜予豐收、平安和昌盛。使徒保羅曾闡述了將上帝所賜的一部分福歸還給祂的原則，讓基督徒加以效法（林前16:2；林後8:7-9）。
4.en: **Before the altar.** The priest waved the basket and placed it before the Lord, in acknowledgment of Jehovah’s ownership of the land. This ceremony was to be one of joy in God, as the Giver of harvest, peace, and prosperity. The principle of returning to God a portion of the blessings received from Him is one stated by the apostle Paul for Christians to emulate (1 Cor. 16:2; 2 Cor. 8:7–9).

5.zh:
你要在耶和華─你神面前說：我祖原是一個將亡的亞蘭人，下到埃及寄居。他人口稀少，在那裡卻成了又大又強、人數很多的國民。

**一個將亡的亞蘭人。**直譯為“一個飄流的亞蘭人”。指這個民族的卑微起源，就是來自巴旦亞蘭的利百加和利亞（創25:20），和在那裡寄居多年的雅各（創29-31章）。雅各的母舅拉班被稱為“亞蘭人”（創25:20；28:5,6；31:20,24）。“將亡”一詞的原文用來指迷路的牲畜（申22:3；撒上9:3,20）、迷路的人（詩119:176）、在死亡危險之中的人（伯6:18）。摩西在這裡所指以色列人遊牧生活的起源。
**下到埃及。**關於遷居埃及以及當時人數稀少，見創46:26；47:4。
**國民。**見出1:7,9,12,20。雅各被稱為敘利亞人或亞蘭人，部分原因是他在北美索不達米亞長期居住過，而且亞伯拉罕也是從那裡出發前往迦南去的（創11:31）。從這個微小的開始興起了一個大國。奉獻初熟之物是為了紀念一切頭生的在埃及得蒙拯救。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖與先知》526。
5.en:
**A Syrian ready to perish.** Literally, “a wandering Aramean” (RSV). This is a reference to the humble origin of the nation, to Rebekah and Leah, who were from Padan-aram (Gen. 25:20), and to Jacob, who spent a number of years there (Gen. 29 to 31). Laban, Jacob’s uncle, was designated as “the Syrian,” literally “the Aramean” (Gen. 25:20; 28:5, 6; 31:20, 24). The expression translated “ready to perish” was used animals that strayed and became lost (Deut. 22:3; 1 Sam. 9:3, 20), and also of men lost (Ps. 119:176) and in danger of perishing (Job 6:18). The nomadic origin of Israel is the point to which Moses refers here.
**Down into Egypt.** See Gen. 46:26; 47:4 for the journey to Egypt and for their fewness in number at that time.
**A nation.** See Ex. 1:7, 9, 12, 20. Jacob is pictured as a Syrian or Aramean, in part because of his long residence in northern Mesopotamia, whence Abraham had come to Canaan (Gen. 11:31). From this small beginning emerged a great nation. The presentation of the first fruits commemorated the deliverance of the first-born from Egypt.

6.zh:
埃及人惡待我們，苦害我們，將苦工加在我們身上。

上帝使他們迅速增長的福惠，也是他們被埃及人嚴厲逼迫的原因（出1:9-14；參民20:15）。
6.en: **Afflicted us.** The blessing of God that cause them to increase so rapidly, became also the reason for severe persecution by the Egyptians (Ex. 1:9–14; cf. Num. 20:15).

7.zh:
於是我們哀求耶和華─我們列祖的神，耶和華聽見我們的聲音，看見我們所受的困苦、勞碌、欺壓，

見出2:23-25；3:7-9；4:31；民20:16。

8.zh:
他就用大能的手和伸出來的膀臂，並大可畏的事與神蹟奇事，領我們出了埃及，

見申4:34；7:19；16:3。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《證言》卷六9。
**懷愛倫註釋（8–11節）**。《先祖與先知》526。
8.en: **Brought us forth.** See chs. 4:34; 7:19; 16:3.

9.zh:
將我們領進這地方，把這流奶與蜜之地賜給我們。

**這地方。**見申1:1,5。
**奶與蜜。**見出3:8註釋；另見申6:3。
9.en:
**This place.** See ch. 1:1, 5.
**Milk and honey.** See on Ex. 3:8; see also Deut. 6:3.

10.zh:
耶和華啊，現在我把你所賜給我地上初熟的土產奉了來。隨後你要把筐子放在耶和華─你神面前，向耶和華─你的神下拜。

**把筐子放在。**就是給祭司，再由祭司獻給上帝（第4節）。
**下拜。**承認上帝的恩慈是崇拜的一個重要部分。耶和華是守約的上帝，信實地履行祂所發的一切應許。祂的子民絕不能疏於表達他們感激祂的信實。原文指俯伏在地（創37:10；出11:8；利26:1；賽60:14）。
10.en:
**Set it.** That is, give it to the priest, who would present it to the Lord (v. 4).
**Worship.** The acknowledgement of God’s gracious mercies is a vital part of worship. Jehovah is a covenant-keeping God who faithfully carries out His promises. His people can scarcely do less than express their appreciation for His faithfulness. Literally, “bow down,” that is, prostrate thyself (Gen. 37:10; Ex. 11:8; Lev. 26:1; Isa. 60:14).

11.zh:
你和利未人，並在你們中間寄居的，要因耶和華─你神所賜你和你家的一切福分歡樂。

在奉獻初熟之物的時候，要有筵席和喜慶。不單是家庭成員，而且利未人、鄰居、寄居的也可以邀請來，分享上天的厚禮（見申12:6,7；16:10-12中）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《服務真詮》281。
11.en: **Rejoice.** There was to be feasting and rejoicing at the time of offering the first fruits. Not only the immediate family but Levites, neighbors, and strangers might be invited to share in the bounties of heaven (mentioned in chs. 12:6, 7; 16:10–12).

12.zh:
每逢三年，就是十分取一之年，你取完了一切土產的十分之一，要分給利未人和寄居的，與孤兒寡婦，使他們在你城中可以吃得飽足。

每逢三年，人們除了照常付給利未人什一之外，還要把一份“十分之一”捐給當地的窮人（見申14:28,29註釋）。上帝沒有忘記那些不幸的人，祂的子民也不應該忘記。
**他們……可以吃。**律法家或道德家可能會說窮人是因為他們自身的缺點而受苦。當然並非所有的人都能表現出應有的謹慎、積極或用功。但是如果他們有困難，就不應因此而被置之不理。上帝有意地把利未人放在依賴於其弟兄的位置上，使以色列人能慷慨待人。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖與先知》530。
12.en:
**The third year.** In the third year a “tithe” was to be given to the local poor (see on ch. 14:28, 29), in addition to that always paid to the Levites. God did not forget the less fortunate, nor should His people do so.
**They may eat.** The legalist or moralist might speak of the poor as suffering on account of their own shortcomings. It is true, of course, that not all are as careful, energetic, or diligent as they might be. But if they are in need they are not to be passed by on that account. God deliberately placed the Levites in a position of dependence on their brethren, as a challenge to the liberality of Israel.

13.zh:
你又要在耶和華─你神面前說：我已將聖物從我家裡拿出來，給了利未人和寄居的，與孤兒寡婦，是照你所吩咐我的一切命令。你的命令我都沒有違背，也沒有忘記。

這種完成任務的聲明乃是一年一次的特權。窮人和利未人都應得到供給。奉獻者確認了上帝對他的要求都已完全執行了，“十分之一”已按照上帝的指示忠實地繳納了，並遵照祂的吩咐使用。只要“十分之一”還留在個人家中，那個家就是欠上帝的債。只有當債務完全付清後，祂才能祝福那個家庭。
13.en: **I have brought.** Such a confession of duty fulfilled was to be a yearly privilege. The poor, with the Levite, were to be provided for. The offerer affirmed that God’s claims on him had been fully met, that the “tithe” had been dutifully paid as designated by God, to be applied in harmony with His instructions. As long as the “tithe” remained in a private home, that home was in debt to God. He could not bless that family until the debt had been discharged in full.

14.zh:
我守喪的時候，沒有吃這聖物；不潔淨的時候，也沒有拿出來，又沒有為死人送去。我聽從了耶和華─我神的話，都照你所吩咐的行了。

**我守喪。**可能與屍體儀文性的不潔有關（見利7:20；21:1；參何9:4）。許多情況會造成不潔，“守喪”會使人不能在上帝面前快樂。如果他在“不潔淨的”狀態中享用聖物，不僅會給周圍的人帶來儀文性的不潔，就連聖物本身也會變得不潔了（見申14:23-26註釋）。
**不潔淨的時候”。**他不會故意把“十分之一”用於“不潔淨的”用途。
**為死人。**。從古時起，異教徒就相信死人喜歡人將食物和他們所可能需要的其他東西當作禮物送給他們。值得注意的是，希伯來人的宗教不但沒有規定這種儀式，反而像這裡所說的予以明確排除。在異教國家中，將食物放在死人墳前當作獻給“陰魂”的禮物（見《多比雅書》4:17；《傳道經》30:18）如今這種習俗仍在印度和中國實行。
葬禮的費用可能很高，所以人很有可能想用部分“十分之一”來支付。
14.en:
**My mourning.** Probably in connection with ceremonial uncleanness for the dead (see Lev. 7:20; 21:1; cf. Hosea 9:4). Various circumstances might produce uncleanness, and thereby “mourning,” rendering it impossible for that person to appear before God with rejoicing. Not only would the person involved be ceremonially unclean, but the consecrated things themselves would become unclean if he partook of them while in his “unclean” state (see on Deut. 14:23–26).
**For any unclean use.** Or, “while I was unclean” (RSV). He would not deliberately put the “tithe” to an “unclean” use.
**For the dead.** Or, “to the dead” (RSV). From ancient times the heathen believed that the dead could be made happy by gifts of food and other things of which they might be in need. It is noteworthy that the Hebrew religion not only made no provision for such rites, but, as here, specifically excluded them. In heathen lands the custom of placing food at the grave of the deceased as a gift to his “spirit” (see Tobit 4:17; Ecclus. 30:18) is still practiced, as in India and China.
Perhaps the expenses incident to a funeral were heavy, and the temptation to use part of the “tithe” in meeting these expenses would in all probability not be uncommon.

15.zh:
求你從天上、你的聖所垂看，賜福給你的百姓以色列與你所賜給我們的地，就是你向我們列祖起誓賜我們流奶與蜜之地。

這是懇求上帝眷顧，虔誠地承認上帝的崇高地位遠高過人類的所有居所，一切福分都來源於祂。見大衛在會眾前所說的話（代上29:11-13）。另見代下30:27；賽63:15；耶25:30；亞2:13。
**賜福。**原文的意思是“跪下”。派生的名詞一個是“膝”，另一個是“福”。“稱頌上帝”（注：“稱頌”與“賜福”在原文中為同一個詞）呈現了一幅屈膝敬拜上帝的畫面。
**就是你……起誓。**這是感激和承認上帝始終不渝地信守其聖約，履行其諾言。耶和華不但能夠實現祂的應許，而且是不折不扣地實行（見第3節，另見申1:8；6:3）。
15.en:
**Look down.** A plea for God’s gracious regard. It is, as well, a devout acknowledgement of the exalted position of God, far above all human habitation, and of the fact that all blessings are from Him. Compare the words of David before the congregation (1 Chron. 29:11–13). See also 2 Chron. 30:27; Isa. 63:15; Jer. 25:30; Zech. 2:13.
**Bless.** The word thus translated means “to kneel.” One derived noun means “knee,” and another, “a blessing.” The expression “bless God” presents the picture of worship to God on bended knee.
**As thou swarest.** A grateful acknowledgement of God’s unswerving loyalty to His covenant and faithfulness to all His promises. Not only is Jehovah able to fulfill His promises, but it is impossible that He could ever fall short of perfection in carrying them out (see v. 3, also chs. 1:8; 6:3).

16.zh:
耶和華─你的神今日吩咐你行這些律例典章，所以你要盡心盡性謹守遵行。

**律例。**這節經文所用的詞語指上帝對祂的子民的一切要求，包括宗教義，民事和社會義務。摩西說他們“在伯毗珥對面的谷中”停留（申3:29）。在那裡他向百姓陳述了他在何烈山所領受的一切律法，開始了一段針對全體會眾莊嚴囑咐。這是提醒他們已與上帝立約，承擔了最嚴肅的義務。耶和華作為立約的一方應許要賜福給他們。
**謹守遵行。**這是他們在莊嚴誓約中的責任。就盟約關係而言，這是對誠實生活的一種呼籲（見申4:6；7:12）。
16.en:
**Statutes.** The various words used in this text comprehend all the requirements God made of His people, in respect to not only religious duties but also civil and social. Moses refers to their stay “in the valley over against Beth-peor” (ch. 3:29), where he presented to the people all the laws that had been revealed to him in Horeb. Here begins a solemn charge to all the people. It is a reminder that they had entered into covenant relation with God, that in so doing they had assumed the most solemn obligations. And on His part Jehovah promised to bless them.
**Keep and do them.** Their part in the solemn covenant. This is a call to sincerity of life with respect to the covenant relationship (see chs. 4:6; 7:12).

17.zh:
你今日認耶和華為你的神，應許遵行他的道，謹守他的律例、誡命、典章，聽從他的話。

這句話在希伯來語中語氣極重：“你們今日使耶和華宣佈祂是你們的上帝”。 要實現這一點，以色列人必須傾聽聖約之一切要求的闡述，並承認自己有責任遵守這些要求。
**懷愛倫註釋（17–19節）**。《先知與君王》18；《證言》卷六222。
17.en: **Thou hast avouched.** In Hebrew the statement thus introduced is most emphatic: “Thou hast this day caused Jehovah to proclaim that He is to thee thy God.” This was accomplished by Israel listening to the recitation of all the requirements of the covenant, and acknowledging their own obligation to abide by them.

18.zh:
耶和華今日照他所應許你的，也認你為他的子民，使你謹守他的一切誡命，

這與第17節的語氣是一致的。直譯為“耶和華今日使你們說，你們是祂的子民”，是祂自己的產業。
**祂的子民。**見出19:5；彼前2:9註釋。該希伯來詞也出現在出19:5；申7:6中。在代上29:3中譯為“自己積蓄的”；在瑪3:17中被譯為“特特”。
**應許。**雙方都承擔了義務。盟約是雙方共有的，應許是有條件的，正如在西乃山一樣（出19:5-8；24:3,7）。
**懷愛倫註釋（18–19節）**。《服務真詮》283。
18.en:
**The Lord hath avouched.** This parallels the emphatic expression of v. 17. It reads, literally, “Jehovah hath this day caused thee to say that thou art to Him a people of possession,” that is, His own private possession.
**Peculiar people.** See on Ex. 19:5; 1 Peter 2:9. The same Hebrew word here translated “peculiar” appears also in Ex. 19:5; Deut. 7:6. In 1 Chron. 29:3 the word is translated “own proper good”; and in Mal. 3:17, “jewels.”
**Promised.** Both parties assumed obligations. The covenant was mutual, and the promise, as at Sinai, was conditional Ex. 19:5–8; 24:3, 7.

19.zh:
又使你得稱讚、美名、尊榮，超乎他所造的萬民之上，並照他所應許的使你歸耶和華─你神為聖潔的民。

**超乎。**見申28:1，以及創17:1註釋。“超乎”的原文（“至高者”）是上帝的聖名之一（見創14:18-20,22；民24:16；申32:8；撒下22:14；詩9:2；賽14:14）。根據上帝的旨意，至高者的名要加在上帝的子民身上（民6:27）。
**尊榮。**源於動詞“美化”、“榮耀”。所派生的名詞是“頭巾”、“飾頭巾”，它原是一種裝飾品。關於該詞在其他經文中的譯法，見賽46:13；62:3。注意基督對該詞內涵的表達（約17:10），以及使徒彼得所闡述對於今日教會的應用（彼前2:9,10）。
所謂“約書”，和摩西的第二次演說在這裡結束了。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》28；《教育論》40。
19.en:
**High.** See Deut. 28:1 and on Gen. 17:1. The adjective here translated “high” is one of the names of God (see Gen. 14:18-20, 22; Num. 24:16; Deut. 32:8; 2 Sam. 22:14; Ps. 9:2; Isa. 14:14). In the divine purpose the name of the Most High is placed upon God’s people (Num. 6:27).
**Honour.** The word thus translated is from the verb “to beautify,” “to glorify.” The derived noun means “turban,” “headdress,” originally, an “ornament.” For other instances of the translation of the same word see Isa. 46:13; 62:3. Note the inward significance of this as expressed by Christ (John 17:10), and its application as touching the church today, as commented on by the apostle Peter (1 Peter 2:9, 10).
Thus closes the so-called Book of the Covenant, and with it, Moses’ second oration.

1.zh:
我所陳明在你面前的這一切咒詛都臨到你身上；你在耶和華─你神追趕你到的萬國中必心裡追念祝福的話；

**心裡追念。**直譯為“帶回心裡”。注意王上8:47中的相同說法。他們應當思考被虜的原因以及與耶和華的關係。這是他們恢復上帝恩眷的先決條件（見利26:40；申4:29,30）。
1.en: **Call them to mind.** Literally, “bring them back to thy heart.” Note the same expression in 1 Kings 8:47. It would be necessary for them to meditate upon the causes of their exile and their relation to Jehovah as a preliminary to their restoration to God’s favor (see Lev. 26:40; Deut. 4:29, 30).

2.zh:
你和你的子孫若盡心盡性歸向耶和華─你的神，照著我今日一切所吩咐的聽從他的話；

他們還必須轉離罪惡，回來敬拜耶和華（見尼1:8,9），通過順從反映誠意。
2.en: **Return.** There must also be a turning away from sin and a return to the worship of Jehovah (see Neh. 1:8, 9). Sincerity would be reflected in obedience.

3.zh:
那時，耶和華─你的神必憐恤你，救回你這被擄的子民；耶和華─你的神要回轉過來，從分散你到的萬民中將你招聚回來。

見詩14:7；85:1-3；126:1,4；結16:53。最重要的不是肉身擺脫囚虜，而是從罪的奴役中得到解救（見詩41:4；耶3:22；17:14；何14:4；太13:15）。
3.en: **Turn thy captivity.** Compare Ps. 14:7; 85:1–3; 126:1, 4; Eze. 16:53. It is not a deliverance from physical captivity that is most important, but rather deliverance from captivity to sin (see Ps. 41:4; Jer. 3:22; 17:14; Hosea 14:4; Matt. 13:15).

4.zh:
你被趕散的人，就是在天涯的，耶和華─你的神也必從那裡將你招聚回來。

先知尼希米提到了本節的應許（尼1:8,9）。類似的說法見申4:32；詩19:4；賽13:5。耶和華不會丟棄祂的子民；祂從來沒有棄絕過他們個人。被趕散是對他們的處罰。上帝的懲罰總是有一個明確的目標。當效果達到時，上帝就會轉向祂的兒女，提出幫助他們復興（見伯23:10；何6:1-3；來12:11）。
4.en: **The outmost parts of heaven.** The prophet Nehemiah refers to the promise of this verse (Neh. 1:8, 9). For a similar expression see Deut. 4:32; Ps. 19:4; Isa. 13:5. Jehovah would not cast off His people; as individuals He has never rejected them. Dispersion was to be their punishment. Divine chastisement always has a particular objective. When that effect is brought about, God turns to His child with offers of, and help to accomplish, restoration (see Job 23:10; Hosea 6:1–3; Heb. 12:11).

5.zh:
耶和華─你的神必領你進入你列祖所得的地，使你可以得著；又必善待你，使你的人數比你列祖眾多。

關於上帝所說實現這應許的方式，見耶32:42,43。
5.en: **Do thee good.** See Jer. 32:42, 43 for the way in which the Lord proposed to fulfill this promise.

6.zh:
耶和華─你神必將你心裡和你後裔心裡的汙穢除掉，好叫你盡心盡性愛耶和華─你的神，使你可以存活。

英文KJV版及原文直譯為“必使你的心受割禮”。見利26:41；耶31:33。心裡受割禮就是喚醒人屬靈的悟性，使人的良心軟下來。
6.en: **Will circumcise thine heart.** Compare Lev. 26:41; Jer. 31:33. To circumcise the heart means to quicken one’s spiritual perception and make tender one’s conscience.

7.zh:
耶和華─你的神必將這一切咒詛加在你仇敵和恨惡你、逼迫你的人身上。

真正的悔改會扭轉因叛逆而帶來的咒詛。在上帝和罪人之間，沒有什麼隔閡太寬太深，以至在罪人再次歸向上帝時無法立即消除。當一個人歸向上帝時，祂就非常高興，因為這樣，天國的福分就能傾降下來。只有頑固不化的罪人才會受到罪的全部咒詛。
7.en: **Upon thine enemies.** Genuine repentance reverses the curse that follows waywardness. There is no separation between God and the sinner so wide and deep that it cannot be closed up immediately, upon the sinner’s turning again to God. The joy of God is complete when a man turns to Him, for then the blessings of heaven can be poured out. It is the persistent sinner who must suffer the full curse of sin.

8.zh:
你必歸回，聽從耶和華的話，遵行他的一切誡命，就是我今日所吩咐你的。

**歸回。**原路返回，如同從旅程中歸回一樣。這個說法常喻指謙卑悔改地歸回上帝（見賽10:21；19:22；耶4:1；15:19；18:11；結18:23等）。
8.en: **Return.** To retrace one’s steps, as from a journey. It is often used figuratively of turning to God in humble repentance (see Isa. 10:21; 19:22; Jer. 4:1; 15:19; 18:11; Eze. 18:23; etc.).

9.zh:
你若聽從耶和華─你神的話，謹守這律法書上所寫的誡命律例，又盡心盡性歸向耶和華─你的神，他必使你手裡所辦的一切事，並你身所生的，牲畜所下的，地土所產的，都綽綽有餘；因為耶和華必再喜悅你，降福與你，像從前喜悅你列祖一樣。併於上節。

**必使你……都綽綽有餘。**當一個人以上帝的要求為樂，愛上帝並且順從祂的旨意時（見約14:15），（見約壹5:3），他就會把上帝的原則銘記在心裡（見詩40:8）。這樣，上帝就能鼓舞那人的心靈和生命，並加上物質的福氣（見申28:63；耶32:41；太6:33）。
**律法。**原文為torah，泛指上帝所顯明的一切旨意。猶太人也以此來指《摩西五經》，甚至指整個舊約。
9.en: **Make thee plenteous.** When a man loves God and obeys His will (see John 14:15), because he takes delight in God’s requirements (see 1 John 5:3), then it is that the divine principles become enshrined in his heart (see Ps. 40:8). This allows God to invigorate the soul and life of that man, and add material blessings (see Deut. 28:63; Jer. 32:41; Matt. 6:33).

11.zh:
我今日所吩咐你的誡命不是你難行的，也不是離你遠的；

就是：不是太難理解的（見創18:14；申17:8；耶32:17,27等）。
11.en: **It is not hidden.** Literally, “not is it too hard,” that is, not too difficult to understand (see Gen. 18:14; Deut. 17:8; Jer. 32:17, 27; etc.).

13.zh:
也不是在海外，使你說：誰替我們過海取了來，使我們聽見可以遵行呢？

第12和13節可能是引用了一句諺語。意思是人不需要為了理解上帝對人的旨意而從事某種超人的工作，走一條漫長艱辛的路，或試圖攀到天上去。上帝已藉著祂的先知摩西將祂的意念清楚地顯示給以色列人。上帝公義的要求已經寫下來了；人已得到充分的告知。參使徒保羅的論證（羅10:5-13）。
**13 也不是在海外，使你說：**‘誰替我們過海取了來，使我們聽見可以遵行呢？’

14.zh:
這話卻離你甚近，就在你口中，在你心裡，使你可以遵行。

摩西不僅口述上帝的旨意，而且以書面形式記錄下來。參保羅的講述（徒20:26,27；腓1:8）。
14.en: **Nigh unto thee.** Moses had not only declared God’s will by word of mouth but had also put it in writing. Compare the defense of Paul (Acts 20:26, 27; Phil. 1:8).

15.zh:
看哪，我今日將生與福，死與禍，陳明在你面前。

**懷愛倫註釋**。《善惡之爭》544。。

16.zh:
吩咐你愛耶和華─你的神，遵行他的道，謹守他的誡命、律例、典章，使你可以存活，人數增多，耶和華─你神就必在你所要進去得為業的地上賜福與你。

**懷愛倫註釋（16–18節）**。《救贖的故事》171。。

19.zh:
我今日呼天喚地向你作見證；我將生死禍福陳明在你面前，所以你要揀選生命，使你和你的後裔都得存活；

**懷愛倫註釋（19–20節）**。《先祖與先知》467。。

20.zh:
且愛耶和華─你的神，聽從他的話，專靠他；因為他是你的生命，你的日子長久也在乎他。這樣，你就可以在耶和華向你列祖亞伯拉罕、以撒、雅各起誓應許所賜的地上居住。

**祂是你的生命。**譯為“那是你的生命” 更好，也就是愛上帝是你的生命。人的生命如果受到上帝之愛的激勵和引導，就能承受永生。每個人的生命最終只有兩種可能性。一種是竭盡全力地愛上帝，實現完美豐滿的人生而融入永生。另一種是輕視上帝的美意，一生追求世俗的事。他們一生這樣度過，就會導致永死。這兩種選擇擺在每個生在世上的人面前。摩西的第四次演說到此結束。
20.en: **He is thy life.** Better, “that is thy life,” that is, to love God. To have one’s life inspired and directed by the love of God is to inherit eternal life. The possibilities of life for every man are ultimately reduced to two. One is to love God with all one’s powers. The end result is life in all its fullness, ultimately merging into immortality. The alternative is a disregard of God’s good pleasure, with one’s life devoted to the things of this earth. A life spent persistently in such a way leads to eternal death. These alternatives challenge every man and woman born into the world. Here ends Moses’ fourth oration.

30.10: **The law.** From torah, which refers to God’s revealed will in general. The Jews also applied it to the Pentateuch, and even to the entire OT.
30.12: **Who shall go?** It is possible that vs. 12 and 13 quote a proverbial saying. The meaning is that one is not required to undertake some superhuman task, to make a long, laborious journey, or seek to climb up into heaven in order to understand God’s will for man. God has clearly revealed His mind to Israel, through His prophet Moses. His righteous requirements have been written down; man is fully informed. Compare the argument of the apostle Paul (Rom. 10:5–13).

1.zh:
摩西去告訴以色列眾人

猶太教註釋家認為這句話的意思就是摩西在這裡結束了他對聚集在面前之人的勸勉。然後他從一個支派到另一個支派去傳達他即將去世的消息，並且勉勵百姓擁護和支持他的繼承人約書亞。
1.en: **Moses went.** Jewish commentators take these words to mean that Moses here concluded his exhortations to the people gathered before him. Then he went from tribe to tribe to give the news of his approaching death, and to exhort the people to uphold and support Joshua, his successor.

2.zh:
說：我現在一百二十歲了，不能照常出入；耶和華也曾對我說：你必不得過這約但河。

他顯然知道他的工作快要完成了。他不久以後就去世了（申34:7）。當摩西站在法老面前時，他是80歲（出7:7）。從那時起，曠野飄流的四十年已經過去了。
**不能照常出入。**他當時仍顯得鍵壯有力（見申34:7；書14:11）。
2.en:
**This day.** He evidently knew that his work was almost finished. He died soon after this (ch. 34:7). When Moses stood before Pharaoh he was 80 years old (Ex. 7:7). Since then the 40 years of the desert wanderings had passed.
**No more go.** He appeared to be strong and vigorous (see Deut. 34:7; Joshua 14:11).

3.zh:
耶和華─你們的神必引導你們過去，將這些國民在你們面前滅絕，你們就得他們的地。約書亞必引導你們過去，正如耶和華所說的。

**引導你們過去（英文KJV版譯為“行在你們面前”）。**見申9:3；出23:23。約櫃和上帝的臨格會行在他們前面（見書3:5,11）。
3.en: **Before thee.** Compare Deut. 9:3; Ex. 23:23. The ark and the presence of God would go before them (see Joshua 3:5, 11).

4.zh:
耶和華必待他們，如同從前待他所滅絕的亞摩利二王西宏與噩以及他們的國一樣。

**西宏。**見申2:32-3:8；29:7。
4.en: **Sihon.** See chs. 2:32 to 3:8; 29:7.

5.zh:
耶和華必將他們交給你們；你們要照我所吩咐的一切命令待他們。

**將他們交給。**見申7:23；9:3。
**一切誡命。**就是上帝所發有關搗毀異教民族“木偶”、偶像和祭壇的各種吩咐（見申7:2-5,25；12:1-3）。
5.en:
**Give them up.** See chs. 7:23; 9:3.
**All the commandments.** That is, the various injunctions that God had given for the destruction of the “groves,” idols, and altars of the heathen (see chs. 7:2-5, 25; 12:1–3).

6.zh:
你們當剛強壯膽，不要害怕，也不要畏懼他們，因為耶和華─你的神和你同去。他必不撇下你，也不丟棄你。

**剛強。**這是呼召百姓要運用信心。
**不要害怕。**被對於他們的父輩曾有相同的吩咐（見申1:21,29；3:2,22；7:17,18,21），但上一代人沒有信心（見申1:28-32）。
**和你同去。**這個應許也曾發出過（見申20:4）。
**必不撇下你。**見摩西死後對約書亞的應許（書1:5）。使徒保羅把這個經歷應用到了基督教會身上（見來13:5）。
摩西度過了漫長而波瀾起伏的一生。他無私而不倦地侍奉了上帝和祂的子民。在世上，他沒有任何時候能比他當時更偉大了，但上帝在天上的迦南為他預備了更多的東西。參保羅的經驗（提後4:6-8）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先知與君王》393。。
6.en:
**Be strong.** A call to the people to exercise faith.
**Fear not.** The same injunction had been given to their fathers (see chs. 1:21, 29; 3:2, 22; 7:17, 18, 21), but the older generation had been faithless (see ch. 1:28–32).
**Go with thee.** This promise had been given before (see ch. 20:4).
**Not fail … thee.** See the promise made to Joshua after the death of Moses (Joshua 1:5). The apostle Paul applies this experience to the Christian church (see Heb. 13:5).
Moses had lived a long and eventful life. He had served God and His people unselfishly and tirelessly. On earth he could never be greater than he was at that moment; yet God had more in store for him, in the heavenly Canaan. Compare the experience of Paul (2 Tim. 4:6–8).

7.zh:
摩西召了約書亞來，在以色列眾人眼前對他說：你當剛強壯膽！因為，你要和這百姓一同進入耶和華向他們列祖起誓應許所賜之地；你也要使他們承受那地為業。

**約書亞。**上帝所任命的新領袖（見民27:18-21）。約書亞的意思就是“耶和華的救恩”。他在出17:9中被首次提到。和摩西一樣，他已為他的工作進行了適當的準備。他曾在頒佈律法、在戰場和在領導工作上與摩西合作。如同基督所揀選的十二個使徒一樣，他在經驗和合作方面接受了特殊的訓練。
7.en: **Joshua.** The new leader by God’s appointment (see Num. 27:18–21). Joshua means “the salvation of Jehovah.” He is first mentioned in Ex. 17:9. Like Moses, he had received an appropriate preparation for his work. He had been associated with Moses in the giving of the law, in battle, and in leadership. Like the 12 apostles selected by Christ, he was given special training in experience and association.

8.zh:
耶和華必在你前面行；他必與你同在，必不撇下你，也不丟棄你。不要懼怕，也不要驚惶。

**撇下。**譯自常用的動詞，“任憑缺乏”（見創24:27；詩16:10）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先知與君王》576。。
8.en: **Will not fail.** From the common verb, “to leave destitute” (see Gen. 24:27; Ps. 16:10).

9.zh:
摩西將這律法寫出來，交給抬耶和華約櫃的祭司利未子孫和以色列的眾長老。

**律法。**原文為torah，包括一切上帝所顯明的旨意。尼希米提到過出13:2,12；23:19，並且稱之為“律法上所寫的”（尼10:35,36）。約西亞實行了利19:30；20:6,27的吩咐，並說他是在遵行“律法書上所寫的話”（王下23:24）。希西家下令實行“律法上所載的”民28和29章的命令（代下31:3）。
**抬耶和華約櫃。**見申10:8；書3:3,6；6:6；王上8:3,4。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖與先知》311；《救贖的故事》171。。
9.en:
**This law.** From torah, a term inclusive of all the revealed will of God. Nehemiah refers to Ex. 13:2, 12; 23:19, and speaks of what is “written in the law” (Neh. 10:35, 36). Josiah carried out the injunctions of Lev. 19:30; 20:6, 27, and said he was doing “the words of the law” (2 Kings 23:24). Hezekiah gave command to carry out the charges of Num. 28 and 29, “written in the law” (2 Chron. 31:3).
**Bare the ark.** See Deut. 10:8; Joshua 3:3, 6; 6:6; 1 Kings 8:3, 4.

10.zh:
摩西吩咐他們說：每逢七年的末一年，就在豁免年的定期住棚節的時候，

**豁免年。**“豁免”一詞的原文源於一個表示“扔下”的動詞。在出23:11中，該詞被譯為“歇息”。這裡所指的是使土地得以“歇息”，債務得以豁免的安息年（見申15:1-10）。對於賣身為奴之人的“豁免”會在滿了六年的服務之後實現（見申15:12）；對他而言，“第七年”不一定就是安息年或“豁免年”。誦讀律法之年始於提市黎月十五日住棚節的時候。安息年顯然和第50年（即禧年）一樣始於提市黎月。禧年是以提市黎月初十贖罪日結束時的吹角而正式開始的（見利25:9）。
**懷愛倫註釋（10–13節）**。《先祖與先知》503。。
10.en: **Year of release.** The word translated “release” is from a form of the verb shamat, “to throw down.” In Ex. 23:11 it is rendered “rest.” The reference here is to the sabbatical year, when the land was to “rest” and when there was release from debt (see Deut. 15:1–10). The “release” of a man who had sold himself into servitude came after six full years of service (see Deut. 15:12); for him, the “seventh year” did not necessarily coincide with the sabbatical year, the “year of release.” The reading year of the law came at the time of the Feast of Tabernacles, which began on the 15th of Tishri. The sabbatical year evidently began, like the 50th year, the year of jubilee, in Tishri. The year of jubilee officially opened with the blowing of trumpets at the close of the Day of Atonement, on the 10th of Tishri (see Lev. 25:9).

11.zh:
以色列眾人來到耶和華─你神所選擇的地方朝見他。那時，你要在以色列眾人面前將這律法念給他們聽。

律法還在其他場合誦讀（見書8:34；王下23:2；尼8:1-3）。虔誠誦讀上帝的聖言在任何人的生活中都是一種穩定因素。聽耶和華向祂的聖徒所說的話是一件美事（見詩85:8）。利未人蒙指示要教導百姓聖經（見申33:10；利10:11；瑪2:7）。
11.en: **Read this law.** The law was also read on other occasions (see Joshua 8:34; 2 Kings 23:2; Neh. 8:1–3). A reverential reading of the Word of God is a stabilizing factor in any man’s life. It is a good thing to hear what the Lord says to His saints (see Ps. 85:8). The Levites were commanded to teach the Scriptures to the people (see Deut. 33:10; Lev. 10:11; Mal. 2:7).

12.zh:
要招聚他們男、女、孩子，並城裡寄居的，使他們聽，使他們學習，好敬畏耶和華─你們的神，謹守、遵行這律法的一切話，

程序是：聽、學習、敬畏上帝、遵行律法（見申4:10；14:23；17:19）。
**懷愛倫註釋（12–13節）**。《先知與君王》465。。
12.en: **Hear.** The sequence is hear, learn, fear the Lord, observe the law (see chs. 4:10; 14:23; 17:19).

13.zh:
也使他們未曾曉得這律法的兒女得以聽見，學習敬畏耶和華─你們的神，在你們過約但河要得為業之地，存活的日子，常常這樣行。

猶太人的特權之一就是上帝的聖言交託給他們（見羅3:1,2）。救贖的計劃，未來國度的奇妙，都記載在祂的聖言中。讓孩子在成長的過程中對聖言一無所知是很愚蠢的。聖經寫出來就是讓人誦讀和默想的。聖經的智慧應是留給我們子女的遺產。不給年輕人適當的宗教訓練乃是一種嚴重的失職。
13.en: **Their children.** One of the outstanding privileges accorded the Jews was the committal to them of the Word of God (see Rom. 3:1, 2). The plan of redemption, the wonders of the future kingdom—all are recorded in His Word. It is folly for children to be allowed to grow up in ignorance of the Word. The Scriptures were written to be read and meditated upon. Their wisdom is to be the heritage of our children. To fail to give proper religious training to the young is to fail in a primary duty.

14.zh:
耶和華對摩西說：你的死期臨近了；要召約書亞來，你們二人站在會幕裡，我好囑咐他。於是摩西和約書亞去站在會幕裡。

你們二人站（見出33:8）。
**囑咐。**見申3:28，叫摩西囑咐約書亞。約書亞的領導職務需要承擔很大的責任。
**站在。**可能站在上帝的榮耀所在的帳幕門口的院子裡。
14.en:
**Present yourselves.** Literally, “take your stand” (see Ex. 33:7).
**A charge.** Compare ch. 3:28, where Moses was commanded to charge Joshua. Joshua’s leadership was to entail great responsibilities.
**Presented themselves.** Literally, “took their stand.” Presumably they stood in the court facing the door of the tabernacle, over which the glory of God would appear.

15.zh:
耶和華在會幕裡雲柱中顯現，雲柱停在會幕門以上。

**耶和華……顯現。**在特殊的情況下，停留在帳幕之上的雲柱（見民9:15,18），會移到帳幕門口。在這裡，耶和華的榮耀從雲柱中照耀出來（見出33:9,10；40:35）。
15.en: **The Lord appeared.** On special occasions the pillar of cloud that rested upon the tabernacle (see Num. 9:15, 18) would move to the door of the tabernacle. Here, Jehovah’s glory shone through it (see Ex. 33:9, 10; 40:35).

16.zh:
耶和華又對摩西說：你必和你列祖同睡。這百姓要起來，在他們所要去的地上，在那地的人中，隨從外邦神行邪淫，離棄我，違揹我與他們所立的約。

看哪（譯者注：英文KJV版直譯，中文沒有）。意思就是“注意”。隨後所說的內容是非常重要的。
**睡。**見撒下7:12；王上2:10；11:43中表示死亡的相同說法。
**這百姓。**對上帝子民未來歷史的一種悲慘的描繪。
**行邪淫。**見出34:15註釋。某些已經很明顯的傾向預示了該民族未來的行為（見士2:7-17）。詩篇的作者記載了以色列人歷史中的一個悲慘篇章（見詩106:34-39）。上帝告訴他們不要害怕異教的神（士6:10），並充分了解他們對真神的義務（出20:3）。
**違揹我與他們所立的約。**就是去敬拜別神（見出20:22,23；23:32,33；申5:3,4；6:3,4）。他們已通過立約承認耶和華是上帝，並且單單敬愛和侍奉祂。
16.en:
**Behold.** Meaning, “pay attention.” What follows is most important.
**Sleep.** See the same expression for death in 2 Sam. 7:12; 1 Kings 2:10; 11:43.
**This people.** A sad picture of the future history of God’s people.
**Whoring.** See on Ex. 34:15. There were certain tendencies already manifest that indicated the future conduct of the nation (see Judges 2:7–17). The psalmist has recorded a sad chapter in Israel’s history (see Ps. 106:34–39). They were told not to fear the heathen gods (Judges 6:10), and knew well their duty to the true God (Ex. 20:3).
**Break my covenant.** By the worship of other gods (see Ex. 20:22, 23; 23:32, 33; Deut. 5:3, 4; 6:3, 4). In entering into the covenant relationship they had agreed to recognize the Lord as God, and to love and serve Him only.

17.zh:
那時，我的怒氣必向他們發作；我也必離棄他們，掩面不顧他們，以致他們被吞滅，並有許多的禍患災難臨到他們。那日他們必說：這些禍患臨到我們，豈不是因我們的神不在我們中間嗎？

**我的怒氣。**正如在士2:14中，當他們過約旦河後第一次背道時的情形。
**掩面。**這意味著上帝保護之手的撤回（見申32:20；賽8:17；64:7；結7:22；39:23）。
**上帝不在我們中間。**見耶14:9；彌3:11；參賽12:6；番3:15,17。
17.en:
**My anger.** So in Judges 2:14 at their first apostasy after crossing the Jordan.
**Hide my face.** This means a withdrawal of God’s protecting hand (see Deut. 32:20; Isa. 8:17; 64:7; Eze. 7:22; 39:23).
**God is not among us.** See Jer. 14:9; Micah 3:11; cf. Isa. 12:6; Zeph. 3:15, 17.

19.zh:
現在你要寫一篇歌，教導以色列人，傳給他們，使這歌見證他們的不是；

見申32:1。以色列人要學唱這歌，並且代代相傳。這樣，他們就會形象地記住摩西所堅持的崇高原則，並受這些原則所約束。
19.en: **This song.** See 32:1. The Israelites would learn to sing the song, and thereby hand it down from generation to generation. It would thus ever remain vivid in their memories, and bind them to the lofty principles for which Moses stood.

21.zh:
那時，有許多禍患災難臨到他們，這歌必在他們面前作見證，他們後裔的口中必念誦不忘。我未領他們到我所起誓應許之地以先，他們所懷的意念我都知道了。

**意念。**原文來源於一個表示“在人心中圖謀”、“圖謀”、“建立”、“形成”的動詞詞根。由此派生的名詞形式用來指心中的衝動、謀略和用意。在許多人心中已有的籌劃、傾向和企圖在上帝面前都是敞開的（見代上28:9；以及詩103:14節，“本體”）。
21.en: **Imagination.** The word here translated “imagination” is from a verb root meaning “to devise in one’s mind,” “to devise,” “to establish,” “to form.” The derived noun form is used of an impulse of the mind, a device, a purpose. The plannings, inclinations, and designs already in the heart of many were open to God (see 1 Chron. 28:9; and Ps. 103:14, “frame”).

23.zh:
耶和華囑咐嫩的兒子約書亞說：你當剛強壯膽，因為你必領以色列人進我所起誓應許他們的地；我必與你同在。

**壯膽。**耶和華在摩西去世之後向約書亞重申了這句話（見書1:6,7,9；參10:25）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖與先知》470。。
23.en: **Good courage.** The Lord repeated this to Joshua after the death of Moses (see Joshua 1:6, 7, 9; cf. 10:25).

24.zh:
摩西將這律法的話寫在書上，及至寫完了，

**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖與先知》312，365；《救贖的故事》149。。

25.zh:
就吩咐抬耶和華約櫃的利未人說：

**利未人。**見王上8:3。他們的特權和責任就是在得到吩咐時靠近約櫃。
25.en: **The Levites.** See 1 Kings 8:3. It was their assigned privilege and duty to approach the ark when commanded to do so.

26.zh:
將這律法書放在耶和華─你們神的約櫃旁，可以在那裡見證以色列人的不是；

**約櫃旁。**見王上8:9；代下5:10；參申29:21；30:10。猶太教註釋家在對這句話的理解有分歧。有人認為寫好的書卷和兩塊石版都放在約櫃裡面；還有人認為是放在約櫃右邊一個由突出的木板做成的分隔空間裡。“約櫃裡惟有兩塊石版，就是摩西在何烈山所放的”（代下5:10），這句話證實了後一種看法。RSV版本譯“為放在約櫃旁”。刻在兩塊石版上的原則是獨一無二的。十誡是至高無上的；含有“這律法的話”（申31:24）的“書”則是十誡原則針對以色列人社會的引申和應用。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《救贖的故事》 172。。
26.en: **In the side.** See 1 Kings 8:9; 2 Chron. 5:10; cf. Deut. 29:21; 30:10. Jewish commentators are divided in their views respecting these words. Some maintain the written scroll was placed inside the ark with the two tables of stone, others, that it was placed in a compartment formed at the right side of the ark by a projecting board. The definite statement that “there was nothing in the ark save the two tables which Moses put therein at Horeb” (2 Chron. 5:10) confirms the latter suggestion. The RSV reads, “by the side of the ark” (Deut. 31:26). The principles inscribed upon the two tables of stone were of such a nature as to place them in a class by themselves. The Decalogue was supreme; the “book” containing “the words of this law” (Deut. 31:24) was an amplification and application of its principles to the economy of Israel.

27.zh:
因為我知道你們是悖逆的，是硬著頸項的。我今日還活著與你們同在，你們尚且悖逆耶和華，何況我死後呢？

**硬著頸項。**“硬著”一詞的原文還表示“堅硬”、“服侍”、“困難”、“頑固”（見耶7:26；17:23；19:15）。百姓固執己見，很難甚至根本無法改變他們。
27.en: **Stiff neck.** The word translated “stiff” also has the meaning of “hard,” “serve,” “difficult,” “stubborn” (see Jer. 7:26; 17:23; 19:15). The people were set in their ways, and it was difficult if not impossible for them to change.

28.zh:
你們要將你們支派的眾長老和官長都招聚了來，我好將這些話說與他們聽，並呼天喚地見證他們的不是。

**見證。**見申4:26；30:19；32:1。

29.zh:
我知道我死後，你們必全然敗壞，偏離我所吩咐你們的道，行耶和華眼中看為惡的事，以手所做的惹他發怒；日後必有禍患臨到你們。

**日後。**該詞語首次出現在創49:1中，英文KJV版譯為“末後的日子”（見民24:14；申4:30）。該詞在舊約中用得很多，通常表示未來。
29.en: **Latter days.** This same expression occurs for the first time in Gen. 49:1, where it is translated “last days” (see Num. 24:14; Deut. 4:30). This expression is used with considerable latitude in the OT. Generally it refers simply to the future.

30.zh:
摩西將這一篇歌的話都說與以色列全會眾聽。

**摩西……說。**約書亞曾在這件事上與他合作（見申32:44）。偉大的立法者摩西，即將卸下他的重擔。一個比他年輕的人，一個勇士，將擔負起領導以色列人征服巴勒斯坦的工作。耶和華曾使摩西壯膽；祂也要在約書亞前面行。
30.en: **Moses spake.** Joshua was associated with him in this (see ch. 32:44). Moses, the great legislator, was about to lay down his burdens. A younger man, a soldier, was to take up the task of leading Israel in the conquest of Palestine. Jehovah had strengthened Moses; He would also go before Joshua.

0.zh:
**一、卷名**
《申命記》是五經的第五卷也是最後一卷，猶太人通常稱之為“這些話”，即希伯來文本的頭兩個詞。英譯本卷名譯自希臘語七十子譯本，意為“第二部（或重複的）法律”，這是與《出埃及記》相對而言，《出埃及記》有時被稱為“第一部法律”。
**二、作者**
傳統的見證一致認為摩西是《申命記》的作者。自古以來，一直沒有提到還有其他作者。只是現代才有學者對此提出疑問。除了傳統的見證以外，還有耶穌基督和使徒的權威（太19:7,8；參申24:1；可12:19；參申25:5；約1:17,7:19；參申4:44；約1:45和徒3:22；參申18:15；來10:28；參申17:2-7）。根據所採用的希伯來用語方式，以及所提到歷史事實和背景，可以證實其著作的年代。上述事實及其他事實均證明摩西為作者（見《先祖與先知》503頁）。
**三、歷史背景**
從出埃及第四十年十一月初一起，以色列人安營在約旦河東摩押平原耶利哥對面的什亭。他們在那裡駐紮了兩個月（申1:3；參書3:1,2,5,7；4:19），準備攻佔迦南，而且也許最重要的是摩西發表講話。這些講話構成了《申命記》的主體。
**四、主題**
《申命記》既有歷史和律法，又有勸勉的話。它主要由四次演講（有些權威認為是三次）加上一些連接性的說明構成。第一次演講宣佈摩西要從領導崗位上退下來。開頭部分是回顧往事，結束部分是規勸人遵守律法。第二次演講回顧十誡為上帝與以色列人所立之約的基礎，並告誡以色列人要順從。這次演講的主要內容是重述有關民事，社會和宗教的法律。第三次演講是關於祝福和咒詛的儀式。在這篇演進中，摩西以滔滔的言辭，達到了文學上無與倫比的高度。第四篇演講簡要地回顧歷史，再次勸人遵守律法，並解釋了心中的約。
在《申命記》的演講中，摩西呼籲百姓在生活上順從上帝所顯示的旨意。順命者生，逆命者死。摩西用歷史事實作為他勉言的根據。他提出以色列人對於上帝的愛和感激，以及他們作為上帝選民的尊榮來加強他的信息。他知道存在著拜偶像和以形式主義代替宗教實質精神的危險，就強調耶和華和祂律法的無上尊嚴，和崇拜祂事奉祂的屬靈性質，以及祂如何會信守祂與以色列人和萬國所立的約。
《申命記》中這一系列偉大而出色的演講，是摩西的告別辭。他深愛自己的同胞, 為了他們的罪得到寬恕，他甚至懇求把他的名字從生命冊上塗掉（出32:32）。
《申命記》的影響，它在希伯來人乃至於基督徒宗教生活中的地位是很大的。約西亞時代“律法書”的重新發現曾導致歷史上最偉大的宗教改革（王下22,23；代下34,35；《先知和君王》392-406）。《申命記》成為希伯來宗教信仰的拱頂石。凡是真正的希伯來人每天都要背誦其中的章節。耶穌曾用三句《申命記》的引文來對付惡者的試探（太4:1-11；見申8:3；6:16；6:13）。祂在回答律法師的問題時，曾引用《申命記》的中心句子作為最大的誡命（太22:35-38；見申6:5；10:12；30:6）。保羅曾應用《申命記》的語句來闡述因信稱義的觀點（羅10:6-8）。
0.en:
